The menu is broadly Eastern Mediterranean, drawing inspiration from the melting pot of Istanbul, with a bounty of dishes—from flaky, cheesy borek to juicy short rib kebabs with sweetbreads—that are well-suited to sharing with a group.Whatever else you opt for, consider it all but mandatory to start your meal with “breaking bread,” an assortment of spreads, olives, and pickles, served with superlatively pillowy, toasty pita that is rolled and hearth-baked to order—you’re unlikely to find better in the Bay Area.

restaurant.Name: Dama
restaurant.Address: 612 E. 11th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90015, USA
restaurant.Description: Folks flock to this breezy, Latin-inspired spot in downtown Los Angeles. Dama's feisty flavors play well off its chic old Havana-style dining room, with plush leather sofas, massive wicker fans spinning overhead and colorful tile underfoot. The front patio is filled with plenty of greenery, while the glam central bar busily blends tropical cocktails to order. As for the menu, there’s plenty to choose from. Think kanpachi aguachile with red pearl onions; shrimp tostadas with pickled chilies, and lamb chops with olive salsa verde. Paella, pork and grilled ribeyes are best for sharing.

restaurant.Name: Dame
restaurant.Address: 87 MacDougal St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Dreamed up by Patricia Howard and Ed Szymanski, this pop-up turned brick-and-mortar is all the rage, so reservations are a must. It's a quaint space, dressed with white and blue hues as well as wood accents. The seafood-focused menu spins to the season, although fish and chips is the dish that catapulted it to fame. Featuring a massive piece of hake with a lacy batter and sprinkling of salt flakes, this cult classic arrives with fries and tartar sauce. For dessert, a slice of olive oil cake with macerated cherries will do the trick. Meanwhile, the wine list is substantial and arranged under two heads—what would James Bond or Austin Powers drink? Naturally, the Bond section features classics, while Powers gets more playful.

restaurant.Name: Damian
restaurant.Address: 2132 E. 7th Pl., Los Angeles, CA, 90021, USA
restaurant.Description: Housed within a repurposed warehouse with polished concrete, exposed brick and pendant lighting, Damian has that industrial chic look down pat, but add plush leather-covered chairs and loads of leafy green plants, plus an ever-popular terrace, and this Arts District denizen is a notch above. The menu speaks to a kitchen that is rooted in the nuances of Mexican cooking. While there may not be a right way to start a meal here, a delicious tamal de elote paired with a thirst-quenching cocktail is always a good idea. The uni tostada with a blue corn base topped with a generous pile of uni petals and a "Caesar salad" represents the kitchen's modern, subtle layering technique. Even the ever-traditional fish taco punches above its weight with precision and surprise.

restaurant.Name: Dampf Good BBQ
restaurant.Address: 6800 Good Hope Church Rd., Cary, NC, 27519, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: In a land where pig is prime, brothers Nick and Bryce Dampf offer a true taste of Texas barbecue here in North Carolina. What started out as a backyard hobby evolved into pop-ups and then, eventually, a career commitment to cooking low and slow. Sides and dessert are not the focus, so focus instead on melting, tender slices of beef brisket, snappy sausages and a righteous, fast-selling beef rib – all sold by weight and verified signatures. Bring friends, a serious appetite and a bit of patience, as lines form quickly. Keep an eye on the restaurant’s social media for specials.

restaurant.Name: Danbi
restaurant.Address: 3465 W. 6th St., Ste. 90-100, Los Angeles, CA, 90020, USA
restaurant.Description: Danbi sports a sleek, modern dining room with an industrial feel (think concrete floors, hanging plants, and dark wood tables) as well as a large bar for bites and sips like their "kimchi mule." Chef Lareine Ko's streamlined menu pops with large, shareable plates. The hit list includes mushroom bibimbap with fresh vegetables, as well as a crispy scallop pancake accompanied by a creamy mentaiko sauce. Wagyu Zabuton, cooked over charcoal and served on a hot cast iron skillet over a bed of grilled onions, is a solid winner. End the meal with one of Chef Isabell Manibusan's pastries—perhaps the almost-nostalgic banana milk cloud with brûléed meringue and banana milk crème anglaise, or the Mont Halla, a Korean twist on a Mont Blanc.

restaurant.Name: Daniel's, A Florida Steakhouse
restaurant.Address: 620 S. Federal Hwy., Fort Lauderdale, FL, 33301, USA
restaurant.Description: A busy bar, a dining room with dark wood tables and banquette seating, and moody lighting—Daniel's looks like a page ripped from the playbook of American steakhouses. This is a place to come with a group, as the large menu of steakhouse favorites is designed for sampling and sharing. Settle in over wagyu tartare or a Floridian take on oysters Rockefeller before tucking in to one of the perfectly cooked steaks. Of course there must be sides, especially grilled asparagus and corn pudding. Desserts may be sized for a crowd but it's difficult not to indulge when met with classics like key lime pie or a warm chocolate chip cookie served in a skillet with vanilla ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Daphne's
restaurant.Address: 299 Halsey St., Brooklyn, NY, 11216, USA
restaurant.Description: Set on the corner of Halsey and Throop in Bed-Stuy, Daphne's sparkles ever so subtly thanks to a front window covered with strands of tiny, twinkling silver beads. But it's not just the exterior that invites curiosity; this refined, contemporary Italian-American restaurant dazzles with its tightly edited menu, too. From shareable plates and house-made pasta to entrees, there is something tempting at every turn. Do not miss the delicious golden-brown focaccia with anchovy butter or grilled mortadella over a bed of house-made giardiniera. Then, mustard green pesto stars in a dish of radiatore pasta, while a grilled pork chop with slow-cooked greens, pancetta, and cicerchia beans is especially flavorful and tender.

restaurant.Name: Das Ethiopian Cuisine
restaurant.Address: 1201 28th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20007, USA
restaurant.Description: In a classic Georgetown townhouse, Das (which in Amharic means a large tent where families and communities gather for celebrations and communal meals) has been an ambassador for Ethiopian cuisine since 2011. The menu features various wats (slow-cooked stews, like the chicken doro alicha wat, flavored with curry and tamarind and served with hard-boiled egg), tibs (sautéed dishes like shrimp with onions, red pepper, garlic and bell pepper), and plenty of vegetarian options, all eaten using the spongy pancake-type injera bread. Dessert leans classically European with baba au rhum, torta della nonna and gelato on offer.

restaurant.Name: Daytrader Tiki Bar and Restaurant
restaurant.Address: 2236 E. County Hwy., Ste. 30A, Unit 4 & 5, Seaside, FL, 32459, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Nestled within the small Seaside community, The Daytrader Tiki Bar and Restaurant leans into the tropical tiki vibe without any of the expected kitsch. Colorful and contemporary with plenty of outdoor seating (some even resembling tiny beach shacks), this spot is all about tiki-style cocktails and a menu that skews both Polynesian and Hawaiian. Start with some sharable snacks like the boiled peanuts, seasoned with anise, ginger and togarashi. Try the pork lumpia with sweet chili dipping sauce and the crispy tuna rice with lime oil, lava salt and fried garlic before tucking into one of the many handhelds, rice bowls and seafood-forward main dishes. The not-too-sweet coconut custard cream pie with mile-high meringue and passion fruit sauce is the perfect ending.

restaurant.Name: Dear Emilia
restaurant.Address: 3615 Delgany St., Denver, CO, 80216, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Ty Leon has delivered a love letter to Italy's Emilia-Romagna with Dear Emilia. The space is comfortable with wood tables, booths and a full-service chef's counter with prime views into the open kitchen. From the cocktails to the dishes, it's all Italian here. These are plates intended for sharing, including appetizers like gnocco frito topped with thinly sliced smoked proscuitto domestico served over mostarda di stagione. Savor entrees like their lasagne verde, featuring a rolled spinach pasta layered with Bolognese, bechamel and pomodoro, or tuck into heartier options like whey-braised pork shoulder accompanied by a creamy Colorado polenta and finished with pear butter and breadcrumbs.End the meal with one of their desserts like tiramisu or the torta tenerina.

restaurant.Name: Dear Jane's
restaurant.Address: 13950 Panay Way, Marina del Rey, CA, 90292, USA
restaurant.Description: In case this Marina del Rey restaurant's glass wall with views of the boats outside didn't give it away, Dear Jane's celebrates the life aquatic with its focus on old school seafood and Continental cuisine. This spot pours it on with large portions and over-the-top flourishes (caviar makes a regular appearance) while keeping things grounded with strong cooking. Shrimp Louie, done tableside, is sized to share, as is the wedge, which brilliantly subs in vinaigrette in place of creamy dressing. Blackened salmon with a rich parsley and caper sauce is perfectly cooked, and lemony potatoes are a nice accompaniment. Signature cocktails riff on the famous Janes but will you choose Jetson, Goodall or Austen?

restaurant.Name: Del Mar
restaurant.Address: 791 Wharf St. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Chef Fabio Trabocchi celebrates the flavors of Spain in this stylish, resort-chic restaurant at the Wharf. With coastal blues and whites, polished brass fixtures and large windows overlooking the Potomac, the yawning space has room for everybody. The cooking, meanwhile, delivers in spades, bringing finesse and refinement to classics like Andalucian garlic shrimp studded with croutons, and Spanish tortilla lined with caramelized onions. Barely touched or simply prepared, beautifully presented fish are a highlight, alongside seasonal soups and hearty paellas. The beverage program is equally impressive, featuring an extensive vermouth selection as well as a superb wine list highlighting gems and superstars from across Spain.

restaurant.Name: Delbar
restaurant.Address: 870 Inman Village Pkwy. NE, Ste. 1, Atlanta, GA, 30307, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This Middle Eastern spot from Fares Kargar is all about bringing people together over flavorful and authentic food. There is a generous spirit here, where the name translates to "heart, captured." The menu, a nod to the dishes Kargar grew up with, is designed for sharing, with spreads and small bites to start, an entire section dedicated to tahdig, that festive Persian crispy rice dish, and meats. Add the dill labneh to the house bread opener, then go for the lamb neck that is falling-off-the-bone tender, and sabzi polo, a basmati rice dish flavored with scallions and herbs and topped with crispy onions. Conclude the evening with a decadent treat like baklava ice cream or pistachio lava cake with cardamom ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Demera Ethiopian Restaurant
restaurant.Address: 4801 N. Broadway, Chicago, IL, 60640, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Demera has long been a favorite in Uptown for its warm hospitality and authentic Ethiopian cooking. The bright, inviting dining room encourages communal meals, where platters arrive on top of tangy, house-made injera that doubles as both plate and utensil. The extensive menu offers everything from richly spiced stews and grilled meats to an array of thoughtfully prepared vegetarian dishes, making it equally appealing to newcomers and regulars alike. Fresh ingredients, vibrant seasoning and generous portions define the cooking, and the traditional family-style service encourages sharing and sampling across the table.

restaurant.Name: Destroyer
restaurant.Address: 3578 Hayden Ave., Culver City, CA, 90232, USA
restaurant.Description: The architecturally intriguing Hayden Tract district is the perfect backdrop for Jordan Kahn's adventurous Destroyer, located just across the street from sister restaurant, Vespertine. The minimalist interior keeps your attention on the food, where each plate is a complex composition of flavors that are bound to delight and surprise. Begin with such harmonious starters as avocado confit, a half avocado dusted with their onion ash and served with confit tomatoes and dressed arugula that is simple but impressive. Koshikari rice porridge delivers depth and a riot of textures, while the milk chocolate crémeux finished with almond streusel, praline and a dusting of frozen cucumber cream is a striking closer.

restaurant.Name: Di An Pho
restaurant.Address: 12934 Bellaire Blvd., Ste. 108, Houston, TX, 77072, USA
restaurant.Description: As soon as it opens, this place is bustling with patrons, all here to slurp bowls of pho. It's a lively spot with music playing and a convivial vibe. The straightforward menu promises exactly what everyone is here for: a variety of beef and chicken noodle soups. You won't go wrong with any selection, but pho dac biet with noodles along with a mix of beef filet, brisket, tendon and tripe is an especially hearty choice. Don't skip the Vietnamese coffee, as it's a treat.

restaurant.Name: Di Vino Rosso
restaurant.Address: 807 Gervais St., Ste. 100, Columbia, SC, 29201, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Exposed brick walls and tile floors hint at the building's former incarnation as a Ford dealership but this address has been home to Di Vino Rosso for more than two decades. This longstanding Italian restaurant is a Columbia favorite, known for its focused menu of Italian staples made with local ingredients (they even list their farmers on the back of the menu). Tuck into a bowl of meatballs resting in tomato sauce before a plate of pappardelle with a rich and flavorful wild boat and Italian sausage Bolognese sauce. While the savory dishes are certainly the highlight, end the meal with an espresso and tiramisu for a classic finish. ---

restaurant.Name: Diavola
restaurant.Address: 21021 Geyserville Ave., Geyserville, CA, 95441, USA
restaurant.Description: Its home in downtown Geyserville has a Wild West appeal, and the interior, styled with vintage film posters and antique tools, has a playful yet smart vibe. Diavola is certainly one of the most popular spots for miles—within minutes of opening, it's always a full house.The crowds are here for pizzas, like the signature combo of spicy meatballs, red peppers, provolone, pine nuts and raisins or the smoked pork belly, goat cheese and scallion, perhaps. Top-notch house ingredients include salumi, lardo and cured olives. But, that’s not to count out their pastas, including linguine tossed with baby octopus, bone marrow, zucchini and bottarga. Finish with their chocolate pistachio semifreddo paired with a Blue Bottle espresso.

restaurant.Name: Din Ho Chinese BBQ
restaurant.Address: 8557 Research Blvd., Ste. 116, Austin, TX, 78758, USA
restaurant.Description: A longtime Austin favorite, Din Ho specializes in Cantonese barbecue and traditional Chinese cooking served in a lively, family-friendly setting. Roast duck, Beijing duck, char siu and crispy pork belly are prepared daily and displayed prominently at the entrance, while an expansive menu spans noodle soups, clay pots, seafood dishes, stir-fries and house specialties. Generous portions, fair prices and consistently satisfying cooking have made this local institution a destination for three decades.

restaurant.Name: Dingles Public House
restaurant.Address: 333 Fulton St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
restaurant.Description: The memorable name of this handsome establishment, tucked away in the back of a boutique Hayes Valley hotel, comes from owners Anissa and George Dingle—natch. She manages the well-edited beverage program, from the expected draughts to wine and pleasingly simple cocktails, while he has the run of the kitchen, serving up classic, unfussy British pub fare with an edge of refinement. Beer-battered fish and chips, paired with classic mushy peas and curry sauce, hits its mark, as does a spot-on Scotch egg, with its jammy yolk and crunchy, panko-crusted exterior, and Welsh rarebit makes a concession to the States with Jasper Hill Farm cheddar from Vermont. Sticky toffee pudding with stout caramel and brown butter ice cream is no slouch, either.

restaurant.Name: Dio Deka
restaurant.Address: Hotel Los Gatos, 210 E. Main St., Los Gatos, CA, 95030, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Dio Deka may specialize in Greek food, but this is no typical taverna, as the stylish dining room (complete with a roaring fireplace) ably demonstrates. A wealthy, well-dressed Los Gatos crowd flocks to the front patio on warm evenings, dining and people-watching within the vine-covered walls of the Hotel Los Gatos. The bar also draws a brace of cheery regulars. Nothing beats a mesquite-grilled and oven-baked pita with olive oil and oregano to kick off the meal. Then, keep things Greek: think stuffed grape leaves with tender braised beef cheek or a bright pan-seared local salmon with roasted yellow peppers, potatoes and artichokes. The adventurous shouldn’t miss out on the fun offering of Greek wines, and sweet buffs should allow space for the crema me meli, a fantastic burnt-honey mousse with almond and lemon.

restaurant.Name: Dio Mio
restaurant.Address: 3264 Larimer St., Denver, CO, 80205, USA
restaurant.Description: Chefs/owners Spencer White and Alex Figura have a background in fine dining, but this popular fast-casual concept thrives on an accessible, laid-back format. Creativity and a clear understanding of flavor go hand in hand on a small, seasonal menu, with house-made forming the centerpiece of the operation (both literally and figuratively—a pasta production table is visible at the heart of the kitchen), from tradition-adjacent mafaldine cacio e pepe, boosted with pink peppercorn, to totally iconoclastic combinations like casarecce with shrimp, dill and toasted parmesan.

restaurant.Name: Discada
restaurant.Address: 1700 E. César Chavez St., Austin, TX, 78702, USA
restaurant.Description: Head to East Austin to find this stationary food truck where they only have one thing on their mind—discada. It may be the easiest order you've ever made, and the only decision you'll need to make is how many taquitos you want. As for the food, it's all in the name. Discada is a Northern Mexican style of cooking with different cuts of beef and pork cooked together with aromatic vegetables. Their version also adds bacon, onion, and roasted poblano peppers, all cooked down and served taquito style in single layers of yellow corn tortillas. Topped with a pulverized pineapple slaw and served with fresh salsa on the side, it's a delicious style not often seen. Elote and soft drinks round out the hyper-focused offerings.

restaurant.Name: Don Angie
restaurant.Address: 103 Greenwich Ave., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This darling of a dining room is designed with elegant blue-gray leather banquettes, bentwood chairs, and a dark checkerboard floor. Potted plants, moody lighting, and a rustic bar with brass accents make it a dream-worthy refuge for a romantic tête-à-tête. Married couple, Angie Rito and Scott Tacinelli, are the brains behind this venture, where the team takes risks that result in highly creative and enriching cuisine.While the menu feels like an American story as told through an Italian lens, Asian elements also make guest appearances as in the spicy pepperoni fried rice gussied-up with tender grilled calamari. Playful aptly describes the combination of spicy veal tartare and tuna carpaccio. Pastas are similarly prolific, like the paprika-tinted sorpresine with smoked mussels or sourdough pasta in a 'nduja sauce with mezcal-braised chicken. Pesce alla griglia in a clam broth and Sicilian scallop crudo speak of bold flavors and polished methods.Desserts, such as the fior di latte mochi with golden Taggiasca olive oil or black cocoa tiramisu garnished with feuilletine, are just the icing on the cake. Go for over-the-top glee with a sip of house-made root beer amaro.

restaurant.Name: Don Antonio
restaurant.Address: 309 W. 50th St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: The namesake outpost is located in Naples and has been running strong since 1901. Meanwhile in Midtown, Don Antonio by Starita has been slinging authentic Neapolitan-style, woodfired pizza since 2012, thanks to Don's daughter, Giorgia Caporuscio, who learned the family craft and took over the family business here. This kitchen's signature is the Montanara Starita—a lightly fried pizza laced with house-made tomato sauce, smoked mozzarella, and basil, then finished in the wood-fired oven. But really, who could stop there with treasures like the salsiccia e friarielli pizza with fennel sausage or the delicious frittatine, where chopped spaghetti pieces and ham are blended with Buffalo mozzarella, breaded, and fried to a golden crisp.

restaurant.Name: Donaji
restaurant.Address: 3161 24th St., San Francisco, CA, 94110, USA
restaurant.Description: Donaji, from Chef Isai Cuevas, who first built a loyal following selling tamales at Bay Area farmers’ markets, remains a cheerful neighborhood spot centered around Oaxacan cooking and exceptional masa work. Named after a Zapotec princess in homage to the chef’s roots, the restaurant continues to showcase handmade tortillas, earthy moles and carefully prepared antojitos. Tamales remain a highlight, but dishes like crispy tacos dorados de pollo with black bean purée and crema, or enchiladas draped in a deep, complex 20-ingredient mole negro, reveal the kitchen’s attention to detail just as clearly. Larger plates, including pollo asado or short ribs with mole coloradito, further highlight the richness and depth of Oaxacan flavors. House-made aguas frescas remain the perfect accompaniment to the savory, earthy fare.

restaurant.Name: Dons Bogam
restaurant.Address: 17 E. 32nd St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
restaurant.Description: At Dons Bogam, the food is fantastic and service indulgent. From the festive bar up front right down to those two-tops sporting blazing grills, every seat is filled, so reserve ahead. Make no mistake: this is no average K-town joint. Inside, a top-notch venting system lets diners enjoy a smoke-free evening of exceptional grilled meats. Start with fried pork mandu, which are on-point and divine. Pork belly marinated in red wine is smoky and supremely tender, but for the ultimate payoff, opt for the beef platter. It features thinly sliced maeun and yangnyeom galbi set beside meaty king trumpet mushrooms. In Midtown for meetings? Pop in for the BBQ lunch, a fun and interactive midday meal that is leaps above a quick grab-and-go salad, yet just as healthy.

restaurant.Name: Dry Creek Kitchen
restaurant.Address: Hotel Healdsburg, 317 Healdsburg Ave., Healdsburg, CA, 95448, USA
restaurant.Description: Open since 2001, this veteran haunt by Chef Charlie Palmer is attached to the sleek Hotel Healdsburg. Airy and elegant, the vaulted room boasts white tablecloths as well as large windows overlooking the downtown square. The cooking, meanwhile, is contemporary in design, with farm-sourced ingredients prepared with style. Snack on oxtail dumplings before moving on to an electric kanpachi tiradito. Mains cover the gamut: Salmon, duck, lamb and pork chops. Finish with an indulgent “cookie butter mousse bomb.”

restaurant.Name: Dubrovnik
restaurant.Address: 721 Main St., New Rochelle, NY, 10801, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Nestled along New Rochelle's more commercial streets, Dubrovnik is a real find—with the added bonus of live Croatian music on certain nights. Diners come from near and far to feast on their items from the wood-burning oven. Equally appealing is the interior design. Next door to the owner’s cabinetry business, everything here is custom-made. Attention to detail isn’t just a hallmark of their décor though; the menu follows close at hand, offering the likes of shatteringly crisp spring rolls filled with tender beef and vegetables and served with a spiced tartar sauce. Or try something cooked on their wood-fired grill like branzino served with smoky vegetables and broccoli rabe risotto, before savoring palačinke (crêpes with peach jam).

restaurant.Name: Dunsmoor
restaurant.Address: 3501 Eagle Rock Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90065, USA
restaurant.Description: With embers glowing, flames snapping and smoke billowing, two ferocious ovens serve as the twin hearts and hearths of this Glassell Park hot spot. Much of the Southern-inspired menu must pass through them — oysters, cornbread, rib eyes and pork chops. Nearly everything here offers some kind of hearty, no-nonsense kind of comfort. Highlights include the excellent pork and green chili stew; grilled quail with pepper jelly; and braised greens that bubble away by the coals all evening. Long communal tables set with flickering wax candles hold the center of the room while prized counter seats offer front row views of a kitchen in constant motion. In the far back, find a calm, intimate wine bar serving a lighter, more limited slice of the dinner menu.

restaurant.Name: Dân Dã
restaurant.Address: 9945 E. Colfax Ave., Aurora, CO, 80010, USA
restaurant.Description: Come to this casual Aurora spot run by sisters An and Thao Nguyen for straightforward but satisfying Vietnamese comfort food. The friendly staff are happy to walk you through the menu with a wide variety, though the build-your-own noodle bowls are always a hit. Vietnamese classics like curry dishes and claypot offerings are signatures and with a menu designed for sharing, why stop at just one? Beer, sake, soju and wine are also available.

restaurant.Name: Dōgon
restaurant.Address: Salamander Hotel,1330 Maryland Ave. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
restaurant.Description: Tucked inside the Salamander Hotel, Chef Kwame Onwuachi's restaurant named for the West African Dogon tribe offers a blend of African and Caribbean inspiration alongside nods to Washington, D.C. The tightly edited menu presents a selection of boldly flavored small and large plates intended for sharing. Each dish is presented with flair and nuance, as in the hoe crab, served in a shell with shredded crab and shito alongside plantain cakes with aji verde sauce. Braised cabbage is given a good char, then paired with a coconut vinegar sauce, while rum cake is far from traditional thanks to the surprise of charred gooseberries. A clever cocktail list is complemented by its N/A counterparts, and the wine list is especially thoughtful.

restaurant.Name: East Harbor Seafood Palace
restaurant.Address: 714 65th St., Brooklyn, NY, 11220, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Credit cards not accepted,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Guests can barely get through this front door, where crowds pack in on weekends for dim sum. They wait patiently as an announcer shouts reservation numbers over a booming speaker—like a game of high-stakes bingo. Dim sum is a well-orchestrated affair, with steaming carts rolling by and waiters ferrying trays into the gold-accented dining room. Eyes can guide the ordering when it comes to the carts, stocked with authentic bites. Highlights include the siu mai, followed by rice noodles wrapped around shrimp and doused in a sweet soy sauce. Black bean spare ribs are flavorful, but don't skip the zongzi—tea leaf-wrapped sticky rice stuffed with pork and mushrooms.Things are more tame on weekdays, but that just means there's no need to fight the lines.

restaurant.Name: Easy Bistro & Bar
restaurant.Address: 801 Chestnut St., Chattanooga, TN, 37402, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This beloved locals' haunt is tucked into downtown Chattanooga, and Easy Bistro is just that. Comfortable but unfussy, this spot from Erik and Amanda Niel has been around for more than two decades. They open early with oyster hour, and it's always a hit. The menu is American at heart, with oysters and small plates, pasta, meat and side dishes, all created with a seasonal mindset. Tagliatelle with Florida rock shrimp and bottarga in a lemon butter sauce is given a boost of texture courtesy of Appalachian rye breadcrumbs, while pot de creme or ricotta doughnuts are worthy desserts. .

restaurant.Name: Edoboy
restaurant.Address: 728 N. Thornton Ave., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
restaurant.Description: From the same team behind Tori Tori and Domu, this casual concept delivers something sleek and simple—a standing sushi counter. It's not a gimmick, it's designed to be fast and fun, and it's a perfect place to bring friends. Be sure to arrive promptly, since you're given a set time slot and you'll be whisked into the space at the start of yours. Once there you'll select a dozen pieces from the selection of nigiri, seared nigiri and hand rolls. Some of the best bites include a sweet Hokkaido scallop finished with briny uni from Tasmania; seared sea bream with uni butter, lemon and sea salt; and spicy Faroe Island salmon with edo sauce, cucumber and fried garlic rolled in crispy nori. Dinner is rounded out with miso soup made in house from the bones and trimmings of the day.

restaurant.Name: Eggboy
restaurant.Address: 1241 Mayport Rd., Atlantic Beach, FL, 32233, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This casual Atlantic Beach spot with a vaguely bodega vibe from brothers Nick and Zachary Presti is all about breakfast. The duo is busy churning out decadent, over-the-top, egg-focused sandwiches in the most delicious way. Try the full Monty with maple pepper sausage, applewood smoked bacon and soft, cheesy scrambled eggs sandwiched between slices of brioche French toast and a side of a sweet maple leche. Consider the large, flaky chicken biscuit with crispy thigh meat, redeye aioli (optional) and why not take it a step further by indulging in an add-on of egg and cheese to really dress it up? Other worthy items include the loaded spuds and cinnamon rolls. No matter what you try, you are sure to be flocking back for more sometime soon.

restaurant.Name: El Buen Comer
restaurant.Address: 3435 Mission St., San Francisco, CA, 94110, USA
restaurant.Description: “Good eats” are promised right in the name of this approachable neighborhood restaurant on the outskirts of the Mission, and La Cocina alum Isabel Caudillo delivers in full. Her menu highlights the cooking of her native Mexico City, featuring homestyle dishes like her signature guisados, as in tender, pork ribs slowly simmered in salsa verde, served with nopales and plenty of warm, handmade corn tortillas to mop up every last drop of the delectable sauce. The focused menu is rounded out with other classics: pambazos, chiles rellenos and fresh-fried tortilla chips accompanied by a hefty scoop of guacamole and zippy house-made salsas. Save room for Caudillo’s desserts, like a chocoflan that combines silky caramelized custard and rich chocolate cake.

restaurant.Name: El Carlos Elegante
restaurant.Address: 1400 N. Riverfront Blvd., Dallas, TX, 75207, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: Don’t be fooled by the nondescript exterior. Inside, this lively spot opens into a warm, rustic dining room with a wood-fired grill at its center. Begin with a drink in the lounge or grab a seat at the horseshoe counter to watch the action. The menu moves from small “one hitter” bites like crab cakes and garbanzo sopes to larger, shareable plates. Grilled meats are the focus, including pork al pastor served with house-made masa for building tacos at the table. Charred okra and shishitos are a strong side, and Mexican chocolate pot de crème closes the meal on a rich note. A deep tequila and mezcal selection completes the offering.

restaurant.Name: El Fish Marisqueria
restaurant.Address: 155 Amsterdam Ave., New York, NY, 10023, USA
restaurant.Description: Don't let the name fool you—this is not your average seafood shack. Instead, this Upper West Side restaurant invites guests to settle into a warm, modern space anchored by a lively bar that draws locals for cocktails and zero-proof drinks. Quality seafood drives the menu, and while some plates lean contemporary, start with the para empezar section for a proper marisqueria-style feast. The Tostada Ensenada, piled high with fresh crab salad, shrimp, octopus and a spicy macha salsa on a crisp tostada, is a standout: bold, generous and best eaten with your hands.Didn't snag a reservation? The raw bar is ideal for walk-ins or solo dining.

restaurant.Name: El Secreto de Rosita
restaurant.Address: 1624 U St. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.Description: The space is snug, romantic and trendy; its cooking is notably creative; and beverages are reviving. Tastefully decked out with artwork, smoky mirrors and a full bar, gracious servers along with plush seats will lull you into a soothing and delicious meal.The dynamic menu certainly leans Peruvian; it also embraces the nation's wide terrain—from the coast all the way to influences from Europe and Asia. Behold the tiradito, featuring sashimi-grade ahi tuna with a passion fruit-and-orange sauce. Classics, like ají de gallina, is served with rice; while the much raved-about arroz chaufa is a global delight. Desserts, like the seasonal flan, warrant bright, beaming smiles.

restaurant.Name: Ela Curry & Cocktails
restaurant.Address: 4650 Donald Ross Rd., Ste. 100, West Palm Beach, FL, 33418, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Amid lush greenery framing the entrance, this restaurant opens to a range of comfortable velvet seating in shades of green and mustard yellow, surrounded by subtle peacock motif artwork throughout the space, adding a touch of color and personality. The menu focuses on Indian cuisine, rooted in regional flavors. Lamb samosas with their savory filling of ground lamb and peas in a flaky pastry purse, well spiced with a gentle heat and served with a cilantro mint chutney, are the perfect starter. Then, move on to the Kerala curried beef short rib, fork tender and served with piping hot, fluffy basmati rice. For sides, try the paratha with tamarind and green mango chutneys. Both lean sweet but offer good depth, with the mango chutney delivering a pleasant touch of heat.

restaurant.Name: Elcielo Bistró DC
restaurant.Address: 1280 4th St. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: In Union Market, this brick-fronted former warehouse is home to the fine dining Elcielo as well as the Bistró, which offers a more accessible take on Chef Juan Manuel Barriento's Colombian-inspired modern cuisine in a luminous and contemporary space with cocktail bar at one end. The à la carte features the likes of hamachi tiradito with sesame oil, leeks and white shoyu; a shrimp empanada with garlic mayo and Meyer lemon; and grass-fed bison ribeye with chimichurri and Appalachian cheese. For dessert, lean classic with flan with vanilla and salted caramel. Professional service and a real desire to act as ambassadors for Colombia add to the appeal.

restaurant.Name: Elcielo New York
restaurant.Address: Virgin Hotel NYC, 1227 Broadway, New York, NY, 10001, USA
restaurant.Description: Sequestered away in a corner of the Virgin Hotel, this experience comes courtesy of Chef Juan Manuel Barrientos, whose culinary footprint crosses states and countries. Large tables clad in white tablecloths and surrounded by floor-to-ceiling glass set the stage for a modern tasting that pulls inspiration from Latin America and, more specifically, Colombia. A meal here is redolent of the tropics. The "tree of life” bread, the chocolate experience and an ornate coffee ceremony are signatures intertwined with courses like a shio koji-marinated duck sauced with a sabayon of honey and passion fruit. A relaxed, attentive team enhances one's time here with stories, attention and sincerity.

restaurant.Name: Electric Bleu
restaurant.Address: 3523 S. Centinela Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90066, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef/owner Craig Hopson's Electric Bleu is indeed buzzy; this California-meets-French bistro in Mar Vista draws a crowd for its likeable plates. Seating at the bar, counter and tables is tight and a hot ticket, so make reservations (especially on weekends) to savor starters like sauteed, foraged chanterelles with parmesan, parsnips and Treviso tardivo, or entrees such as duck breast with dates, saffron and green olives. Pick and choose from the à la carte offerings or go for the prix fixe with plates prepped in the open kitchen for all to see. Desserts, like their local lime tart with whipped crème fraîche, are worth saving room for, and the wine list is stocked with a nice selection of bottles.

restaurant.Name: Element 47
restaurant.Address: The Little Nell, 675 E. Durant Ave, Aspen, CO, 81611, USA
restaurant.Description: The name is a nod to Aspen’s origins as a silver mining town, and its location inside the luxurious Little Nell Hotel, mere steps away from the slopes, is certainly glitzy. Enter the sleek, modern dining room through the lounge warmed by a crackling fireplace and settle in for an approachable menu that has something for everyone. The lunch crowd leans into comforting, warm bowls of tortilla soup and verdant salads. Dinner is a more involved affair, raising the stakes with the likes of lobster, roast duck and even a Wellington. Diners will make note of the array of bottles displayed behind glass in the bar area, a telltale sign of the restaurant’s impressive wine program.

restaurant.Name: Elfegne
restaurant.Address: 2420 18th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: This family-owned and operated Adams Morgan spot easily gives its brethren a run for their money—the food is that good. Its interior is welcoming, flooded with natural light and generously spaced tables; comfortable booths along one wall, beautiful artwork, as well as a long bar pouring wines and spirits welcomes one and all.This kitchen's exquisite cuisine reflects the many fascinating nuances of Ethiopia itself. While many cultures break bread together, few do it as well as this one, where injera is torn apart to scoop up stews, like awaze tibs. Its tender lamb cubes in a smoky, brick-red berbere are simmered to tender perfection, then crowned with greens, spicy lentils and potatoes for a dish that rarely receives the credit—or fanfare—it is due.

restaurant.Name: Elina's
restaurant.Address: 1202 W. Grand Ave., Chicago, IL, 60642, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: What's the best Italian-American restaurant in town? There is no right answer. Then consider Chef/owners Ian Rusnak and Eric Safin's newcomer and you might just change your mind. With Sinatra crooning overhead, sleek wood overtones, and handsome leather, it's hard not to be besotted by this intimate little gem—and everyone is.A hearty bread basket is the kickoff of dreams, while that cherished classic, clams casino, flaunts a divine blend of taste and texture. Rigatoni a la vodka requires little introduction but a garnish of breadcrumbs makes a welcome surprise. Then, chicken parmesan arrives surmounted with marinara and mozz. If the words nostalgic and classic come to mind, you get the picture.

restaurant.Name: Ella
restaurant.Address: 1131 K St., Sacramento, CA, 95814, USA
restaurant.Description: This upscale beauty in downtown Sacramento is equal parts rustic and refined, with floor-to-ceiling curtains, thick linens and a colorful overhang comprised of antique wood. You're likely to be seated among regulars chatting with the attentive staff while exploring the thoughtful wine selections. The menu offers creative takes on globally influenced dishes, while perfectly crispy Southern fried chicken remains a staple and rightfully so. The bar is also a great place to linger — with an expertly prepared cocktail, like the house gin and tonic.

restaurant.Name: Elliott Aster
restaurant.Address: 501 5th Ave. NE, St. Petersburg, FL, 33701, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: Located within the Vinoy Resort and Golf Club, with its high ceilings and large chandeliers, this Italian-inspired steakhouse has a grand feel. The menu is centered around wood-fired steaks and house-made pastas, blending classic Italian foundations with a polished steakhouse sensibility. Begin with the focaccia "pull apart" rolls with pecorino and taleggio cheese and wildflower honey. If pasta is your passion, have the radiatore alla vodka with a decadent sauce that clings to every ridge and finishes with a little heat from Calabrian chili. Complete your meal with a caramel coffee budino, served in a sundae glass topped with a chocolate cookie crumble.

restaurant.Name: Elmina
restaurant.Address: 2208 14th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.Description: Elmina is the kind of place with wide-reaching appeal, where a warm spirit and a stylish, contemporary decor encourage lingering over Chef Eric Adjepong's modern West African/Ghanian cuisine. Choose between a multicourse tasting menu or the à la carte bar menu, a play on Ghana’s popular, counter-service-style “chop bars,” with snacks like tartare, okra fries and pork belly. Those who opt for the tasting will be rewarded with the likes of scallop crudo with cucumber granita and coconut broth, as well as braised goat with fufu, or pounded plantain and cassava, and a tableside pour of creamy, deep orange-red nkati nkwan sauce. Malva pudding cake with sweet, pickled apricot and vanilla gelato is a delightful ending.

restaurant.Name: Elsie's Plate & Pie
restaurant.Address: 3145 Government St., Baton Rouge, LA, 70806, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Paul Chauvin Dupré has created an homage to his grandmother with Elsie's Plate & Pie. It's quite casual, with a welcoming and friendly vibe, and it's often crowded, so you'll likely need to wait for a table or sit at the full-service bar. They have a number of offerings but make sure to try their pies—both sweet and savory. Chicken pot pie with peppers in a tasso cream sauce is served in a cast iron skillet for a homey touch and a taste of home, but don't even think about skipping out before enjoying dessert. Can't decide which one to order? Opt for a flight with four varieties.

restaurant.Name: Elyu Omakase
restaurant.Address: 2626 Ponce de Leon Blvd., Unit 3, Coral Gables, FL, 33134, USA
restaurant.Description: Enter this hushed space defined by a blonde wood counter set with a dozen warm wood chairs and it would be natural to assume it's a traditional Japanese restaurant. This Coral Gables spot isn't, however, as Chef Reiji Yoshizawa weaves together his Japanese and Filipino heritage for a highly original omakase. Expect creativity and a bit of showmanship at this intimate space where meals begin with a series of snacks, including an impressive Kumamoto oyster in a "shell" made of dashi. Whimsical, it's also loaded with flavor. Madai and persimmon, sliced and plated to look like a rose, create a vibrant, bold dish. The sushi course includes several highlights, including the binchotan-seared blackthroat sea perch, before rounding out the meal with miso ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Eléa
restaurant.Address: 217 W. 85th St., New York, NY, 10024, USA
restaurant.Description: Fitted out with whitewashed brick walls, weathered wood beams, and pretty lighting, this bi-level space exudes all the modern Med feels. Add on the deliciously rustic food and you have a win. Imagine everything from creamy spreads with pita bread to fresh fish. Following suit, ingredients are given the spotlight in the likes of htipiti (feta with roasted chili pepper) as well as whole grilled tsipoura in a lemon, olive oil, and caper sauce. The stuffed tomato filled with arborio rice, golden raisins, pine nuts, and herbs is a savory delight, as is the elevated version of a classic moussaka. Finish with sokolatina, a scoop of Valrhona chocolate mousse topped with cherries and resting atop a chocolate cookie.

restaurant.Name: Ember
restaurant.Address: 1200 E. Grand Ave., Arroyo Grande, CA, 93420, USA
restaurant.Description: Ember was at the forefront of open-fire cooking on the Central Coast when it opened, and this Arroyo Grande charmer still hasn’t lost its spark. Its inviting industrial-rustic interior remains a fitting backdrop for the restaurant’s heartfelt and approachable cooking. The contemporary menu leans into comforting flavors and wood-fired touches, from summer squash bruschetta layered with zucchini ribbons, roasted torpedo onions, ricotta-goat cheese, caramelized fennel aioli and mint on grilled walnut bread, to staples like the grilled under-a-brick chicken and the towering 50-layer lasagna. Desserts maintain the same crowd-pleasing spirit, as in a cream puff filled with dark chocolate mousse and strawberry Chantilly, served alongside strawberry ice cream and angel food cake.

restaurant.Name: Enoteca Maria
restaurant.Address: 27 Hyatt St., Staten Island, NY, 10301, USA
restaurant.Description: Enoteca Maria is just blocks from St. George Terminal and brought to you by Joe Scaravella, whose cookbook, Nonna’s House, has been earning him (and this tiny gem) much applause. This is the kind of place where the phone is always ringing and it's perpetually packed with guests eager to sample the cooking, which changes nightly depending on which nonnas are cooking. There is a clear adoration for these stars of the show. Expect soul-soothing dishes like Nonna Zoraida from Paraguay's traditional vori vori, a dish of chicken soup with cheese and cornmeal dumplings, shredded chicken, and vegetables. Meanwhile, if Nonna Yumi from Japan is in the kitchen, you'll find a Hokkaido kombu seaweed salad with house-made yuzu-ginger vinaigrette.

restaurant.Name: Enso
restaurant.Address: 117 Berry St., Brooklyn, NY, 11249, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Located in the heart of Williamsburg, Enso is sleek and modern. Most guests are here for Chef Nick Wang's omakase, comprised of edomae-style sushi, though à la carte offerings are available in the bar and garden. It all begins with otsumami like anago, crispy and golden-fried, garnished with yuzu zest and served with green tea sea salt. Nigiri courses feature the likes of blue mackerel from Chiba that has been cured with Okinawan sea salt and marinated in aged vinegar. Sea urchin from Hokkaido, simply served with a sprinkle of salt over rice, is as sweet and meltingly tender as hoped.

restaurant.Name: Entre Nous
restaurant.Address: 39 Clifton Pl., Brooklyn, NY, 11238, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This Clinton Hill wine bar channels the spirit of a French apéro with ease and confidence. It’s the kind of place that works just as well for a single glass and a snack as it does for settling in with friends. The room is warmly lit and inviting, anchored by a handsome copper bar wrapped in cherry wood. A wall of bottles hints at the depth of the natural wine program, and the food rises well above what the casual setting might suggest. French-leaning small plates are cooked with intention and restraint: chicken liver parfait with cornichons, crisp mushroom croquettes with truffle aioli, and a bright Jonah crab salad that lets the seafood lead. Heartier dishes like roasted carrots with lentils and chèvre feel rustic and satisfying.

restaurant.Name: Ernest
restaurant.Address: 1890 Bryant St., Ste. 100, San Francisco, CA, 94110, USA
restaurant.Description: Once you’ve managed to make your way inside (the entrance is around the block from the address, at the corner of Florida & Mariposa), you’ll meet no additional difficulty in finding fun at this unorthodox Mission hotspot. Chef Brandon Rice’s hip, irreverent cooking style sets the vibe, exemplified in fancy-meets-comforting combos like prawn toast with green garlic tartar sauce. A small, eclectic menu spans raw bar items like crudos and oysters, plus a handful of snacks and more substantial mains, all featuring top-notch seasonal products. To try nearly everything, let the kitchen take the reins in the form of a family-style fixed menu. Reservations are snapped up quickly, but the bar is open for walk-ins—the better to sample a terrific cocktail program.

restaurant.Name: Ernesto's
restaurant.Address: 259 E. Broadway, New York, NY, 10002, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: It’s all too easy to find favor in this bustling Basque getaway, located at the foot of the Brooklyn and Manhattan Bridges. Sleek coffee-brown tables, globe light fixtures dangling throughout, and a long, marble-top bar exude midcentury-modern style, while a constant crowd fosters a near electric vibe. Indeed, everything is meant to be shared, and everyone is having a good time.A mound of house-made potato chips layered with thin slices of jamón Ibérico is a fitting start, before piling the table with heartier dishes like meltingly tender tripe slow-braised with tomatoes and morcilla. Then linger over an equally rich grilled squad breast served with rice and mushrooms. The wine list is an impressive tomb of small organic and biodynamic Spanish producers.

restaurant.Name: Este
restaurant.Address: 2113 Manor Rd., Austin, TX, 78722, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: Set in a converted bungalow in East Austin, Este sparkles with a cool vibe while highlighting contemporary Mexican cuisine with a seafood focus. Ceviche amarillo with white fish and a piña turmeric broth is a delicious way to kick off the meal. From there, piña preparada with slices of pineapple topped with a piloncillo salsa and dusted with cacao nibs and chile salt is incredibly simple yet highly memorable. Main dishes are largely inspired by the grill, while the fish of the day is wrapped in banana leaf served with hoja santa salsa verde and refried beans. Round out the meal with one of their desserts, perhaps the pastel de elote, a round moist corn cake topped with candied hazelnuts, blueberries, and a brown butter creme.

restaurant.Name: Estiatorio Milos
restaurant.Address: 730 1st St., Miami Beach, FL, 33139, USA
restaurant.Description: This "Greek God" has been a beacon of seafood excellence for the glamorous diners of South Beach since opening its doors in 2012. Some don’t even need a menu and prefer to order based on a guided tour to the back, where all manner of fish and crustaceans gleam on packed ice.With fresh seafood arriving multiple times a week, the kitchen tends to keep preparations simple. Sashimi of any type is a good first step, though we’re partial to the bigeye tuna with yuzu kosho and dill. Thin slices of fried zucchini and eggplant mounded around creamy tzatziki are also worth an order. Grilled whole fish baked in salt, and large lobsters round out the feast, though big spenders should inquire about deep-sea prawns for a pricey but precious seafood luxury.

restaurant.Name: Estiatorio Milos
restaurant.Address: The Venetian Las Vegas, 3355 S. Las Vegas Blvd., Las Vegas, NV, 89109, USA
restaurant.Description: With locations scattered across the globe, this Las Vegas iteration nestled inside The Venetian does the name proud. Expect refined yet unpretentious, contemporary Greek cuisine. One glance at the superb fresh fish on display will clue you in on what to order. An elegant, modern nautical flair defines the dining room, where shades of white, blue and light wood, with terracotta amphorae evoke Greece. The set menu offers excellent value at lunch, while both afternoons and evenings include a full à la carte menu ranging from openers like ceviche, tartare and crudos to grilled or fried fish from the display counter, as well as a selection of classic Greek dishes with a modern twist.

restaurant.Name: Ethel's Fancy
restaurant.Address: 550 Waverley St., Palo Alto, CA, 94301, USA
restaurant.Description: Honoring the shared name of his mother and grandmother, Chef/owner Scott Nishiyama has taken off his fine-dining toque to don more casual garb at this Palo Alto charmer, and thankfully he hasn't missed a stitch. Appropriately, the space has a rustic-meets-elegant vibe, mirrored in eclectic, down-to-earth Californian cuisine that showcases peak-season ingredients prepared with care and refinement. A small menu, geared towards sharing, exemplifies this creative ethos with dishes like a beautifully fried "katsu-style" cutlet of swordfish matched with spiced kumquats and tangy Dijonnaise. Intriguing desserts like a hojicha tapioca pudding topped with a rice cracker bark are hard to resist, and the friendly, professional service sweetens the pot even further.

restaurant.Name: Ettan
restaurant.Address: 518 Bryant St., Palo Alto, CA, 94301, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Srijith Gopinathan brings his impressive pedigree and unique brand of upscale Indian cooking to the south (Palo Alto). With local products at the heart of this carte, Ettan is a sure-fire hit. It's an airy, bi-level setting, with a ring of mezzanine seats on the upper deck. Wood-plank floors, indigo-dyed fabric, floral wallpaper, and a beaded chandelier decorate the skylit room.Kulchas are a menu highpoint, deliciously stuffed with the likes of peak-season peas and ricotta and served with a bright green kale chutney. Deep-fried cauliflower florets flecked with cracked black pepper and arranged with Asian pear deliver a delightful contrast of tastes; while crisped branzino with a chutney of green garlic, herbs, and chilies is all heart and soul.

restaurant.Name: Eulalie
restaurant.Address: 239 West Broadway, New York, NY, 10013, USA
restaurant.Description: New York loves a good throwback and Chef Chip Smith and wife/general manager Tina Vaughn have leaned into that vibe at Eulalie, where reservations are required and made exclusively by phone, the menu is handwritten, and guests are buzzed in at the door. If this all sounds a bit formal, it's not. It's very warm and welcoming. Chef Smith's four-course, French-leaning prix fixe may begin with a delicious opener of duck liver terrine dotted with green pistachio and peppercorns, followed by a savory tart with caramelized onions, Gruyère, and prosciutto. Golden-brown, crispy flounder atop a green tomato beurre blanc is a lovely main dish. Wine pairings, a cheese course, and dessert are also available—do get the coconut cake.

restaurant.Name: Evelyn's
restaurant.Address: Four Seasons Hotel and Residences Fort Lauderdale, 525 N. Fort Lauderdale Beach Blvd., Fort Lauderdale, FL, 33304, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: It may be tucked inside the Four Seasons Hotel Fort Lauderdale, but you're in for a different experience at Evelyn's. As might be expected given the location, the look is coastal chic with views extending over the pool and beyond to the Atlantic Ocean. Coastal Floridian influences find their way into dishes with a Levantine focus. Begin with their French onion labneh, a slightly sweet spread served with paper-thin, buckwheat lavash and house-made pita. Skewers, perhaps the pomegranate-glazed ora king salmon, are even better with a side of spiced basmati rice and lentils served with key lime tzatziki. Dessert is worth saving room for, with a large list of favorites including a pistachio mille-feuille that riffs on baklava with delicious results.

restaurant.Name: Ever Andalo
restaurant.Address: 3116 N. Davidson St., Charlotte, NC, 28205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Named for the mountain village in Italy where owner Jeff Tonidandel's family originally hails, this charming spot feels like it's been here for years (spoiler alert: it hasn't). Its warm manner and simple bistro style have the look and feel of a traditional family-owned trattoria down pat. The menu is not strictly Italian, as there are American leanings, too, but expect rustic preparations and high-quality ingredients. Order some oysters and fresh anchovies to start along with a pasta dish, or perhaps one of the daily specials. The wine list is exclusively Italian and is categorized by region of origin.

restaurant.Name: Evie Mae's BBQ
restaurant.Address: 11610 Emerald Coast Pkwy., Miramar Beach, FL, 32550, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Located in Miramar Beach, this spot's focus is on Texas-style barbecue. The sweet smell of smoke fills your nose as you approach the space, and once inside, step in line, order and wait for your cut-to-order meal to be called. Do not miss the green chili cheese sausage; a large link dotted with peppers and gooey pockets of cheese. Next, try the smoked turkey breast with a black pepper rub, both moist and flavorful. Notable sides include the baked potato casserole, a warm potato salad with sour cream and cheese elements and the sautéed green beans with bacon.

restaurant.Name: Evvia
restaurant.Address: 420 Emerson St., Palo Alto, CA, 94301, USA
restaurant.Description: Inviting with its rustic wood beams, hanging copper pots and roaring wood-burning fireplace, this central Palo Alto spot is a draw for Maserati-driving tech billionaires by day and couples in the evening. Dress to impress here, where the scene dictates high prices (though lunch features lighter dishes and more palatable pricing).Much of the menu emerges from the wood-fired grill, including smoky, tender artichoke and eggplant skewers drizzled in olive oil and paired with garlicky Greek yogurt. The rustic, impossibly moist lamb souvlaki is nicely contrasted by a refreshing tomato, cucumber and red onion salad. For dessert, pumpkin cheesecake is subtle, sweet and accented with syrup-poached chunks of pumpkin.

restaurant.Name: Evviva
restaurant.Address: 2600 Dauphine St., New Orleans, LA, 70117, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This lively hangout in Marigny is a constant hive of activity, anchored first and foremost by a serious bar that mixes and stirs finely crafted cocktails amid a glowing, amber-hued backdrop. The menu, meanwhile, is always on the move and reflects wide-ranging inspiration that often leans Italian. Start with a refreshing crudo or the signature anchovy bread before diving into heartier, bigger plates that are built for sharing. Consider duck confit or grilled gulf shrimp zapped with garlic and oregano. All the while, friendly servers roam a room full of handsome wood, quirky art and a crowd that keeps on coming.

restaurant.Name: Ezov
restaurant.Address: 2708 E. Cesar Chavez St., Austin, TX, 78702, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This family-style Mediterranean/Middle Eastern restaurant comes from the same group behind Emmer & Rye. Terrific for groups, it's the kind of place where you want to snack on a little bit of everything. First up, smashed cucumber marinated with amba and set atop luscious labneh is an ideal starter. Beef and lamb kebab on a bed of fire-roasted eggplant and charred onions is even better with dipping sauces like tahini with herbs, schug, and a spicy chili sauce. It's even better with a glass of wine from their keenly organized list. Meanwhile, baklava is a treat enough on its own, but here it's given an extra boost thanks to a scoop of tahini ice cream and brûléed banana.

restaurant.Name: Family Ethiopian
restaurant.Address: 1414 9th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
restaurant.Description: This bright and trendy sibling-owned spot is made with love—and it clearly shows. Enter to find a smattering of yellow metal chairs, walls vibrant with art and a kitchen teeming with a focused brigade—serious women chefs preparing complex Ethiopian fare, with nostalgia at the forefront.The family platter, with both vegetarian and meat dishes, is an excellent way to sample the variety. That beloved sour and spongy injera is ideal for sopping up the likes of gomen (collard greens with fresh garlic and onions) or kik alicha (a stew of yellow split peas with turmeric and ginger). Tikil gomen with cabbage and potatoes is an herbivore's dream; while quanta firfir, deliciously tender beef imbued with berbere and purified butter, has carnivores coming in droves.

restaurant.Name: Farmstead
restaurant.Address: 738 Main St., Saint Helena, CA, 94574, USA
restaurant.Description: For a down-home (but still Napa-chic) alternative to the Cal-Ital wine country grind, follow your nose to this Long Meadow Ranch-owned farmhouse, whose intoxicating smoker is parked right in the front yard. The cathedral ceiling, old-school country music and boisterous locals give Farmstead a lively air; for quieter dining, hit the front terrace. Naturally, the smoker-cooked meats like chicken wings, ribs and pulled pork are a major draw, but ranch-grown products utilized in simple, satisfying preparations, like a grilled artichoke with tangy sauce gribiche, are also a hit. Take the farm-fresh flavor with you — on weekends the restaurant's stands are brimming with produce, beef and honey for purchase.

restaurant.Name: Farra
restaurant.Address: 71 Worth St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
restaurant.Description: The word “Farra” has several meanings, all of which would be appropriate for this sleek retreat. Attractive, fun, and a bona fide party, Farra is a full-fledged restaurant that promises to garner a cultish following. Sharing the same wine cellar with next-door Atera, the team shows similar levels of hospitality, attention to detail, and creativity. Maybe you’ve had salmon tartare before, but was it mixed with potato chips for crunch and served with nori? Chicken schnitzel with seasonal accompaniments is classic comfort, and while we've all had ravioli, what about the crown-shaped corona ripiena? Stuffed with lobster, ricotta, and set in a dashi broth, this course is in a league of its own.

restaurant.Name: Fasano Restaurant
restaurant.Address: 60 E. 49th St., New York, NY, 10017, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
restaurant.Description: With its restaurants and hotels worldwide, the São Paulo-based Fasano hospitality group will be familiar to discerning travelers; and the setting will be familiar to savvy diners as the short-lived home of the relocated Four Seasons. However, New York's own Fasano restaurant looks poised for longevity offering a dose of sophistication to Midtown's dining scene. The spacious, elegantly arranged dining room looks luxe and feels soothing. The menu honors the gastronomic legacy of northern Italy and offers a range of highly enjoyable preparations. Excellent pasta, like the cappellacci di granseola with its squid ink-tinted pockets stuffed with King crab and saffron-spiked "fumetto," is offered along with Milanese di vitello and ossobuco.

restaurant.Name: Fat Beet Farm Kitchen and Bakery
restaurant.Address: 13830 W. Hillsborough Ave., Tampa, FL, 33635, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Founded by husband-and-wife duo Jen and Tim Curci in 2013, what began as a farm outside of Tampa has morphed into so much more. Focusing on sustainable initiatives, their kitchen and storefront offer an all-day dining menu, utilizing local products while showcasing house-made bakery items. Community events, including tours and yoga on site are posted on a calendar inside which doubles as a meeting place for all things delicious. Order the biscuits with honey, whipped butter and jam, or any one of their flavorful soups or sandwiches, like the turkey Reuben. On any given day you'll find their mac & cheese, including the decadent green hog version with pulled pork, green chilis and lots of gooey cheddar.

restaurant.Name: Fausto
restaurant.Address: 348 Flatbush Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11238, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: This sleek and upscale restaurant serves consistently delicious Italian-influenced food courtesy of Chef/owner Erin Shambura, but its overall ethos is guided by restaurateur (and sommelier), Joe Campanale. The dimly lit space and open hearth lend a warmth to the space that is perfect for date night or an evening out with friends. Meanwhile, the kitchen showcases a distinctive take on Southern regional fare. Pasta is a showstopper, as in tagliatelle with lamb ragu and saffron. Snack on a bowl of roasted and raw cauliflower with Romanesco and an anchovy caper vinaigrette, then forge ahead with main dishes like steelhead trout and roasted chicken. Braised pork shank atop Tuscan beans is a rich and savory dish that melts in your mouth. To finish, gelato or sorbet are the ideal conclusion to a hearty meal.

restaurant.Name: Fawn
restaurant.Address: 937 Cooper St., Memphis, TN, 38104, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This handsome restaurant in the heart of Cooper-Young is the place to be. Tile floors, handsome wood tables, mustard-yellow banquettes and sleek lighting make for a sharp dining room that’s bathed in light thanks to large, street-facing windows. The tight menu trades in familiar dishes calibrated with global touches. Past highlights include fried artichokes with harissa labneh; duck confit with braised greens; rabbit agnolotti with pickled pears and sour cherries; and French onion tartine with oyster mushrooms and thyme aioli. This is cooking with easy appeal and bold, balanced flavors.

restaurant.Name: Fawn Wine & Amaro Bar
restaurant.Address: 119 E. Ponce De Leon Ave., Decatur, GA, 30030, USA
restaurant.Description: There are two ways to experience Decatur's Fawn. Those who want to stop in for a bite and a drink will discover an interesting amaro selection and wine list alongside a seafood-focused à la carte that tempts with everything from fritto misto and crudos to dry-aged fish. However, the tasting menu is where this place really shines. Creative, unexpected and often bold, this is where the kitchen does its best work. House-made spaghettini with a hazelnut miso and uni is finished with caviar, shaved cured egg yolk and summer truffle for a spectacular dish, while hiramasa is dry-aged for 14 days and cured for 24 hours in miso for a flavor-packed punch. A nostalgic send-off riffs on a classic float with cherry sorbet and house-made kombucha.

restaurant.Name: Fearing's Restaurant
restaurant.Address: The Ritz-Carlton Dallas, 2121 McKinney Ave., Dallas, TX, 75201, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: Nestled inside the luxe Ritz-Carlton, Fearing's is elegant and dramatic. The handsome look may read traditional steakhouse but this flagship restaurant from Chef Dean Fearing isn't straightforward. Instead, the American menu with clear Southwestern influences is both complex and composed with buffalo and antelope along with classic-leaning filets. The dishes are surprising, offering bold flavors and new takes on the tried-and-true. Case in point? Their Lone Star mosaic, Fearing's take on carpaccio with tuna, wagyu beef, salmon, and barbecued eel composing a vivid plate resembling stained glass. Baklava S'more riffs on the campsite classic with puff pastry piped with milk chocolate pot de creme, pistachio marshmallow, and burnt rosemary ice cream for a refined finale.

restaurant.Name: Felicia Suzanne's
restaurant.Address: 383 S. Main St., Memphis, TN, 38103, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Scarlet-red banquettes, a long marble bar and checkered tile cut a striking, seductive figure in downtown Memphis. This is a restaurant whose identity is never in question thanks to veteran Chef Felicia Suzanne, now situated in a swanky new dining room where she sources quality ingredients and honors Southern traditions with class and elegance. Plucky Gulf shrimp set with tasso ham sauce and jalapeño cornbread is a superb signature and a reflection of this kitchen at its very best. Other hits on this finely curated menu include buttermilk fried quail with greens and spiced honey as well as fried green tomatoes with Creole remoulade.

restaurant.Name: Feliciana Bistrôt and Bar
restaurant.Address: 405 E. Gibson St., Covington, LA, 70433, USA
restaurant.Description: Across the bridge over Lake Pontchartrain, Chef John Besh delivers with this refined French bistro in the city of Covington. The historic space was previously a theater. Now, sunlight floods the beautiful corner dining room fit with a large, curved bar, globe lights, handsome tile floors and gold touches throughout. The menu is classic in aim and elegant in execution: Oysters on the half shell, buttery escargot, blue crab beignets and gnocchi with crawfish. For dessert, aim for the warm apple tarte tatin with vanilla ice cream. Afterwards, continue the adventure upstairs where you’ll find a rooftop bar and patio.

restaurant.Name: Fia
restaurant.Address: 2454 Wilshire Blvd., Santa Monica, CA, 90403, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: A Santa Monica landmark dating back to the 20s, the onetime Wilshire has been reimagined with an Italian streak. It’s hard to imagine a more exquisitely Angeleno locale than this sprawling courtyard, encased by massive pine trees and illuminated by twinkling string lights. Fia's menu features organic produce from local farmers from no further than 50 miles away, and though it appears routine on the surface, it's full of inventive twists, as seen in the spicy tuna on crispy arancini, or the porcini tortellini with asparagus, spinach and pearl onion. Save room for the Amalfi lemon mousse cake with Limoncello granita and meringue.

restaurant.Name: Fia Steak
restaurant.Address: 2458 Wilshire Blvd., Santa Monica, CA, 90403, USA
restaurant.Description: Fia Steak remains the sort of place designed for dressing up and leaning fully into indulgence. The dining room still embraces the classic steakhouse playbook, from dramatic dry-aged cuts on display to plush interiors and a menu layered with luxury touches like caviar, Champagne and Japanese wagyu. Seafood-driven starters continue to open the meal, including hamachi crudo with lime leaf and coconut dressing or spicy ahi tuna cigars topped with caviar and black garlic aioli. Steaks remain the centerpiece, from prime ribeye cap and filet mignon to an elaborate beef Wellington, while house-made pastas and rich sides like dauphinoise potatoes and miso bagna cauda broccolini round out the experience. Desserts keep the decadence going with options like sticky toffee pudding with brown butter ice cream or a towering chocolate soufflé finished with Grand Marnier anglaise.

restaurant.Name: Fig
restaurant.Address: 232 Meeting St., Charleston, SC, 29401, USA
restaurant.Description: This Charleston favorite has been at it for more than two decades, but judging by the demand, you’d think they had just opened. Reservations are a hot ticket, and crowds hoping to grab a walk-in seat line up before the front door opens. Despite its age, the food feels anything but dated. This is a kitchen that knows itself, its position in the South and its place in the Lowcountry. Seafood is a strength, and the slow-baked red snapper is a good example of this; here plated with a classic sauce Américaine and wilted heirloom spinach. The chicken liver pâté is accompanied by turnip remoulade and pickled beets. End on a sweet note, say the Carolina Gold rice pudding with Johns Island strawberries.

restaurant.Name: Fiola Mare
restaurant.Address: 3050 K St. NW, Ste. 101, Washington, DC, 20007, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: Perched along the Potomac River, Chef Fabio Trabocchi's salute to seafood enjoys privileged views that never get old. With more than a decade of history behind it, this nautical dining room is built for crowds with private rooms and expansive patio space to boot. Still, the well-oiled kitchen keeps a firm grasp on its strengths, preparing high-quality seafood and pasta with care and class. Vibrant salads, zippy crudos and expertly grilled fish delight, alongside the signature lobster ravioli, a rich triumph that will never leave the menu. Such pleasures and views are not without expense, but rest assured there is substance to all this style.

restaurant.Name: Firstborn
restaurant.Address: 978 N. Broadway, Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef/owner Anthony Wang, a first-generation American at the name suggests, weaves in his own interpretations and influences at this Chinese American restaurant in Mandarin Plaza. The dining room is welcoming and comfortable, offering a view into the well-organized kitchen turning out dishes that are intended for sharing. Begin with a cocktail from their enticing lineup before tucking into dishes like tender tofu dumplings with sautéed shiitake mushrooms or duck sausage. While their main dishes rotate, if the aged duck breast with persimmon and parsnip is available, order it. Round out your meal with a slice of vanilla sponge cake with red bean, oolong and berry sauce.

restaurant.Name: Fish Shop
restaurant.Address: 610 Water St. SW, Washington, DC, 20024, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: If the name isn't a clear sign and the location facing the waterfront doesn't give it away, one look at the sophisticated nautical decor will set you straight. The large space includes a semi-open kitchen but the patio with marina views is the place to be on warm days.The menu echoes their sister spot in Scotland with a clear focus on fish, though here it's given a Mid-Atlantic update. The Maryland crab crumpet perfectly illustrates that across-the-pond connection and is a perfect opener. The fish is sourced from the Chesapeake region and from a D.C. farming operation, and the menu presents plenty of interesting items, like sugar toads, or northern puffer fish, served whole and crispy fried. Order the Virginia peanut tiramisu for a twist on a classic.

restaurant.Name: Fishing with Dynamite
restaurant.Address: 1148 Manhattan Ave., Manhattan Beach, CA, 90266, USA
restaurant.Description: This tight and warm seafood spot is located just down the block from the ocean. Inside, it has a decidedly beachy vibe, flooded with sunlight and colors that make it feel cozy even when it's loud and busy. Raw bar dishes comprise half the menu, and if the list of first-class oysters, clams, and lobsters seems overwhelming, the friendly staff will help make sense of it all. Dishes such as wild New Caledonian prawns with garlic butter and fragrant lemon jasmine rice or seared diver scallops with Japanese curry sweet potato coulis are indicative of the delicious, decidedly uncomplicated cooking available here.

restaurant.Name: Flea St. Cafe
restaurant.Address: 3607 Alameda de las Pulgas, Menlo Park, CA, 94025, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This longtime café has been welcoming diners since 1980 and still feels comfortably like dining in someone’s home, with small rooms spread throughout the house and walls lined with eclectic artwork. A cozy front bar and relaxed atmosphere add to the intimate charm. The kitchen continues to focus on California’s farm-to-table ethos, building a seasonal menu around produce sourced from nearby farms and the coast. Dishes highlight fresh vegetables, simple preparations and familiar comforts, from fritto misto of market vegetables to creamy risottos and classic desserts. The approach is straightforward and ingredient-driven, emphasizing freshness above all.

restaurant.Name: Florence Supper Club
restaurant.Address: 375 S. Pearl St., Denver, CO, 80209, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This nostalgic, dimly lit throwback hits all the right notes. Wrapped in dark wood, roomy booths and red-and-white checkered tablecloth, this Italian-American restaurant delivers a tightly crafted menu that covers the classics with style and heart.
