Where to begin? Clams casino, a towering Caesar salad or a righteous, fork-tender meatball? Pastas like spicy rigatoni alla vodka or linguine vongole are made-in house. Rich and bold flavors extend to entrees like chicken Parmesan or veal marsala. The food is far from light and diners should bring friends with appetites at the ready. Reservations can be scarce; walk-ins may have better luck at the bar.

restaurant.Name: Flour + Water
restaurant.Address: 2401 Harrison St., San Francisco, CA, 94110, USA
restaurant.Description: As the name implies, two ingredients create a world of possibilities at this always-packed Mission stalwart. Affable service, plus a space that’s both buzzy and approachable, partly explain the evergreen appeal of this humble space, but it’s really the kitchen’s vibrant blend of Californian and Italian cuisines that draws the crowds. An ever-changing array of expertly handmade pastas is the main event, with creative offerings like chitarra spaghetti made with sea lettuce, paired with manila clams, guanciale and crunchy pangrattato, or ginger-infused caramelle filled with creamy koginut squash, sauced with sage brown butter. The option of half portions helps to ease the difficulty of choosing only one, but for those seeking even more variety, a multicourse pasta tasting is a real treat.

restaurant.Name: Focaccia Sandwich + Bakery
restaurant.Address: 2300 Bee Ridge Rd., Unit 207, Sarasota, FL, 34239, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: The team rises before the crack of dawn every day to fire up the ovens and make trays of gorgeous, fluffy rounds of focaccia. From buffalo chicken with green goddess to prime rib with smoked horseradish cream, this bread serves as the base for satisfying, hulking sandwiches that are finely constructed and come in half portions for those with more petite appetites. The simple operation has a few outdoor tables along with counter seats at the edge of the kitchen, which also turns out fine soups and salads.

restaurant.Name: Folk
restaurant.Address: 823 Meridian St., Nashville, TN, 37207, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This East Nashville restaurant from Chef/owner Philip Krajeck is the more casual sibling of Rolf & Daughters. Warm wood paneled walls and plenty of light lend an inviting ambience to this dining room. Chef Krajeck's contemporary menu is driven by local, seasonal produce. Items shift often but you'll always discover simple-but-satisfying plates with items like stracciatella dressed with olive oil and topped with fresh peaches or main dishes like bluefin tartare or chicken Milanese. Naturally leavened pizzas topped seasonally minded items (perhaps a summery treat of fresh sweet corn) are always a good bet. Then, round it all out with something sweet like focaccia ice cream set with rhubarb jam and whey caramel.

restaurant.Name: Fond
restaurant.Address: 1601 Elm St., Ste. 110, Dallas, TX, 75201, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Located across from Thanksgiving Square in Downtown Dallas, Fond is the restaurant from Chefs Jennie Kelley and Brandon Moore, two longtime fixtures of the city’s dining scene. By day, the space functions as a cafe serving sandwiches, salads and Detroit-style pizzas; by night, the menu expands to include small plates and seasonal entrees alongside a thoughtfully curated wine selection. The cooking blends comfort and creativity, drawing on a variety of influences while remaining approachable. Familiar dishes are often elevated through house-made components, careful technique and unexpected combinations, resulting in food that feels both contemporary and satisfying. A daily soft serve, always finished with olive oil and Maldon salt, has become a signature.

restaurant.Name: Food Terminal
restaurant.Address: 5000 Buford Hwy., Atlanta, GA, 30341, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef/owner Amy Wong's Food Terminal may have multiple locations, but the Buford Highway original will always stand out from the rest. Located within a cavernous space that sports a contemporary feel (think exposed ducts, charcoal-gray walls and metal chairs), it's designed to resemble a night market. As for the food, it's Malaysian at its core. The massive menu is matched only by the portions, perfect for enjoying family style. It's a celebration of the cultural mash-up that is Malaysia with dishes like garlic noodles, made in house and tossed in a garlic sauce with spinach and mushrooms. It's so good it's nearly impossible to put your chopsticks down. Fried curry chicken nasi lemak features their take on the classic dish.

restaurant.Name: Forsythia
restaurant.Address: 233 Chestnut St., Philadelphia, PA, 19106, USA
restaurant.Description: This restaurant is temporarily closed.For an unabashed, full-steam-ahead celebration of French cooking, look to Chef Christopher Kearse at this relaxed, modern bistro. Cute tile flooring, globe lights and simple tables set the stage for tempura frog legs with saffron aioli, escargot with Pernod-almond butter and yellow corn vichyssoise with crab. Some opt for a seat at the bar in the front for snacks and a drink or two. Open since 2019, the dining room further in offers clear views of the open kitchen, which shows a fine hand with the likes of dry-aged duck and halibut poached in olive oil. To finish, think chocolate mousse or peach and apricot mille-feuille.

restaurant.Name: Forsythia
restaurant.Address: 9 Stanton St., New York, NY, 10002, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
restaurant.Description: Open since 2020, this intimate, Lower East Side nook is all about pasta. Set menus begin with warm, pillow-like slices of fresh-baked focaccia. Take a look around – just about everyone is after the longstanding fried cacio pepe risotto suppli made with buffalo mozzarella and pecorino. Seasonal preparations can be as satisfying as they are generously portioned, and past highlights include grilled octopus with jimmy nardello peppers. The main event is, of course, the pasta. Agnolotti packed with short rib and tossed in butter has few equals, and the carbonara never disappoints. The restaurant also offers cooking classes during the week for those looking to up their game at home.

restaurant.Name: Fort Oak
restaurant.Address: 1011 Fort Stockton Dr., San Diego, CA, 92103, USA
restaurant.Description: Named for the majestic oaks of nearby Presidio Park, this Mission Hills eatery helmed by Chef Brad Wise is perfect for happy hour or an intimate "chef's experience" tasting. Just don't let the fire fool you—Fort Oak is no log cabin. This historic, former car dealership is bright and airy, complete with a glamorous horseshoe-shaped bar and sleek, mid-century vibe. Chef Wise's menu is one intended for sharing. Try a bit of everything, from raw seafood appetizers or towers to hot appetizers like their cinnamon heavy lamb merguez kefta with a pistachio muhammara. Heritage pork chop with roasted Brussels sprouts and potatoes shows off the kitchen's flair for the flame, while desserts like apple crisp served hot in an iron skillet are the epitome of comfort.

restaurant.Name: Fortu
restaurant.Address: The Ponce De Leon Hotel, 97 Central Ave., St. Petersburg, FL, 33701, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This attractive, high-energy dining room in downtown St Petersburg is cool in all the right ways. Handsome wood finishes, sleek lighting, and large arched mirrors cut a sharp figure at the base of the Ponce de Leon Hotel. Most importantly, this Pan-Asian kitchen backs up all this style with proper substance. Skip the raw bar in favor of plump, spicy pork wontons showered with crispy garlic and chili crisp. Glazed carrots in kimchi butter are both satisfying and sophisticated. And though the restaurant isn’t technically a steakhouse, this might be the best place around to splurge on beef. Beautifully marbled cuts of Japanese A5 wagyu are seared and seasoned to exacting measure. Desserts, like walnut and apple torte, make for a sweet finale.

restaurant.Name: Found Oyster
restaurant.Address: 4880 Fountain Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90029, USA
restaurant.Description: There is no ocean in sight from this busy corner of East Hollywood, and yet, this no-frills bar trades in impeccably sourced and prepared seafood. Opened in 2019, the cozy restaurant is minimally decorated and has kept a full house since the very beginning. From sea urchin to razor clams to freshly harvested scallops from Maine, this team knows that such treasures need little more than a drizzle of olive oil or squeeze of lemon to sing. Lobster rolls, tostadas, trout dip — the temptations are endless, down to the oysters sourced from the general manager’s family oyster farm.

restaurant.Name: Four Flamingos, A Richard Blais Florida Kitchen
restaurant.Address: Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress Resort, 1 Grand Cypress Blvd., Orlando, FL, 32836, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
restaurant.Description: This exciting concept from Chef Richard Blais is nestled in the Hyatt Regency Grand Cypress property. Follow the footpath that leads over a bridge and towards the bright pink entrance, fronted by a waterfall. This retreat radiates a calming, coastal vibe with design details like plentiful windows, warm wood and pops of color. Fittingly, the menu is contemporary Americana meets the tropics. The chef's focus is on seasonal, bold and creative flavors, as in savory-sweet smoked salmon croquetas with sweet plantain and red pepper relish in an Old Bay aioli. Big eaters know to save room for mains like swordfish, grouper and deliciously spiced mojo chicken.Couples rejoice, as this is a perfect place to splurge, celebrate and eat to your heart's content.

restaurant.Name: Four Kings
restaurant.Address: 710 Commercial St., San Francisco, CA, 94108, USA
restaurant.Description: Restaurants don’t get much buzzier than this bustling Chinatown haunt, where Chefs Franky Ho and Michael Long are drawing crowds eager to sample their breezy contemporary take on Cantonese cuisine. Reservations evaporate almost immediately, but determined diners can line up for counter seating before doors open—though there’s no guarantee of getting in. Once inside, the favored few will find themselves packed into a lively room with quirky décor, where food takes center stage. From claypot rice with bacon and Chinese sausage to savory “fish fragrant” eggplant, the cooking taps into traditional flavors while offering a fresh perspective, a formula that seems to have struck gold.

restaurant.Name: Four Twenty Five
restaurant.Address: 425 Park Ave., New York, NY, 10022, USA
restaurant.Description: Jonathan Benno and Jean-Georges Vongerichten are behind this elegant restaurant named for the address of the sleek building it occupies. Flooded with natural light, the soaring dining room is striking yet understated, offering a polished Midtown setting. The menu pulls influences from France, Italy, and Asia, pairing classical technique with contemporary flavors. Delicate kampachi with aji amarillo, lime and crushed corn nuts highlights the kitchen’s restrained touch, while beautifully handmade rabbit agnolotti showcases refined pasta-making. Main courses such as steamed black bass in a fragrant mushroom broth demonstrate careful technique, and desserts balance familiar flavors with modern presentation.

restaurant.Name: Four by Brother Luck
restaurant.Address: 321 N. Tejon St., Colorado Springs, CO, 80903, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Brother Luck is the memorable name of this appealingly quirky establishment’s chef and proprietor, and the “four” refers to the number of courses offered in its prix fixe menu. The creative modern Southwestern cuisine presents an alluring variety of dishes to choose from, boasting a panoply of proteins and produce. You might begin with the likes of a rabbit empanada cleverly paired with pea and carrot relish with habanero hot sauce, then proceed to a dish of green chile and duck confit, before landing on a Colorado lamb chop with artichoke soubise and tamarind demi-glace. A blue corn tres leches cake with smoky agave crème anglaise and blueberry ice cream is similarly intriguing. Folksy service and an inventive cocktail selection make everything fit together.

restaurant.Name: Frances
restaurant.Address: 3870 17th St., San Francisco, CA, 94114, USA
restaurant.Description: Stylish and always packed, this disarmingly personal restaurant from Chef/owner Melissa Perello remains a neighborhood favorite. It’s as perfect for a low-key date night as it is for dinner with the kids, and while reservations are difficult to score, its cozy setting and gracious staff justify planning ahead.The ultra-seasonal tasting menu, served family style, combines fantastic Californian produce with a Mediterranean bent, eschewing trendy powders and foams for appealingly rustic fare like Charentais melon with coriander capers and dill pollen. House-made pastas, like a lumache with wagyu ragu, pecorino romano and Sicilian chili flake, are eminently satisfying. The meal ends with a homey dessert like roasted strawberry shortcake, finished with a cloud of mascarpone Chantilly.

restaurant.Name: Friends Only
restaurant.Address: 1501 California St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
restaurant.Description: Although reservations are now open to the public, an air of exclusivity still pervades this hot-ticket counter, not least of all because of the Olympian price point. What that pretty penny buys, however, is one of the most engaging and indulgent omakase experiences in town, replete with enough luxury to sate even the most committed of sybarites. Sip on delightfully unique cocktails with the likes of black truffle amaro or sesame orgeat and enjoy a parade of bites highlighting seafood of impeccable quality, much of it painstakingly dry-aged in house. Traditional nigiri and sashimi are served alongside cooked dishes, as in cherrywood-smoked unagi brightened with the prickle of sansho pepper, or bouillabaisse reimagined with dry-aged fish bone broth.

restaurant.Name: Fry Bread House
restaurant.Address: 4545 N. 7th Ave., Phoenix, AZ, 85013, USA
restaurant.Description: North of downtown in Phoenix's Melrose neighborhood, this spot from Cecelia Miller of the Tohono O'odham Nation specializes in fry bread, a Native American dish of fried dough that's crispy on the outside and tender and fluffy in the middle. You'll need just one bite to see why this spot draws large crowds every day of the week. Fry bread topped with refried beans, green chilis, sour cream and cheese is simple, but it's a messy delight. Red chili beef stew, thick and hearty, is even better with a fry bread on the side. The signature item even appears at dessert, dusted with cinnamon sugar and worth every last bite.

restaurant.Name: Funke
restaurant.Address: 9388 S. Santa Monica Blvd., Beverly Hills, CA, 90210, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Evan Funke, who also runs Felix and Mother Wolf, is at it again with this eponymous restaurant. Set in a three-story 1930s art deco building, it's a stunning tribute to Italian cooking, with handmade pasta taking center stage (there's even a glassed-in room to watch them at work). Tall ceilings, red leather booths, and stone tables with brown leather/suede chairs set a stunning tone for a menu that pulls from their sister restaurants while remaining true to itself. Start with their pillowy focaccia, then savor a plate of tender South Pacific blue prawns in a garlicky salsa verde. Handmade agnolotti is delightful with a creamy filling of taleggio fonduta, finished with a meaty, buttery sugo di arrosto and parmigiano reggiano. Finally, torta di cioccolato is a wonderful finish.

restaurant.Name: GG's Chicken Shop
restaurant.Address: 3325 N. Southport Ave., Chicago, IL, 60657, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Bright and contemporary, this utterly charming spot from Chef Lee Wolen is named for his mother. It's casual, an order-at-the-counter-style spot, and as the name suggests, it's all about chicken. Rotisserie chicken is available by the quarter, half or whole, along with chicken sandwiches (fried and rotisserie) and sides like creamy broccoli slaw with golden raisins and crunchy almonds or chicken drippings smashed potatoes that will have you hoarding your portion. The comforting menu is rounded out with a few nostalgia-inducing desserts including oatmeal cream pies and a dirt cup topped with gummy worms that makes you feel like a kid again.Despite the downhome digs, the kind and caring staff are incredibly professional, elevating an already enjoyable experience.

restaurant.Name: Gage & Tollner
restaurant.Address: 372 Fulton St., Brooklyn, NY, 11201, USA
restaurant.Description: Vintage mirrors, cherry wood and brass chandeliers line the length of this historic restaurant, which first opened in 1892. With an amber glow and buzzing crowd, the room immediately charms, down to the no-nonsense all-classic cocktail list. There is plenty to eat here, as the team is not content to merely let history and looks stand in for substance. Seafood towers, big steaks, crab cakes and a superb platter of fried chicken with cornmeal fritters take their cues from the legendary Edna Lewis, who ran the kitchen in the late 80s and whose Southern cooking has inspired countless followers. Dessert is essential and all of them, from the coconut layer cake to the baked Alaska, will make for a fond farewell.

restaurant.Name: Gaijin
restaurant.Address: 950 W. Lake St., Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Gaijin is Paul Virant's love letter to okonomiyaki. Okonomi in Japanese means "what you like” and accordingly guests here are encouraged to choose their own course. Thanks to his time in Japan, the chef displays ace skills and experience. Osaka and Hiroshima are the main styles on his menu, which also flaunts a custom brew from Moody Tongue. While Tuesdays bring a tonkatsu feast, steamed rice with furikake, miso soup, and tsukemono are eternal hits. Desserts, like shirokuma with pineapple-buttermilk sherbet and coconut syrup, are worth the splurge.The room resembles a veritable izakaya, with an okonomiyaki griddle dominating the space—and conversation. Brass accents, exposed brick, and concrete floors add a dash of rusticity to this otherwise premium den.

restaurant.Name: Galatoire’s
restaurant.Address: 209 Bourbon St., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: At one of the city's oldest institutions, Friday lunch is a revelrous rite of passage. Pearls and suits file in right as doors open to a gold-accented dining room encased in mirrors and watched over by tuxedoes. Everyone is celebrating something and has the balloons, Champagne, and party hats to prove it. For more than a century, French-Creole classics have run up and down the menu. Go heavy on appetizers, like the Oysters Rockefeller, crabmeat maison with shrimp remoulade, or those superb, puffy soufflé potatoes dipped in a rich béarnaise. For entrees, find more seafood topped with all manner of crab, cream, and butter. There is nothing light, quick, or quiet about this meal. This is about leisure. Take your time. There’s nowhere else you need to be.

restaurant.Name: Gallaghers
restaurant.Address: 228 W. 52nd St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Gallaghers is an icon. Walls covered with photos of horses and jockeys harken back to the seasoned stallion’s former proximity to the old Madison Square Garden. From the rolling carts of steaks and desserts to a bar scene that feels as alive as ever, this place hums with energy. The menu’s “other soup” is a sly reference held over from Prohibition days; and diners still walk past the window-fronted meat locker where slabs of USDA Prime beef are dry-aged.Gallagher’s fresh sparkle is exhibited by the display kitchen, set behind glass panes. The kitchen turns out classic dishes – steaks over hickory logs, creamed spinach and other faithful sides that are executed with care. The rib steak is a bone-in ribeye that arrives mouthwateringly tender with a side of warm and savory house sauce.

restaurant.Name: Garcia's Mexican Food
restaurant.Address: 842 Fredericksburg Rd., San Antonio, TX, 78201, USA
restaurant.Description: Open since 1962, this venerable institution from the Garcia family remains a vibrant, proud part of the city’s dining fabric. At all hours, the squat building has people waiting outside waiting for a table and ready to dig into classic Tex-Mex cooking. The menu is expansive, and one could spend weeks trying to cover it. There are those who come to order eggs over easy, douse them in salsa, and scoop them up in warm flour tortillas. And then there are heartier appetites who launch right into the deluxe dinner, which features enchiladas, a tamale, chili con carne, and a hard-shell taco. Should you also tack on a brisket taco? Of course you should. Adding to the convivial charm of the diner setting is a staff that’s all smiles.

restaurant.Name: Gary Danko
restaurant.Address: 800 North Point St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
restaurant.Description: Opened in 1999, Chef Gary Danko's eponymous dining room is a San Francisco institution. Located in Fisherman's Wharf, the restaurant continues to be a busy beacon for colleagues on business dinners and celebratory couples. The cooking is rooted in classic French cuisine with a wandering sense of global inspiration. Diners select from a prix-fixe with ample options in each category of appetizer, seafood, meat and dessert. Those who aren’t in the mood to decide can hand over the reins with the five-course chef’s tasting menu. An extensive wine list, servers dressed in dark suits, and an impressively large cheese trolley round out the vintage experience.

restaurant.Name: Genesis House Restaurant
restaurant.Address: 40A Tenth Ave., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Housed in a glass and steel structure adjacent to the High Line and across from Little Island park, Genesis House is a cool and modern respite from the surrounding cacophony. The ground floor is a gallery of the brand's luxury cars, while the second floor is a stunning, expansive dining room delivering skyline views and modern Korean fare. Think curls of amberjack crudo in a kimchi and asparagus brine or a 36-hour beef bone broth that’s boldly seasoned with pepper. Desserts like pear sorbet with tapioca pearls, cinnamon and ginger make for a captivating ending. Beverages include a thorough wine list and premium teas from Korea.

restaurant.Name: Georgia Boy
restaurant.Address: 1043 Ponce de Leon Ave. NE, Atlanta, GA, 30306, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: You don't just walk in off the street to Georgia Boy. First, it's secreted away within Southern Belle. Then, if you're one of the diners with reservations, you'll be seated in the "library" for drinks, snacks and a hint of what's to come. Find the chef's favorite book on the shelf and voila!, a secret door opens, revealing an open kitchen. Chef Joey Ward enjoys teasing diners, and while some courses are highly experimental, others are interesting and fun. Milk and cereal is a perfect example of his creative styling, with seared snapper presented alongside a box of cereal containing puffed rice and a tableside pour of hot coconut milk broth.

restaurant.Name: Girl & the Goat Los Angeles
restaurant.Address: 555-3 Mateo St., Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Girl & the Goat, Chef Stephanie Izard’s West Coast offshoot of her wildly popular Chicago original, has settled comfortably into downtown LA’s Arts District amid Spotify’s sprawling podcast campus. The space remains unmistakably boho chic, filled with natural light, linen-toned textures and plenty of greenery, while the perpetually buzzing crowd keeps the energy high from lunch through dinner. Diners come for the chef’s signature style of globally influenced, boldly flavored small plates, ranging from chickpea fritters with goat yogurt, tamarind and herb chutney to wood-fired broccoli topped with shrimp crunch and blue cheese labneh. Larger dishes like goat curry with masa chips and pickled vegetables or grilled kalbi-style short ribs with stone fruit and perilla vinaigrette continue the eclectic theme. Desserts remain just as playful, especially the mango sticky rice with tamarind sorbet, coconut cloud and watermelon granita.

restaurant.Name: Giulia
restaurant.Address: 1682 Massachusetts Ave., Cambridge, MA, 02138, USA
restaurant.Description: It’s all about the pasta here at Giulia, sister restaurant to Moëca around the corner. There are usually around nine varieties on offer; you can go for lighter choices like fresh-tasting fusilli with tomato and zucchini or plump for the smooth ribbons of pappardelle with succulent braised wild boar and pair it with a red from the all-Italian wine list. Start by sharing some burrata or caponata and you’ll leave feeling fully satisfied. The atmosphere is great and it’s always very busy – although the team copes effortlessly with the numbers. If you haven’t booked, try your luck with the counter seats at the bar that stretch down one side of the room – they’re kept aside for walk-ins.

restaurant.Name: Gjelina
restaurant.Address: 1429 Abbot Kinney Blvd., Venice, CA, 90291, USA
restaurant.Description: In more than a decade, this buzzy restaurant has spawned a to-go counter, highly popular bakery and cookbook. The ambience is ceaselessly upbeat, resulting in a scene that is a major draw among pretty young things.Brick floors and creeping vines fashion a picturesque, garden-like setting that is an idyllic match for their simply prepared Mediterranean menu of pizzas and shared plates like saffron spaghetti with bottarga, confit tomato, and garlic or grilled hanger steak with a rhubarb chimichurri. Vegetables, many sourced locally, are an absolute must with winning options like Japanese sweet potato with jalapeno yogurt and scallion, or the umami-rich grilled oyster mushroom with tarragon butter.

restaurant.Name: Glai Baan
restaurant.Address: 2333 E. Osborn Rd., Phoenix, AZ, 85016, USA
restaurant.Description: Set within a converted bungalow, this spot from Pornsupak "Cat" Bunnag and Dan Robinson translates to "far from home," and the space does feel like you’re in your own world, with its door covered in vines and greenery and dark, moody interior. As for the food? It's Thai street food designed for sharing. Spicy, sweet and savory comingle in dishes like Japanese eggplant salad topped with minced pork and steamed shrimp or skewers of local pork shoulder in soy coconut milk, garlic marinade and a bold-but-classic jaew dipping sauce. Don't skip the kao soi, a vibrant curry-laced Thai broth studded with tender chicken, egg noodles, pickled mustard greens and fried crispy noodles. For dessert, it's mango sticky rice for the win.

restaurant.Name: Glin Thai Bistro
restaurant.Address: 330 Myrtle Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This charming spot just steps from Fort Greene Park has an inviting tropical ambience and an even more enticing menu. Showcasing dishes from northern and southern Thailand, Glin Thai Bistro is the real deal, with unique offerings using high quality ingredients, all with a distinctively Thai look and feel. Begin with an order of gui chai, or crispy, golden-fried chive pancakes that balance sweet and savory. Fried rice studded with crabmeat, egg, and vegetables is ramped up with cilantro chili lime sauce and chili fish sauce, while the kra pow nuer, or 24-hour braised short ribs, will linger in your memory for their caramelized crust and fork-tender meat.

restaurant.Name: Golden Hour
restaurant.Address: The Radical Asheville, Tapestry Collection by Hilton, 95 Roberts St., Asheville, NC, 28801, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Located at the Radical hotel in Asheville's River Arts District, this red brick structure was originally built in 1923 and was previously a breakfast cereal factory. The space is done up in dark painted exposed brick walls decorated with murals, large windows with views of the French Broad river, tall ceilings, exposed air ducts and an open kitchen.Wood-fired is the dominant feature of this kitchen. Small plates include smoked fish dip accompanied by crunchy seasonal vegetables and house-made matzo; North Carolina crab beignets with Old Bay-seasoned powdered sugar for dusting, or a "Girl's Dinner" board of cheeses, local meats and pickles. A wood-grilled half chicken or slow-roasted lamb with pita are tempting and comforting large plates.

restaurant.Name: Good Alley
restaurant.Address: 8450 E. Valley Blvd., #108, Rosemead, CA, 91770, USA
restaurant.Description: This Rosemead restaurant may be slightly short on fuss, with a well-lit dining room with booths and banquette seating and ordering conducted via a tablet, but the Chinese menu with a variety of offerings is the real reason you're here anyway. Several items are musts, including the rou jia mo, a street food-style Chinese hamburger of sorts with your choice of a protein (order the Kurobuta pork that's slow cooked and sandwiched between a properly crispy flatbread). Other nonnegotiables include xiao long bao, or soup dumplings, and the braised beef noodles with tender and flavorful beef and springy noodles.

restaurant.Name: Good Hot Fish
restaurant.Address: 10 Buxton Ave., Asheville, NC, 28801, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Good Hot Fish, found in the South Slope District among a bevy of craft breweries, stands out with its dark exterior and a whimsical neon fish over the door. The small setting is mostly all business, but there are a number of seats along dining counters inside and out, and the team is a pleasant bunch.Chef Ashleigh Shanti's enticing vision of a traditional fish fry features product like North Carolina catfish and dayboat shrimp. The fish sandwich is a must — dredged in coarsely ground, locally milled cornmeal for an enticing crunch, tucked between slices of white bread and drizzled with spiced buttermilk tartar sauce. A concise range of seafood preparations are also on offer, as well as side dishes like baked mac and cheese and Sea Island red peas.

restaurant.Name: Goosefeather
restaurant.Address: Tarrytown House Estate, 49 E. Sunnyside Ln., Tarrytown, NY, 10591, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: Housed within the historic King Mansion on the Tarrytown House Estate, Goosefeather offers a lively counterpoint to its stately surroundings. Chef Dale Talde’s menu draws on Cantonese traditions while embracing an Asian-American perspective, pairing Hong Kong-inspired staples with contemporary influences and seasonal ingredients. Bold flavors, playful combinations and a touch of nostalgia define the cooking, whether in spicy salmon tartare atop crispy rice, a flaky crab Rangoon scallion pancake, or a crown of duck served with lettuce wraps and Hong Kong toast. The result is an engaging restaurant that remains one of Westchester’s more distinctive dining destinations.

restaurant.Name: Grazie Nonna
restaurant.Address: 1100 15th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20005, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Gerald Addison and Casey Patten are behind this spot that's long on nostalgia and short on shortcuts. This is hearty food that uses quality ingredients while channeling the memories of Mr. Patten's nonna's cooking. Italian-American classics are leveled up in plates of clams casino, perfectly tender and briny with sweet bacon and crunchy breadcrumbs. A handful of pizza selections includes the classics, but creative ones make interesting detours. Macaroni is given the Sunday supper treatment, but it's not just red sauce—prosciutto and peas, tossed with garlic-spiked cream, is a good bet too. Of course, the whole roasted chicken with capers and lemon never disappoints, just like this experience, where a buzzy bar is always packed.

restaurant.Name: Great Maple
restaurant.Address: 1451 Washington St., San Diego, CA, 92103, USA
restaurant.Description: Take the classic 50s diner, add a little swagger and you get Great Maple. It is one of four outlets statewide, but this particular location is always buzzing. Be warned though as parking and counter seats are coveted, so plan ahead.Three-course chef dinners on Mondays; burger and beer nights on Wednesdays; and prime rib Fridays are popular, but it’s also great at brunch. Fruity Pebbles pancakes, lolliwaffles on a stick and maple-bacon donuts are sweet-tooth satisfiers. Late night? Sip a Bloody Mary and tuck in to the brisket popover, a fluffy base with tender smoked meat, poached eggs and béarnaise that will cure what ails you. Seasonal dessert pies are all the rage—including the Valencia orange cream with a pistachio- and brown butter-shortbread crust.

restaurant.Name: Guelaguetza
restaurant.Address: 3014 W. Olympic Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90006, USA
restaurant.Description: This distinct Oaxacan eatery knows exactly what its culinary mission is—so much so that it is made abundantly clear in everything from its website address (ilovemole.com) to the orange façade that announces its presence from blocks away. Inside, pops of green, vinyl-covered tables and happy faces brighten the whimsical setting. A grill station fills the room with the scent of blistering peppers and more.The tlayudas, enchiladas and pozole are all delightful, but it is their negro and rojo moles that are absolute favorites. Mole estofado is so complex that it is nearly impossible to pick out the ingredients creating such a rich and dark sauce, slathered onto chicken or pork. Everyone gets a taste of mole coloradito, drizzled over gratis chips.

restaurant.Name: Guesthouse
restaurant.Address: 850 College Ave., Kentfield, CA, 94904, USA
restaurant.Description: After a decade cooking at Larkspur’s beloved Picco, Chef Jared Rogers has grown well-attuned to the tastes of the polished Marin crowd. His Kentfield eatery is a neighborhood gem, but for residents with million-dollar homes. The menu is appropriately packed with dressed-up crowd-pleasers—from grilled king salmon with chimichurri and summery succotash to decadent flourless chocolate cake piled with chocolate ice cream.Donning soft leather booths, eye-catching wallpaper and a tiled central bar, the room has the feel of a cavernous old barn transformed into a luxe vacation hideaway. This holiday vibe continues with hand-crafted cocktails, like the Royal Bermuda Yacht Club — a tropical rum concoction with lime and grapefruit.

restaurant.Name: Gui Steakhouse & Prime Rib
restaurant.Address: 776 8th Ave., New York, NY, 10036, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: Dining in the heart of Times Square isn't always a good bet, but Gui Steakhouse changes the narrative. A natural choice for pre- or post-theater dining, it's also worth a trip without show tickets to experience their traditional steakhouse classics with Korean influences in a sleek setting. The menu includes raw bar items (Alaskan king crab leg) before shifting the focus to steaks with Japanese wagyu and USDA Prime meat. With a beautiful sear and deep grill marks, the aged steaks are finished simply with a sprinkling of Maldon salt. While steaks are indeed the raison d'être, the menu also features traditional American dishes like flounder and grilled chicken alongside Asian-inspired plates like dan dan noodles and wagyu fried rice.

restaurant.Name: Guisados
restaurant.Address: 2100 E. Cesar E. Chavez Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90033, USA
restaurant.Description: Set on a busy corner with an unassuming façade, this may be a humble storefront, but it’s all heart with an inimitable taste of home. This clean, airy and family-owned spot is open all day, so pop in when the mood strikes to sample their daily specials. Consult the chalkboards for the latest update, then snag a seat at one of the few tables with a view of the grill.It's all about their skillfully prepared tacos and expect to make a mess, as the sauce and juice drip while you're eating. Steak picado tacos with stewed flank steak served over black beans, or their cochinita pibil, with shredded pork braised with achiote and topped with pickled onions, are two favorites.

restaurant.Name: Gusto Handcrafted Pasta & Pizza
restaurant.Address: 1901 Fremont Blvd., Seaside, CA, 93955, USA
restaurant.Description: The surroundings may not be glamorous (Monterey airport is just a skip away), but this family-run establishment is a popular venue for large groups—and the proof is in the pasta. Gauging from the sizable menu of saucy, generously portioned Italian-American staples, no one is likely to leave their table hungry. Delightfully al dente house-made pastas are sure to banish any associations with mushy chain restaurant versions, and even hearty, rustic dishes like eggplant parmigiana get an extra touch of care. The from-scratch approach extends to the mozzarella, which is certainly worth sampling, whether as an antipasto or a topping for an array of thin-crust pizzas.Desserts, like cannoli with sweet mascarpone and ricotta, will tick the nostalgia box.

restaurant.Name: Gwen
restaurant.Address: 6600 Sunset Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90028, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: During the day, this attractive butcher shop sells humanely raised meats from local partner farms. At night, the glowing dining room comes alive, showcasing the same upscale cuts prepared with panache in a room that conjures Art Deco glamour with crystal chandeliers and a roaring fireplace. The menu, meanwhile, offers something for everyone. Start with house-made charcuterie or perhaps smoked beets with leek ash yogurt before picking up the pace with heartier courses like pastas (lobster ravioli with confit leeks) and wood-fire grilled steaks. A seat at the chef’s counter offers a prime vantage point into this kinetic kitchen. Save room for dessert like yuzu tart with buttermilk sorbet.

restaurant.Name: Gymkhana Las Vegas
restaurant.Address: ARIA Resort & Casino, 3730 S. Las Vegas Blvd., Las Vegas, NV, 89158, USA
restaurant.Description: Boasting a swanky, sumptuous interior in a prime location inside Aria Resort and Casino, it’s no wonder that this is one of the buzziest restaurants in town. Scoring a reservation may be a tall order, but intrepid epicures can line up before doors open to vie for seats at the bar, where their efforts will be rewarded with a wealth of tantalizing contemporary Indian dishes — with excellent cocktails and suave service to match. Appetizers draw inspiration from classic street foods, like naan stuffed with wagyu beef keema, or Patiala fried chicken tossed with mint and tamarind chutney. Boldly flavorful curries, ideal for sharing, are a centerpiece, as in a meltingly tender pork cheek vindaloo flavored with red chili and palm vinegar.

restaurant.Name: Gyukatsu Rose
restaurant.Address: 3201 Corrine Dr., Fl. 1, Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
restaurant.Description: This food stall in the East End Market is from the same team behind Domu. Pull up a seat at this Japanese-focused counter and the concept becomes immediately clear as they fire up the grill—it's all about gyukatsu, or breaded beef cutlets. The menu is simple, and the only decision needed is whether you want one portion or two. Sided by cabbage salad, rice, and soup, the beef arrives on a tray seasoned, lightly fried, and sliced, and from there, it's in your hands, searing on your grill and seasoning with soy and onion sauces to your liking. End on a sweet note with their frozen matcha pudding layered with Oreo crumble and brûléed sugar on top. It's a hot ticket, so reservations are a must.

restaurant.Name: HK Lounge Bistro
restaurant.Address: 1136 Folsom St., San Francisco, CA, 94103, USA
restaurant.Description: You're likely to find this modest yet tidily appointed SoMa spot full of regulars during lunch hours, as it's one of the city's most cherished Cantonese establishments. Families and business types alike find pleasure in artfully pleated Shanghai dumplings filled with rich broth and fresh crab meat, or baked pork buns with a crackling topping; sweet bites like fried sesame balls, egg tarts and mango pudding are also much admired. At dinner, the menu is fleshed out with more substantial, large-format dishes, including crisp-skinned roast duck and fragrant steamed seabass.

restaurant.Name: HWARO
restaurant.Address: 776 8th Ave., New York, NY, 10036, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Sungchul Shim is no stranger to the New York restaurant scene, but this 22-seat counter located inside Gui Steakhouse is certainly one to watch. Begin with a cocktail before riding the elevator to discover this hidden-in-plain-sight spot. The space is stunning, though all eyes are drawn to the center where the chefs prepare a multicourse menu fusing Korean flavors with French techniques. The meal begins with a bowl of luscious brown butter miso soup before wild amberjack crudo with a tableside pour of buttermilk koji sauce. The shrimp toast sandwich reveals perfectly cooked abalone nestled at its center, though the white soy custard with Osetra caviar for spooning over top is reason alone for its guest favorite status. A sesame ice cream popsicle is a delightful finale.

restaurant.Name: Haberdish
restaurant.Address: 3106 N. Davidson St., Charlotte, NC, 28205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Set in NoDa, a neighborhood once known for its textile mills, this restaurant's name is a play on the past. Inside, it's rustic-cool with exposed beams and denim-covered banquettes. The action takes place at the counter; order a draft beer or craft cocktail and take it all in. Meanwhile, the menu is rooted in southern comfort. Be sure to order the devilled eggs and the crispy, fried chicken. Sides like homemade tater tots and mac & cheese make everything better. Don't skip dessert, especially the house-made banana pudding served in a Mason jar. Come lunchtime for hearty sandwiches or delicious brunch offerings on the weekends.

restaurant.Name: Hakkasan Miami
restaurant.Address: Fontainebleau Miami Beach, 4441 Collins Ave., Miami Beach, FL, 33140, USA
restaurant.Description: Finding Hakkasan means wading through the lobby of the Fontainebleau—a historic, if riotous, hotel in Miami Beach swimming with beach bodies and night owls. The restaurant’s signature imperial style is on display, featuring dramatic lights, sleek marble tables and ornate wooden slat dividers. Its clubby beats are a constant reminder that you are never far from the party.High quality seafood figures prominently on this carte, among a selection of Cantonese classics and contemporary interpretations. Steamed dumplings highlight scallop, shrimp, spinach and crab; while plucky prawns arrive in a delicate curry with almonds and lily bulbs. A satisfying Peking roast duck is served with such usual but delicious trappings as crêpes, hoisin and cucumber slivers.

restaurant.Name: Hamano Sushi
restaurant.Address: 1332 Castro St., San Francisco, CA, 94114, USA
restaurant.Description: This Noe Valley sushi spot straddles the line between easygoing neighborhood appeal and high-end indulgence. While the dining room is first come, first-served, offering an approachable à la carte menu featuring the likes of maki, tempura, and sashimi, the front counter by contrast is reservation only, and commands a much loftier price point. The omakase option is where Chef Jiro Lin flexes his creative muscles by complementing the likes of salt-cured tile fish, aged hamachi, and sea perch with a potent dose of wasabi, Japanese chili pepper, and fish liver. The more casual option offers less personality, but guests will still find skillful preparation and high-quality ingredients. Wine geeks might find themselves besotted by a tightly curated list.

restaurant.Name: Han Il Kwan
restaurant.Address: 5458 Buford Hwy. NE, Atlanta, GA, 30340, USA
restaurant.Description: Located on Buford Highway in Doraville, the setting stands out with its standalone structure and pagoda roof. The large dining area is bright and well maintained, and offers a variety of seating areas including a section with tabletop grills. Tiled flooring, wood furnishings and a beamed roof produce a pleasant arena.The menu covers the delights of Korean cuisine, from appetizers like haemul-pajeon, the crispy pancake studded with vegetables and seafood; to stimulating stews like the kimchi jjigae served bubbling hot with strips of pork belly and cubes of soft tofu. And then there's barbecue, with an array of sliced and marinated certified Angus beef on offer; or one can choose the vegetable platter option. Come hungry or bring a crowd.

restaurant.Name: Hana re
restaurant.Address: 2930 Bristol St., Costa Mesa, CA, 92626, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list
restaurant.Description: Tucked away in the back corner of a Costa Mesa shopping mall, this intimate ten-seat counter offers a relaxing retreat from the outside world. Chef Atsushi Yokoyama skillfully oversees a leisurely omakase, beginning with variety of composed dishes such as chawanmushi with blue shrimp and smoked trout roe, perhaps followed by such delicacies as hairy crab dressed with tangy tosazu gelee, or tender braised abalone with leek puree and Hokkaido uni. Nigiri forms the final portion of the savory menu, continuing the theme of simply prepared, excellent quality seafood. To finish, a delicate almond panna cotta with seasonal fruit. A compelling variety of sake options adds an additional appeal.

restaurant.Name: Handle
restaurant.Address: 136 Heber Ave., Ste. 107, Park City, UT, 84060, USA
restaurant.Description: This American restaurant in Park City from Chef/owner Briar Handly has a welcoming vibe. Often packed and almost always lively, Handle is the sort of place that works for both groups and date nights alike. The mood is upbeat, with tightly packed tables and an elevated comfort food menu that is dictated by the seasons. Tuck into items like baby carrots over baba sauce, finished with crushed pistachio and honey to start before a hearty entree like beef cheek bourguignon or one of their house-made pastas. Tres leches topped with a scoop of Thai tea ice cream is a perfect send-off.

restaurant.Name: Hank’s Oyster Bar
restaurant.Address: 1624 Q St. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: The original of three locations, Hank’s Oyster Bar promises a good time and a full stomach. Snag a seat on the spacious front patio or opt for a table indoors where bottles of malt vinegar and Old Bay seasoning are a sign of things to come.Meals begin with a bowl of humble Goldfish cheese crackers, then prepare yourself for a sea, ahem, of dishes. Feast on platters of raw bar beauties (including Hank's signature Salty Wolfe oyster) to oysters any way you want them (Hog Island style includes being doused with tangy lemon garlic and Tabasco butter sauce, sprinkled with buttery breadcrumbs and broiled until caramelized). Lobster rolls, creamy chowder and crab cake sandwiches with Old Bay-seasoned fries conjure up days at the beach from years gone by.

restaurant.Name: Harborview
restaurant.Address: 4 Embarcadero Center, San Francisco, CA, 94111, USA
restaurant.Description: With a behemoth $14-million space in the Embarcadero Center to call its own, this restaurant and bar is no mom-and-pop Cantonese spot. In fact, its dining room showcases impressive views of the Ferry building and Bay Bridge from its sunny upper deck patio; add to that a beautiful and polished interior space offering sun-drenched rooms as well as more intimately lit nooks. For lunch, you can order from the extensive dim sum selection or a separate kitchen menu. At dinner, go for the crispy, golden-brown Peking duck, served with crunchy cucumber and scallions, steamed buns and a decadent house-made sauce.

restaurant.Name: Hart's
restaurant.Address: 506 Franklin Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11238, USA
restaurant.Description: Tucked behind the Franklin Avenue subway stairs, this intimate Mediterranean venue has been causing quite a stir. A pretty slate-blue façade directs you to a small space starring whitewashed brick walls, blonde wood tables and a skylight. A handful of seats at the marble counter offer a view into the mini kitchen. But, there is nothing mini about Chef Nick Perkins’ culinary skills. In fact, he is the master of working magic out of a small kitchen.Start with an heirloom tomato salad laced with olive oil, dried red chili, and paired with escabeche-style mussels. Then perfectly poached hake is served with anchovies and bitter greens for a rustic yet relishable dish. Pork Milanese plated with cucumber and shaved fennel flaunts a great deal of fun and flair.

restaurant.Name: Harvest at the Masonic
restaurant.Address: 215 N. Kentucky St., McKinney, TX, 75069, USA
restaurant.Description: Located in McKinney’s historic Masonic Lodge, Harvest pairs seasonally driven cooking with live music and a deeply rooted commitment to sustainability. The restored, multi-level space feels warm and inviting, while the kitchen works closely with local farmers and ranchers to build a menu centered on regional ingredients. Dishes like Creole pan-seared shrimp lean rustic yet thoughtful, balancing richness and brightness with generous portions and clean flavors. An American-focused wine list spotlighting small producers further underscores the restaurant’s community-minded spirit, making this a lively gathering place where sourcing and integrity take center stage.

restaurant.Name: Hatchet Hall
restaurant.Address: 12517 Washington Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90066, USA
restaurant.Description: This lively Culver West spot is always in full swing, starting with the sprawling, pergola-shaded patio that rallies groups when the weather is right. Beyond lies an equally ample dining room with vintage accents like tufted leather banquettes and an L-shaped bar. The lengthy menu highlights a broad range of classics from across the South and, rightly so, biscuits, seasonal vegetables and plenty of pork are given due billing. Deviled eggs, pimento cheese and fried green tomatoes channel all the comfort of an old-fashioned picnic. Entrees, which are often easy to share, cover land and sea, though you could assemble a feast from the vegetable section, starting with collard greens with smoked turkey or blistered snap peas with buttermilk.

restaurant.Name: Hattie B’s Hot Chicken
restaurant.Address: 112 19th Ave. S., Nashville, TN, 37203, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Nashville is synonymous with hot chicken and if you want a true taste, head to Hattie B's. It's a pretty simple promise at this family-run concept. Step up to the counter and decide if it's a bones or no bones day with dark or white meat or tenders and sandwiches. Then comes the all-important decision—how hot? Southern kicks it off with no heat and then reaches increasingly hotter in five tiers. Not sure which level you want? Order the tenders with three heat levels in one dish. Sides are classic Southern staples like green beans and pimento mac and cheese, plus fried pickles and loaded fries. If you've gone a bit overboard, cool your tongue with peach cobbler topped with vanilla ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Hav & Mar
restaurant.Address: 245 Eleventh Ave., New York, NY, 10001, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: How do you share your melting pot heritage without pandering? Just ask Chefs Marcus Samuelsson and Fariyal Abdullahi, the brains behind Hav & Mar. This modern spot pays homage to Samuelsson's Ethiopian and Swedish roots with a seamless and heartfelt approach. The menu pulls from both cultures and their staple ingredients. Start with the bread basket, an impressive collection of lentil roti, oat porridge crisp and teff biscuit. Few dishes represent this cultural collision better than the Swediopian, a berbere-cured salmon shingled between slices of Granny Smith apple, dressed with mustard seed caviar and buckthorn and finished with injera chips. Corn-wrapped snapper served with a bright salsa verde and crispy coconut rice is a can't-miss main.

restaurant.Name: Hed 11
restaurant.Address: Kimpton Hotel Enso, 1800 Sutter St., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
restaurant.Description: Perched in a swanky space at the corner of the Kimpton Hotel Enso, this ambitious Thai project from Chef Piriya "Saint" Boonprasan and owner Naruephon "Billie" Wannajaro gives a hint to its concept right in the name: an 11-course menu that celebrates regional Thai flavors with a contemporary style. The price point doesn’t lend itself to dining on a budget, but despite its variety, the meal won’t over-tax your schedule, with most of the courses arriving together as a sort of miniature banquet for the main. Sweet and savory are blended throughout the menu, whether in bites like a coconut pancake with lime and caviar, a take on khanom jeen sao nam with seared scallop paired with chilled rice noodles, tangy pineapple, and garlic, or even a Thai-style cheesecake with crispy fried onions and passionfruit syrup.

restaurant.Name: Helen
restaurant.Address: 2013 2nd Ave. N., Birmingham, AL, 35203, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Chef Rob McDaniel and his wife Emily built this downtown Birmingham restaurant as an homage to Rob's maternal grandmother who gathered her family for meals that she cooked over her indoor grill. Here at Helen, many of the dishes feature grilled elements.The menu is concise and showcases plates with Southern and international flair. Warm angel biscuits served warm alongside a quenelle of whipped cane syrup butter will soothe your soul. Enjoy a bowl of comfort with braised Peruvian lima beans in a golden broth with coal-roasted rapini and garlic chili oil. Cobia is beautifully seared on the plancha for a simple-but-satisfying dish.

restaurant.Name: Hello Sailor
restaurant.Address: 20210 Henderson Rd., Cornelius, NC, 28031, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Hello Sailor, the younger sibling of nearby Kindred, occupies a prime position overlooking Lake Norman, and the two outdoor terraces are the place to be when the weather is nice (though inside by the wood-burning stove is certainly no consolation prize when winter arrives). While this neighborhood spot that works for all occasions could rest on its setting alone, the menu ticks all the boxes. Its lakeside location means you'll find plenty of seafood on the menu, and PEI mussels and oysters with a glass of wine or cocktail is never a bad idea. Friendly service completes the sunny picture.

restaurant.Name: Hen Mother Cookhouse
restaurant.Address: 11705 Jones Bridge Rd., Ste. B 201, Johns Creek, GA, 30005, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Hen Mother Cookhouse has a setting that befits its name. This Johns Creek charmer (there are two locations) has kitschy farmhouse down pat with blue walls, white-painted bench seating and wood tables, while Chef/owner Soraya Khoury's menu of breakfast and brunch favorites has exactly what you want. From avocado toast and quiche to Southern classics like sourdough waffles with fried chicken, if you want (and you most certainly do), mornings are met with a bevy of delicious choices, but it doesn't end there. Come lunch and BLTs, burgers, and baked goods are the perfect order. No matter your selection, it's all prepared with skill and care, and you'll have a hard time putting down your fork (though the portions are generous, and sides are shareable).

restaurant.Name: Henry's Cuisine
restaurant.Address: 301 E. Valley Blvd., Alhambra, CA, 91801, USA
restaurant.Description: In an unremarkable building that nearly blends in with the rest of the street, Henry’s has quietly but confidently satisfied an ever-dwindling demand for homestyle Cantonese cooking since 2015. With a scarlet-red lobster as their logo, shells painted silver and gold and hung on the wall, and large groups huddled around platters of it, there isn’t much guessing as to what the signature is here. Come for dinner to unlock the menu’s full breadth of specialties. Highlights include delicately fried shrimp with salted egg as well as a striking deep-fried salted pig’s feet, its skin as crisp and crunchy as a chip. Vegetables are a must but ask what’s in season. We’re partial to the soothing, quiet bitterness of mustard greens with garlic.

restaurant.Name: Herb & Wood
restaurant.Address: 2210 Kettner Blvd., San Diego, CA, 92101, USA
restaurant.Description: This establishment enjoys a loyal following. The multilevel former warehouse could lean cavernous, but its barrel-vaulted ceilings and funky artwork exude a distinct Parisian bohemian warmth. The whole place is set aglow and everyone, including the staff, wants to be here. Its wide-ranging menu runs the gamut—from rustic, wood-fired dishes including grilled trumpet mushrooms and pizzas, to more refined plates like venison over buttermilk polenta. The PB&C, a chocolate-whiskey cake with peanut butter mousse and rich milk chocolate gelato, absolutely hits the spot.

restaurant.Name: Herbsaint
restaurant.Address: 701 St. Charles Ave., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
restaurant.Description: More than two decades after opening, Herbsaint remains one of New Orleans’ most dependable dining destinations. Set along bustling St. Charles Avenue, the dining room hums with regulars, business lunches and visitors drawn by Chef Donald Link’s influential blend of French, Italian and Southern cooking. Signature dishes endure for good reason, including the rich house-made spaghetti with guanciale and fried egg and Muscovy duck leg confit served with dirty rice and citrus gastrique. Cornmeal-fried oysters showcase the kitchen’s lighter touch, while an excellent wine list and warm service reinforce the restaurant’s enduring appeal.

restaurant.Name: Heretík
restaurant.Address: 1441 26th St., Denver, CO, 80205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Sunlight cuts through a wide, makeshift garage door window, warming this lively little spot where a small kitchen prepares a smart, creative roster of Basque-inspired dishes. Whole, glistening chickens spin on the rotisserie all night long, as friends crowd around small plates like pan con tomate crowned with Hokkaido uni or deviled eggs gussied up with tuna and capers. Merging Spanish and French sensibilities, the cooking is carefully calibrated and matches a short but thoughtful wine list featuring pours from Galicia to Jurançon. No dinner is complete without the grand finale: A perfect wedge of Basque cheesecake, at once indulgent and luxurious.

restaurant.Name: Herons
restaurant.Address: The Umstead Hotel & Spa, 100 Woodland Pond Dr., Cary, NC, 27513, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Need a getaway but have limited time? Herons offers the experience of a country escape without the commute. Set within The Umstead Hotel and Spa on three acres of woodland, this restaurant is a showpiece for their nearby farm's produce. Try several dishes or opt for the chef's surprise five- course menu to relish fresh and vibrant plates crafted with care by Chef Steven Devereaux Greene. His South Carolina roots are best seen in dishes like shrimp and grits, and a tropical-inspired dessert that combines pineapple jam, rum whipped ganache and ginger sorbet is impressive. Be sure to consult the extensive, globally minded wine list. The restaurant has even developed several wines in close collaboration with the vineyards.

restaurant.Name: Hey Kiddo
restaurant.Address: 4337 Tennyson St., Ste. 300, Denver, CO, 80212, USA
restaurant.Description: Perched above Tennyson Street, Hey Kiddo stands out as the hippest of Denver powerhouse Chef Kelly Whitaker’s empire. The third-floor venue encompasses a rooftop bar area and a bespoke cocktail lounge in the back (referred to as “Ok Yeah”) but the restaurant is the heart of the operation. The playful menu centers around broadly Asian-inflected shareable plates like an exceptionally crunchy take on Korean fried chicken, or tender pork ribs with a salted plum barbecue sauce, accompanied by compelling sides like crispy potato pavé with a trout roe gravy, or an assortment of house-made pickles and kimchi. For a sweet finale, red miso ice cream can be customized with the likes of brûléed banana, broken cone or grappa whipped cream.

restaurant.Name: Hidden Fish
restaurant.Address: 4764 Convoy St., San Diego, CA, 92111, USA
restaurant.Description: You’ll be on the clock at this tiny sushi spot, where the omakase is a 90-minute experience, but despite such punctuality, you will savor every bite here. In fact, you’ll find yourself slowing down to savor each and every creation from the talented chefs. However, seats here are hard to come by so be sure to reserve ahead of time or risk serious FOMO.Like other top tier sushiyas, they source both locally with San Diego uni and across the globe with Peruvian scallops and of course, plenty of Japanese species. A chalkboard menu keeps diners apprised of the current lineup, and for those who are still peckish after their tasting, there’s a bonus menu of handrolls and special seasonal nigiri for further sampling.

restaurant.Name: High Street
restaurant.Address: 101 S. 9th St. Door 1, Philadelphia, PA, 19107, USA
restaurant.Description: The Franklin Building plays host to this modern American restaurant founded by Ellen Yin. It’s quite an operation with a bakery nearby along with a private dining space at the back for that big celebration. Furthermore, they hold classes for anyone who wants to learn how to bake or make pizza. Robustly flavored, keenly seasonal, and generously sized dishes are the mainstay of the kitchen, which is visible through glass walls. At lunch, most customers come in for a vibrant salad or a hearty sandwich. Come dinner, roast chicken and steak mingle alongside pastas, all of which show a level of care, commitment and originality.

restaurant.Name: Himitsu
restaurant.Address: 1030 Torrey Pines Rd. G, La Jolla, CA, 92037, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: "Irasshaimase!" is the greeting commonly heard upon entering this cozy little sushiya. You’ll want to plan ahead to snag one of the eight coveted seats at the pristine counter, but it’s well worth the forethought, as these friendly chefs take great pride in discussing the quality of their fish and the techniques used to prepare your meal. It’s also a front row seat to their admirable knife skills.Such affability extends to the dining room, where servers flash big smiles and loads of greenery as well as natural wood come together to create a truly serene effect. Omakase is the way to go, but there are à la carte options as well—from appetizers, soups, sashimi and maki (sporting soft, well-seasoned rice) to specialty plates and daily fish specials.

restaurant.Name: Hippo
restaurant.Address: 5916 1/2 Figueroa St., Los Angeles, CA, 90042, USA
restaurant.Description: The name comes from the building’s former life as the Highland Park Post Office, but everything else here is Cal-Ital in spirit. The dining space is convivial and airy, with beamed ceilings and an open kitchen as its focal point. The vibe is as good for dates as it is for groups. Complimentary bread is rarely as satisfying as their focaccia, with its crispy, salty crust and soft interior. Begin with a sampling of small plates, like hamachi crudo topped with dollops of Meyer lemon relish. Then move on to freshly made pasta, like tortelloni with herbed ricotta in a lemon butter sauce before enjoying the chicken grilled over almond wood and served with a slightly spicy aji panca sauce and griddled potatoes.

restaurant.Name: Hiyakawa Miami
restaurant.Address: 2700 N. Miami Ave., #5, Miami, FL, 33127, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Notable sake list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: Is there a dining room cooler than Hiyakawa Miami? Probably not. Modern art hangs throughout the space that is art itself, with the counter and tables under an arch of backlit, undulating wood slats. This intimate stage glows at the bottom of an apartment building in trendy Wynwood.Top-quality seafood flown in from Japan and beyond meets creative flourishes like cured egg yolk and Okinawa salt. A multicourse omakase is available at the counter and in the dining room, and the a la carte offers a range of items in addition to nigiri, sashimi, and maki. Don't sleep on the Sakana Kara Age, or fried fish fillets sprinkled with seaweed salt and resting in a fish broth, but it's the lamb chops, doubling as performance art thanks to a bed of burning rosemary, that make a lasting impression.

restaurant.Name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
restaurant.Address: 1 Ferry Building, #11, San Francisco, CA, 94111, USA
restaurant.Description: Can’t make the trip to Marin to shuck oysters on Hog Island’s docks? They’ll bring Tomales Bay’s finest to you at this buzzing cityside outpost in the Ferry Building, which draws long lines of tourists and locals for platters of some of the sweetest, freshest bivalves on the West Coast. You’ll receive all the accompaniments — lemon, Tabasco, mignonette — but they’re good enough to slurp solo. Once you’ve had your fill, sample other aquatic offerings: crudo featuring sustainably caught sea bass; a rustic seafood stew loaded with prawns, clams and mussels; as well as the exceptional Manila clam chowder. Throw in the expansive Bay views from the patio and dining room, and those lines come as no surprise.

restaurant.Name: Home grown
restaurant.Address: 968 Memorial Dr. SE, Atlanta, GA, 30316, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Located in the Reynoldstown neighborhood in East Atlanta, Home Grown is a classic all-day breakfast and lunch spot complete with knotty pine paneling and booth seating. While it has a retro feel to it, don't assume you know everything on this menu. Instead, expect oodles of Southern charm and definitely ask about the daily specials, since you may come across items like house-made tamales, Gulf red snapper tacos, lasagna or even a pu pu platter with frog legs and crab claws. The focused menu stays largely local in both theme and sourcing, delivering country cooking that never disappoints. Case in point? That open-faced buttermilk biscuit layered with perfectly crisp chicken drowned in hearty pork sausage gravy, of course.

restaurant.Name: Honeysuckle
restaurant.Address: 631 N. Broad St., Philadelphia, PA, 19123, USA
restaurant.Description: There is no exact right way to experience Omar and Cybille St. Aude-Tate’s darling restaurant on North Broad. You could post up at the big bar or hold court on a large communal table or ease into the couches. In this airy, industrial space, you have choices, just as you do with their wonderful, Afro-centric prix fixe. Hush puppies come crowned with country ham and paired with smoked bacon aioli. You’ve never seen a potato salad like this one or had fried fish with crème fraîche and chive-dill sauce. How about wagyu beef cheek and oxtail tamales? Course after course, find refinement and imagination, careful calibration and attractive presentation. Service is equally warm and attentive, and the whole thing comes together like a charm.

restaurant.Name: Hong Kong Food Street
restaurant.Address: 23015 Colonial Pkwy., Ste. a101, Katy, TX, 77449, USA
restaurant.Description: Congee with abalone and chicken. Pork and shrimp wontons in a clear, light broth. Portuguese egg tarts. In a non-descript shopping center in Katy, this family-owned restaurant brings a taste of Hong Kong to Houston. The modern dining room features sleek light fixtures and handsome private dining rooms fit with lazy susans. And unlike some restaurants that compile an endless book of options, the kitchen here keeps things tight with a relatively curated selection of classics. Nothing is rushed or thrown together, and food arrives piping hot. Beautifully fried shrimp with candied walnuts is an indulgent throwback. Shrimp and tofu fritters delight as well. On weekends, be sure to ask about any seafood specials.

restaurant.Name: Hot and Hot Fish Club
restaurant.Address: 2901 2nd Ave. S., Ste. 110, Birmingham, AL, 35233, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: With history dating back to 1994, Chris and Idie Hastings have cooked their way into the very fabric of the city’s culinary tapestry. Now located in trendy Pepper Place, the bustling space features a curved chef’s counter in the kitchen as well as ample bar and table seating. Their respect for the seasons means that the menu is constantly on the move. Come winter, look for hearty preparations like rabbit pappardelle with butternut squash or ancho-rubbed Iberico pork chop with apple chutney. In the summer, everyone comes for the tomato salad, which features a towering stack of heirloom tomatoes dressed up with lady peas, fried okra and a zippy balsamic vinaigrette. For dessert, chocolate souffle with crème anglaise is a lovely, sweet finale.

restaurant.Name: Hugo’s Frog Bar & Fish House
restaurant.Address: 1024 N. Rush St., Chicago, IL, 60611, USA
restaurant.Description: Housed in a sprawling setting adjacent to big brother Gibson’s, Hugo’s always seems packed. The vast dining room sets white linen-topped tables amid dark polished wood and pale walls decorated with a mounted swordfish, fish prints, and model ships. Hugo’s bar draws its own crowd with abundant counter seating. The menu focuses on a selection of fish, steaks, and chops, supplemented by stone crab claws, oysters, crab cakes, chowders, and sautéed frog’s legs. Family-style sides—creamed spinach or roasted Brussels sprouts in Bourbon maple butter—are a worthy addition.With generous portions all around, you'll need a football team to share a slice of the Muddy Bottom Pie, or just a handful of pals to savor other decadent desserts like the apple pie.

restaurant.Name: Hungry Thirsty
restaurant.Address: 407 Smith St., Brooklyn, NY, 11231, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Hungry Thirsty breathes new life into the space formerly occupied by the popular Ugly Baby and now draws lines of its own for its standout southern Thai cooking. From the bright yellow facade to the orange walls and blue-and-green bar, this place doesn't pull any punches when it comes to bold design, and the vibe is equally upbeat. And then there's the food, with a range of likeable dishes like salads, curries, stir-fries and sides turned out by Chef Prasert "Tee" Kanghae. Pla Kra Pong Tod Nam Pla is a beautiful, fried branzino served with dipping sauce that impresses with each bite, and thirteen eggs, a plate of soy sauce-marinated eggs, is a worthy accompaniment. For dessert, a coconut houses jelly with strips of sweetened coconut flesh for an intriguing ending.

restaurant.Name: Hush Public House
restaurant.Address: 14202 N. Scottsdale Rd., Ste. 167, Scottsdale, AZ, 85254, USA
restaurant.Description: Reading as a relaxed neighborhood bar, this spot from Chef Dom Ruggiero offers an unexpectedly ambitious menu. From the strong cocktail program to the chalkboard trumpeting local producers, everything is intentional. The menu draws from a range of global influences. Dishes like spaghetti squash sautéed in brown butter, layered over labneh, and finished with a combination of pepitas, pomegranate seeds and harissa chili crunch display skill. Silky, whipped eggplant crowned with pine nuts, fresh herbs, and braised lamb neck is deeply savory. Other notable dishes include the Italian beef, an unapologetically indulgent, fork-and-knife homage to a Chicago tradition. Don't even think about skipping desserts like date cake resting in a bourbon toffee sauce.

restaurant.Name: Husk
restaurant.Address: 76 Queen St., Charleston, SC, 29401, USA
restaurant.Description: Open since 2011, the enduring legacy of this Southern restaurant continues to draw in waves of diners. Reservations are scarce, and before doors open, crowds form on the sidewalk hoping to snag a table inside this historic, two-story house. But make no mistake, this kitchen isn’t resting on any laurels. The menu is full of Southern favorites prepared with notable care: pimento cheese with country ham and biscuits, cornbread, fried catfish. Pies, cakes and a generous dose of warm hospitality make for a complete experience at this Southern staple.

restaurant.Name: Hyderabadi Zaiqa
restaurant.Address: 785 9th Ave., New York, NY, 10019, USA
restaurant.Description: Don't come with a big group expecting a seat, as this tiny Theater District spot only has a few tables and counter seats, but Mohammad Tarique Khan and Jayesh Naik deliver food with a big personality. Service is a rare cross between attentive and efficient, and the food comes out just as quickly. This is Indian cooking with a focus on Hyderabad, though regional favorites from the north and south also make an appearance on the menu. First up is the unmissable samosa, that flaky, golden-brown pyramid filled with a comforting blend of potatoes, peas, and spices. Then, opt for the goat fry biryani with an oval silver tray piled high with rice studded with tender, stewed bone-in goat meat. Fragrant and flavorful, it's served with a side of raita.

restaurant.Name: Hyun
restaurant.Address: 10 E. 33rd St., New York, NY, 10016, USA
restaurant.Description: Hyun is a luxurious take on Korean barbecue, focusing squarely on top-notch Japanese A5 Wagyu, butchered in-house and grilled tableside. Enter this temple of indulgent tranquility to discover sleek dark wood, cool slate surfaces, and private rooms.The Hyun-makase is the gateway into this one-of-a-kind meal which takes you on a journey of 12 different pieces of Japanese A5 Wagyu. Each piece is expertly prepared tableside and served alongside house-made fresh kimchi, green lettuce for wrapping, and a crispy scallion salad that balances the unctuous Wagyu. The tasting is complete when the bulgogi is prepared. Diners may also look forward to other indulgences like rice with uni and truffles, or thick noodles with cold beef broth.

restaurant.Name: I Cavallini
restaurant.Address: 284 Grand St., Brooklyn, NY, 11211, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: Chef Nick Curtola cooks with restraint and confidence at this regional Italian spot just across from sibling The Four Horsemen. The menu is rooted in tradition, handled cleanly and without excess. Begin with the nervetti and onion salad, where braised beef tendons are shaved thin and paired with crisp, acidic onions; a striking dish that signals the kitchen’s comfort with depth and simplicity. Handmade pastas and rustic mains follow with balance and control. Desserts are essential here: the tiramisu is feather-light, generously portioned and among the most satisfying in the city. Reservations may be hard to come by, but arrive early for a seat at the bar and a lovely way to experience the room and the cooking up close.

restaurant.Name: I Sodi
restaurant.Address: 314 Bleecker St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Manhattan has no shortage of Italian restaurants, but surely Rita Sodi runs two of the most beloved ones. Just down the street from Via Carota, this cozy, buzzy hotspot remains a difficult reservation to score so consider planning on an early-hour walk-in. The kitchen watches the seasons closely in daily specials like grilled tomato and burrata, while also respecting that some signatures can never leave the menu. The perfectly layered lasagna is a must for first timers, and it contrasts wonderfully with a citrusy tangle of pappardelle al limon. Regardless of where you sit – bar, dining room, or further back – the neighborhood restaurant is a constant hive of activity, fueled in part by a busy bar that knows its way around a Negroni.

restaurant.Name: IMA
restaurant.Address: 9669 S. Santa Monica Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90210, USA
