Huarache de huitlacoche is a well-known dish prepared with care, and nothing completes the meal quite like cinnamon-dusted churros.

restaurant.Name: La Costanera
restaurant.Address: Oceano Hotel, 260 Capistrano Rd., Half Moon Bay, CA, 94019, USA
restaurant.Description: Where else can you stroll in after a day at the beach and get a delicious Peruvian meal? La Costanera, nestled within the darling coastal town of Half Moon Bay, of course! Traditional and modern art abound, but it's the boldly flavored plates from Chef Carlos Altamirano and his team that garner attention. Palta rellena, which fills half an avocado with roasted chicken chicharrones and lime-infused mayonnaise, is a fun and light-hearted interpretation of the dish. Cebice pescado marinated in aji rocoto leche de tigre is both tangy and kicky, while lomo saltado is savory and hearty. Be sure to sample the creative cocktails. Alternatively, try a delicious and refreshing chicha morada.

restaurant.Name: La Devozione: The Oval
restaurant.Address: 428 W. 16th St., New York, NY, 10011, USA
restaurant.Description: This international outpost from Italy's 110-year-old, family-run Pastificio Di Martino, is a multi-concept space nestled within the Chelsea Market. The restaurant houses a pasta shop along with two dining spaces, including The Oval. It is aptly named, as the 30-seat counter awaits diners who will twirl their forks through a pasta tasting menu. It's all shapes, styles, and sizes, and it's far from dainty, with plate after plate of pasta. The manicotti is filled with sole and served with a bracing butter and caper sauce. Enjoy the penne served with rabbit confit and artichokes, and finish with a refreshing Mojito-inspired dessert with granita and grapefruit foam.

restaurant.Name: La Marcha
restaurant.Address: 2026 San Pablo Ave., Berkeley, CA, 94702, USA
restaurant.Description: This Spanish delight is a coveted spot for both tapas and paella, offered in varieties from the traditional mixta (prawns, chicken, chorizo, garlic, peppers) to the inventive “tres cerditos” (three little pigs) featuring pork chorizo, shoulder and belly. The classic tapas are also out in full force — from grilled head-on garlic shrimp and salt cod croquettes with nutty romesco, to tortilla Española. Located on busy San Pablo Avenue, the lively space offers enticements for groups of all sizes: foursomes can make the most of the sizable paellas, while a duo of happy hours offer discounts on wine at the L-shaped bar and a selection of free tapas, perfect for solo diners or couples.

restaurant.Name: La Mercerie
restaurant.Address: 53 Howard St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Tucked inside the Roman and Williams Guild in SoHo, La Mercerie is one of the city’s most beautiful dining rooms. Soaring ceilings, tall windows, pale blue banquettes, and crisp white tablecloths create an atmosphere that feels effortlessly Parisian. The cooking is equally appealing, with chef Héloïse Fischbach offering a menu of French classics prepared with confidence and care. A warming stew of lentils and merguez is deeply satisfying, while salmon wrapped in cabbage and golden puff pastry arrives with a velvety beurre blanc brightened by citrus. A wealth of classic desserts, including profiteroles, tarte tatin, and crème brûlée, offers a sweetly nostalgic finish.

restaurant.Name: La Padrona
restaurant.Address: 38 Trinity Pl., Boston, MA, 02116, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: This glamorous, two-story looker is the place to be. Located within Raffles Boston, this playful Italian restaurant starts with an easygoing ground floor bar and lounge. Up the grand staircase, find a high-energy dining room, while a large, U-shaped bar anchors this gorgeous space fit with big windows, globe lights and gold accents. Thankfully, these stylish environs also come with substantial cooking. Start with cheese and fennel breadsticks before digging into beautifully seared scallops finished in saffron butter. The pastas are all made in-house and many of the entrees are portioned to share. An extensive wine selection, an astute cocktail program and a sharp service team complete this proper night out.

restaurant.Name: La Petite Grocery
restaurant.Address: 4238 Magazine St., New Orleans, LA, 70115, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Tucked into a historic corner building on Magazine Street, La Petite Grocery captures the easy elegance that defines the best of New Orleans dining. Beneath yellow walls and crisp white tablecloths, Chef Justin Devillier’s kitchen delivers Louisiana flavors with a light touch and a strong sense of place. Signature blue crab beignets remain a must-order, arriving hot, airy and surprisingly delicate. Elsewhere, feather-light ricotta dumplings with wild mushrooms and beautifully fried paneed rabbit showcase the kitchen’s knack for balancing comfort and refinement. Finish with the warm gâteau Basque, a fitting finale to one of Uptown’s most enduring neighborhood favorites.

restaurant.Name: La Taqueria
restaurant.Address: 2889 Mission St., San Francisco, CA, 94110, USA
restaurant.Description: This local favorite always has a queue — and for good reason. From tech bros in hoodies to families out for Sunday lunch, the jovial Miguel Jara serves a diverse crowd. You may find him working the register or handing out roses to customers. Counter service makes it feel no-frills, but this is the kind of place that relishes in its simplicity. Most are here for the same thing: A carne asada super burrito that is everything you dream it should be. It may not be on the menu, but order your taco “Dorado-style,” which begins as a corn tortilla crisped on the plancha, layered with cheese and another tortilla, before getting loaded with toppings.

restaurant.Name: La Tête d’Or
restaurant.Address: 318 Park Ave. S., New York, NY, 10010, USA
restaurant.Description: Glamorous and grand, this Flatiron looker is a reminder of what steakhouses can be in their most satisfying and beautiful form. Thank Chef Daniel Boulud, who brings his signature French flair to this classic genre. Start in the bar, a striking stage with leather-paneled walls and smart cocktails, before heading to the table. The setting is expansive with soaring ceilings, walnut floors, and servers positioned like turrets, ready to swoop in at any moment. Indeed, this is a room where deals get done. Caesar salads made tableside and prime rib sliced on roving trolleys up the charm on a menu that covers all the bases with dry-aged steaks, prime seafood, and ice cream sundaes. Expense accounts will take to the top-shelf Bordeaux and private dining rooms.

restaurant.Name: La Vara
restaurant.Address: 268 Clinton St., Brooklyn, NY, 11201, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Alex Raij knows her tapas, helping to kickstart the craze in Manhattan. More than a decade ago, she jumped boroughs to Brooklyn and opened La Vara, which she co-owns with husband, Eder Montero. Billing itself as “cocina casera” or “home cooking,” this kitchen elevates humble cuisine to impressive levels. Product quality is excellent, and the playful spirit behind these dishes is the definition of creative cooking. Menu highlights include huevos rellenos, judías a la plancha, or grilled romano beans and butter beans in a bright Romesco sauce, and cochinillo, or a slow-roasted suckling pig leg with chimichurri.

restaurant.Name: La'Shukran
restaurant.Address: 417 Morse St. NE, Washington, DC, 20002, USA
restaurant.Description: La' Shukran feels like a discovery, as you'll need to walk down an alley, look for a green door and climb the stairs to arrive at this cool spot with a funky, retro vibe. It's definitely a hot spot for drinks, but the Levantine cuisine designed for sharing is far from second place.From escargot and sweetbreads to labneh with Maryland crab, summer peppers and corn in green harissa, some dishes lean less traditional, while others, like haswei, or fried rice with seven-spice lamb, seem simple but are spot on. Every table needs an order of their soujek dumplings. Filled with beef and lamb shoulder and resting in a vibrant smoked corn and tomato brodo with urfa chili crunch and toum, it's easy to see why reservations are snapped up so quickly here.

restaurant.Name: Lakruwana
restaurant.Address: 668 Bay St., Staten Island, NY, 10304, USA
restaurant.Description: Prepare for a sensory overload the moment you set foot into Lakruwana—the Sri Lankan hot spot is covered from floor-to-ceiling in murals, sculptures, flags, and more. The kaleidoscope of textures and colors is a welcome sight, as is the energetic owner who drifts from table to table.Street food takes center stage here, where you a variety of traditional dishes hit the mark. Don't miss the kottu roti, a stir-fried dish with godamba roti, chicken, vegetables and chicken curry or the traditional hoppers, with its bowl-shaped crepe served with a yellow fish curry. The oversized platter is ideal for sharing.

restaurant.Name: Lamaii
restaurant.Address: 4480 Spring Mountain Rd., Ste. 700, Las Vegas, NV, 89102, USA
restaurant.Description: Lamaii is located at Shan Tau Square in Las Vegas' Chinatown. Large arched windows and a contemporary look of dark wood, woven vinyl seating and metallic embellishments produce a pleasant mien. While the wine list is lengthy, the food menu is concise, with offerings that are equal parts home-spun and dialed in. Diners can expect to find small plates, noodles, and specialties like gang rawaeng (turmeric curry with slow-braised beef); kao soi from the north; and kua gling (ground pork stirred fry with spicy southern curry paste and young peppercorn).

restaurant.Name: LanZhou Ramen
restaurant.Address: 5231 Buford Hwy. NE, Doraville, GA, 30340, USA
restaurant.Description: Located on Buford Highway in a busy shopping center, LanZhou is both the name of a Chinese city and a type of hand-pulled noodle that just so happens to be this spot's main attraction. Those delicious noodles are available in hearty soups with a variety of proteins, and also come broth-less. From there, broad Sichuan-leaning dishes tempt diners. Fried pot stickers sport a beautiful crispy, lacy base and delight with a savory goodness. Roast duck hand-pulled noodle soup is pure, unadulterated satisfaction, slurp by glorious slurp. Served in a massive bowl bobbing with bouncy noodles, baby bok choy, roast bone-in duck and scallions, it's loaded with flavor and will certainly cure whatever ails you.

restaurant.Name: Larb Thai-Isan
restaurant.Address: 6234 N. Federal Hwy., Fort Lauderdale, FL, 33308, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This restaurant brings plenty of color, character, and Thai flair (note the tuk tuk in the back) to a space nestled within a busy shopping center in Fort Lauderdale. It's always busy and there are no reservations, but it's worth the wait. Their large menu is far from standard, including everything from curries, noodle dishes, and salads to signature dishes from the Isan region. Like spicy? They'll ask for your preference and won't hold back if you indicate you're a heat seeker. Dishes to order include Yum Naem Khao Tod, a classic crispy rice salad studded with fermented sausage and mixed with peanuts, ginger, and fresh herbs. Fried banana is a must-order, as is a classic mango sticky rice.

restaurant.Name: Laser Wolf
restaurant.Address: 1301 N. Howard St., Philadelphia, PA, 19122, USA
restaurant.Description: This Philadelphia skewer shop is the original (there's a sister spot in Brooklyn). This hipster chic spot, where industrial design elements are softened by lush greenery and lanterns suspended from the ceiling, is perfect for a group. The vibe is buzzy with a menu built around charcoal-grilled meat, fish and vegetable skewers sided by a generous spread of salatim, a variety of mezze and warm pita. It's a place that begs for sharing, with everything from hummus and muhammara to tabouleh, Moroccan carrots, Yemenite pickles and more. As if that's not enough, fries and grilled halloumi are on offer, but don't skip an order of the tender lamb ribs in a deliciously sticky cola and sour cherry reduction glaze. Sorbet and soft serve round out the satisfying meal.

restaurant.Name: Laser Wolf
restaurant.Address: The Hoxton, Williamsburg, 97 Wythe Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11249, USA
restaurant.Description: Guests of Williamsburg's hip Hoxton Hotel who seek to sip a cocktail while enjoying a stunning sunset over Manhattan need to just hop on the elevator and head to the rooftop to reach Laser Wolf. Of course, scoring a reservation at this hot spot is not as easy. The atmosphere is especially buzzy with lights strung overhead, plus trendy music and a bustling open kitchen. This menu focuses on Israeli cuisine centered around grilled skewers. It all begins with salatim including the likes of babaghanoush, mushrooms with Swiss chard and sour cherry, pickles, gigante beans with harissa and more. Meat and vegetable skewers are next, with lamb kofta a winning choice. Finally, brown sugar soft-serve ice cream rounds out the satisfying meal.

restaurant.Name: Latha
restaurant.Address: 628 E. Adams St., Phoenix, AZ, 85004, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Latha, which means "flavor" in Swahili, promises exactly that. Set within the bungalow-style Silva House in downtown Phoenix's Heritage Square, this restaurant spotlights the food of the African diaspora, blending influences from Africa, Brazil, the Caribbean and the American South on a three-course prix fixe and an à la carte menu. Expect a parade of dishes made with care, from burnt onion hummus, centered around vibrant cherry tomatoes, finished with za'tar and served with whole grain chapati flatbread, to pineapple-glazed piri piri chicken with a round of jollof rice. Opt for a warmed wedge of Southern pound cake for dessert, with house-made whipped cream, white chocolate and tropical marmalade.

restaurant.Name: Launderette
restaurant.Address: 2115 Holly St., Austin, TX, 78702, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Chef Rene Ortiz's spot is good, clean fun, and not just because it's a former laundromat converted into this contemporary diner. Inside, tables and bar seating welcome diners, while patio seating is ideal for nice weather. The cocktail selection is notable (think mezcal negronis and other inventive drinks), and their happy hour is a nice way to sample without busting your budget. From beef tartare with tonnato, chestnut mushrooms, and an ash- infused rye bread to grilled octopus served over roasted yellow tomato sauce with Calabrian chili mayonnaise and bottarga, the dishes are creative and craveable. Desserts, like the tonka bean mille-feuille with lemon curd, blueberry jam and crème fraiche ice cream, are worthy of attention.

restaurant.Name: Le B
restaurant.Address: 283 W. 12th St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: Chef Angie Mar presents a celebration of haute French cuisine married with her Chinese heritage in this luxurious Greenwich Village location. The intimate and opulent space glimmers in sapphire hues and velvet banquettes, while white tablecloths and jacketed staff set the tone for a celebratory night out or an intimate date. Le B is her passionate celebration of classic French cuisine. The gorgeous terrine of pork and duck, draped in pistachio and garnished with kumquat confit is always a fine start. From there, choose your own decadent adventure of lobster "blanquette," poached foie gras or pig's trotter. Rich sauce work, like Madeira-spike pork jus for the chou farcie with rabbit or Sauternes and tarragon cream to dress the seafood wellington, is a distinctive touch. Additionally, tasting menus are offered; and exclusively at the bar the chef's 45-day aged burger is served.

restaurant.Name: Le Calamar
restaurant.Address: 1600 S. 1st St., Ste. 100, Austin, TX, 78704, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: France meets Texas at restaurant tucked at the base of a contemporary building in South Austin. It's equal parts mod (concrete floors and exposed ductwork) and moody (dark colors, leather chairs) and has the bistro vibe down pat. The compact menu is designed for sharing and though elegant, it's far from fussy, as in the daily catch with almondine sauce and salsa macha. Seared gnocchi Parisienne may be a side, but it gives main dish energy with a decadent brown butter sauce, and for a twist on tradition, order the baked Texas with honey pecan dacquoise cake, olive oil semi freddo and torched meringue. The wine list even features some Lone Star State varieties by the glass.

restaurant.Name: Le Chêne
restaurant.Address: 76 Carmine St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed everywhere
restaurant.Description: With tables huddled close, the ceiling low and the room packed, everyone looks when a pithivier emerges from the kitchen. Ornately carved, perfectly bronzed and flaky, and layered with precision, this French throwback tells you everything you need to know about Alexia and Ronan Duchêne’s West Village bijou. Rich, robust cooking celebrates French excellence of yesteryear with foie gras terrines and vin jaune sauces prepared with substance and astuteness. A wonderful, curved bar in the front room welcomes walk-ins. Wine lovers will not want for choice, as the serious list is deep and carefully curated.

restaurant.Name: Le Gigot
restaurant.Address: 18 Cornelia St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.Description: At first glance, Le Gigot transports guests to a romantic and inviting little bistro—the kind you’d only find in La Ville-Lumière. The service exceeds expectations with uncharacteristic warmth that brings a welcoming vibe to the nostalgic dining room. Tasty renditions of classic bistro fare dominate the menu, so expect the cooking to be familiar and pleasing. The petit bouillabaisse begins as a saffron fish broth with a red-peppery North African accent to elevate the traditional fish and seafood dish. Their cassoulet is a beloved Toulousaine version with duck confit, bacon, cannellini beans, herbs and luscious pork. Finally, apple tarte tatin, served warm with a dollop of crème fraîche and fresh blueberries, is a perfect closer.

restaurant.Name: Le Jardinier New York
restaurant.Address: 610 Lexington Ave., New York, NY, 10022, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Chef Alain Verzeroli's light-filled space is a verdant vision—with olive-green velvet furnishings, green-veined marble flooring, and lush plants at every turn. It’s the perfect effect for the chef's produce-driven menu, where seasonal vegetables, fruits, and herbs play a prominent role—with carefully sourced meats and sustainable fish as the supporting cast. Dishes have included the likes of grilled Spanish octopus, plated with green olives, romesco, and green beans, or Ora King salmon enhanced with smoked chili butter and pak choi. End with a Valrhona chocolate crémeux with a salted caramel sabayon or the delightful lemon tart with tarragon ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Le Rock
restaurant.Address: 45 Rockefeller Plaza, New York, NY, 10111, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: No stranger to crowds, the team behind Frenchette has quickly found its footing on the ground floor of bustling Rockefeller Center. Dim lighting blankets this elegant, Art-Deco space where a large bar up front mixes and stirs at a fast clip. They have good reason to be speedy: This is one of the more refined restaurants to open in the area in years, and the crowds have caught on immediately. In line with a French brasserie, the menu offers familiar trappings: seafood platters, hearty pâtés, classic sauces like bearnaise and brown butter, duck confit lentils, and, of course, delicious profiteroles smothered in buckwheat honey fudge. Adding to the fun is a welcome bit of tableside showmanship for dishes like leeks vinaigrette.

restaurant.Name: Le Veau d'Or
restaurant.Address: 129 E. 60th St., New York, NY, 10022, USA
restaurant.Description: Originally established in 1937 and steeped in history, this charming bistro is intimate in scale and rocks a decidedly throwback look. Dark wood, a liberal use of red, and small closely set tables draped with linens produce a cozy yet sexy ambience that has diners swooning.The team of Lee Hanson and Riad Nasr, the founding chefs of Balthazar and Minetta Tavern, have ushered in a new era at Le Veau d'Or which offers a prix-fixe menu reverential to classic French cuisine. Pâté en croûte is among the greatest hits, as is the golden-roasted poulet à l'estragon with an unapologetically buttery sauce flecked with tarragon. A small salad arrives after the entree to cleanse the palate, paving the way for sweets, such as a warm gratin au chocolat.

restaurant.Name: LeYou
restaurant.Address: 1100 N. First St., Ste. C., San Jose, CA, 95112, USA
restaurant.Description: LeYou is an ode to contemporary Ethiopia, where the dining room is filled with tall, leafy greenery, tables are topped with burlap coffee bags tucked under thick glass, and artwork adorns the walls. Dynamic chef/co-owner Aida Taye offers a lighter, unique approach to Ethiopian cuisine, as in a kifto that substitutes lean tuna for beef. Kick off the meal with kategna, an injera toasted to a crisp, doused with chili powder and served with a sour cream/yogurt dip. A vegetable platter includes your choice from gomen, or chopped collard greens; atakilt, a tender stew of cabbage, potatoes and carrots; fossolia, or green beans stewed with carrots, turmeric, tomato and onions; and azifa selat'a, refreshing green lentils tossed in lemon juice and hot mustard vinaigrette.

restaurant.Name: Leche de Tigre
restaurant.Address: 318 E. Cevallos St., San Antonio, TX, 78204, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: A ceviche bar, a cocktail menu full of pisco sours, and a cute patio? What’s not to like? This colorful hotspot is buzzing for good reason. Driven by the owners' time spent growing up in Peru, this little bungalow emphasizes seafood dressed up in bright, zippy, punchy flavors. Striped bass with ginger leche de tigre thrives with the clever addition of plantains and huacatay oil. Scallops set in a sharp parmesan leche de tigre are paired with capers and garlic chips. Tostadas come piled high with yellowfin tuna tossed with Nikkei ponzu and showered with crispy leeks. Break from the sea with lomo saltado, a bold effort thanks to an umami-packed sauce that coats seared beef tenderloin, crispy-fried potatoes and charred scallions.

restaurant.Name: Lei
restaurant.Address: 15-17 Doyers St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: In the beating heart of Chinatown on Doyers Street, Annie Shi’s little wine bar is a gift to the city. Rare wines are everywhere. They line the edges of the room, and they fill countless boxes stacked to the ceiling. People are everywhere, too, sitting elbow to elbow and even spilling out onto tables in the alley. This talented team doesn’t waste a single square inch of space – and that includes the kitchen, which turns out smart, thoughtful modern Chinese dishes. Chilled celtuce with shallots and red wine vinegar is an essential starter. Other hits include fried whiting with seaweed, scallops with lily buds and ginger, and hand-rolled noodles with braised lamb.

restaurant.Name: Len Len
restaurant.Address: 40 E. 20th St., New York, NY, 10003, USA
restaurant.Description: Behind a modest Flatiron storefront, LenLen opens into a lively dining room inspired by 1970s Bangkok shophouses, complete with vintage televisions, family photographs and retro touches. The cocktail program is as thoughtful as the kitchen, turning out bright, aromatic drinks that pair naturally with the food. The menu draws from a range of Thai traditions while embracing modern influences. Highlights include a beef tartare larb wrapped in endive and perilla leaves, and a rich crab curry that balances sweetness, spice and coconut milk with surprising finesse. Open late, LenLen feels equally suited for dinner or a spontaneous night out.

restaurant.Name: Lenoir
restaurant.Address: 1807 S. 1st St., Austin, TX, 78704, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Inside this cozy whitewashed bungalow, find a gem of a place with a sprinkling of tables and a few seats at the bar. These tiny digs turn out big, impressive dishes. The farm-to-table menu is one of the most creative around and changes every six weeks or so. Owners Todd Duplechan and Jessica Maher tempt guests with seasonally shifting dishes available as an a la carte or a multicourse chef's tasting. Served family style but focused on a different global theme, a recent menu spotlighted French Cajun cooking with the likes of pan-roasted cobia with cremini mushrooms, andouille duck with dirty rice cake and gumbo espagnole, plus caramelized banana pudding to finish.

restaurant.Name: Lenox Sophia
restaurant.Address: 87 A St., Boston, MA, 02127, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Bring your own bottle,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: On a quiet corner in South Boston in a dining room the size of a postage stamp, Chef Shi Mei offers an experience that’s about as intimate as they come. You will not find a fleet of servers, expensive plates and cutlery, or lavish decorations. This is not the place for pampering. What you will find is a chef who openly engages customers and cooks with a refined casualness that often takes you by surprise. Both the meat and vegetarian tasting menus yield a handful of courses that do not hew to one particular region or cuisine. Highlights like scallop crudo with rose, rutabaga soup with truffle, and parsnip panna cotta change with the seasons. Bring your own wine, share glasses with a nearby table, and enjoy the night on your own terms.

restaurant.Name: Leo's House of Thirst
restaurant.Address: 1055 Haywood Rd., Asheville, NC, 28806, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Leo's House of Thirst is the sort of place we all want in our neighborhoods. This wine bar feels like your coolest friend's living room, livened up with books, wine bottles and plants. Inside, there’s a small bar with seating, plus a patio outside with tables and umbrellas.Stop in during the day for a cup of coffee and a breakfast sandwich or swing by at night for a glass of wine and a meal. Mornings are met with the likes of avocado toast and a beef short rib hash, while come evening, it's oysters, crudos and tartares, along with heartier options like chicken and pasta.

restaurant.Name: Leona’s Sushi House
restaurant.Address: 11814 Ventura Blvd., Studio City, CA, 91604, USA
restaurant.Description: Some places have great ambience. Others have terrific food. Think you can't find both in the same spot? Think again, then head to Leona's Sushi House. This hip spot has a variety of distinctive spaces that lure creative types and beautiful people. This Japanese fusion menu never misses a beat. Dishes are often irreverent, as in rich and savory udon carbonara with paper thin smoked pork belly, creamy egg and parmigiano; and the sticky-sweet oxtail-stuffed bao is craveworthy. Seafood is impressive, whether it's ceviche or sashimi-quality halibut bathed in a ponzu sauce vinaigrette. Chef's specials include shimeji risotto or whole baked branzino with sake.

restaurant.Name: Les Petites Canailles
restaurant.Address: 1215 Spring St., Paso Robles, CA, 93446, USA
restaurant.Description: Courtney and Julien Asseo have named this Paso Robles restaurant in honor of their three children (the name translates to "the little rascals") but this welcoming spot with a spot-on kitchen is more head of the class than detention bound. Set smack in the heart of downtown, the space's pressed concrete floors, simple furnishings and Edison lights read contemporary. Meals begin with a warm gougère before moving on to a selection of hearty appetizers. The menu features several entrées, though most eyes land on the perfectly cooked steaks. Leeks à la plancha, served on an oversized platter, are grilled, covered with an herb vinaigrette and finished with flaky salt, Espelette pepper and toasted pine nuts for a simple, yet refined dish.

restaurant.Name: Levant BBQ
restaurant.Address: 5884 Westheimer Rd., Houston, TX, 77057, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Mohamad Kharboutli grew up cooking in Aleppo before spending years running Mediterranean restaurants across Moscow, Jordan and Houston. Here at Levant BBQ, he blends Central Texas barbecue with Levantine flavors, incorporating spices like cardamom, Aleppo pepper, and ginger into their rubs while smoking everything over post oak. Lamb neck, lamb chops or lamb leg are some of the more unusual finds, or go with classic barbecue staples like beef ribs or brisket — you can't go wrong either way. And don't even think about skipping the sides, with fried okra or a smoked potato finished with cheddar and sour cream calling your name.

restaurant.Name: Lewis Barbecue
restaurant.Address: 464 N. Nassau St., Charleston, SC, 29403, USA
restaurant.Description: Smoke drifts through the gravel courtyard, stacks of firewood tower beside the smokers, and picnic tables fill with trays of Central Texas-style barbecue. At this bustling operation from pitmaster John Lewis, meats are sold by the pound and sliced to order, with brisket leading the way alongside house-made sausages, smoked turkey, and traditional sides like green chili corn pudding and potato salad. By this point, few will have room for dessert, but perhaps consider ordering a banana pudding. It’s worth the extra bite. It’s a lively, casual spot that has become a Charleston staple.

restaurant.Name: Liberty
restaurant.Address: 12995 S. Cleveland Ave., Ste. 112, Fort Myers, FL, 33907, USA
restaurant.Description: Aptly named, this Fort Myers restaurant is hidden away in an unremarkable strip center. With burners on full blast and music turned way up, Chef Bob Boye is front and center cooking at warp speed and engaging customers seated right before him at the counter. The menu doesn’t align itself with any one cuisine or style, and the inspiration seems at the whim of the chef and his merry band of rebels. Plates are designed to be shared so order without restraint. Think shrimp toast with sweet chili, smoked wagyu beef cheek with peanut nuoc cham and steak tartare with “bone-mayo.”

restaurant.Name: Liholiho Yacht Club
restaurant.Address: 871 Sutter St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
restaurant.Description: Although not quite the impossible-to-book hotspot it was at its peak, this lively spot still has plenty of enthusiasts. Combining Californian technique with the flavors of Chef/owner Ravi Kapur’s native Hawaii, this airy space is known for strong cocktails and shareable plates. Pivoted around a large, open kitchen, the dining room hums with groups savoring the likes of halibut kinilaw with macadamia nuts and scarlet grapes, or fried game hen with sweet & sour glaze. If you turn your nose up at Spam, consider sampling the house-made version, featured in a dish of kimchi and mushroom fried rice.

restaurant.Name: Lilac
restaurant.Address: The Tampa EDITION, 500 Channelside Dr., Tampa, FL, 33602, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: This concept from John Fraser occupies its own corner of the sleek and stylish Tampa EDITION hotel. An open kitchen with glossy emerald-green tile overlooks the small dining room and delivers a contemporary prix-fixe with broad Mediterranean influences. Dinner begins with a series of bites, including French onion pull-apart bread topped with slow-cooked onions. Grilled Spanish octopus tails set with seared pork belly rest atop a succotash base made with stewed corn, white beans and 'nduja for a particular delightful entree before a classic baba au rhum. A lengthy list of cocktails and rather pricey wines are available as well.-

restaurant.Name: Ling Kitchen
restaurant.Address: 8423 Research Blvd., Austin, TX, 78758, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Ling Qi Wu is known in Austin for several restaurants, but Ling Kitchen offers something considerably more personal. Hosted inside the commissary kitchen that supports her restaurant group, this intimate communal dining experience invites guests directly into the heart of the operation for a tasting menu that blends Chinese culinary traditions with playful presentations and luxury ingredients. Dishes like the Water Lilies Goldfish Soup, featuring delicate seafood dumplings served in a clear broth, show both technical precision and a sense of whimsy, while crisp pork belly with fermented red tofu sauce demonstrates a more restrained approach. Throughout the meal, familiar flavors are reimagined through elaborate presentations.

restaurant.Name: Little Betty Steak Bar
restaurant.Address: 321 Rele St., Mountain Brook, AL, 35223, USA
restaurant.Description: Handsome and high energy, this modern steakhouse in Mountain Brook can do no wrong. Cushy banquettes, a long marble bar, tables draped in white tablecloth, a glass-enclosed wine cellar, and wood-trim all around set the stage as everyone arrives dressed for a proper night out. Most importantly, the restaurant cooks as good as it looks. One could make a full meal out of starters like wagyu croquettes or housemade pastas like ricotta tortellini. Finely marbled wood-grilled steaks arrive with proper sears and must be flanked by a superb side of creamed corn baked with a polenta crust. Service is at once professional, personable, and relaxed.

restaurant.Name: Little Bull
restaurant.Address: 301 E. Chapel Hill St., Durham, NC, 27701, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Blending his experience cooking across America with his Mexican heritage, Chef Oscar Diaz has created his own style of cooking. His time on the West Coast is evident and best seen in the vibrant and fresh small and larger plates designed for sharing. Judicious spicing and an array of textures add to the allure of these dishes, and house recommendations include the al pastor skewer and the tom kha ceviche. Really hungry? Tuck into the half chicken with pita for a satisfying meal. It's all better paired with one of their very cold beers or a house cocktail.

restaurant.Name: Little Em’s Oyster Bar
restaurant.Address: 1024 S. Alamo St., San Antonio, TX, 78210, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Cute as a button, this breezy seafood hangout is dressed head to toe in cupcake-pink and white frosting. A spacious patio deck doubles the size of the dining room and is shaded by surrounding trees. The menu matches the décor, starting with a revolving selection of oysters and moving into light and bright preparations of seafood and salads. It is hard to imagine stopping by and not ordering fish tacos or, even better, a lobster roll served with herbed fries. A glass of rosé completes this summery daydream.

restaurant.Name: Little Mama's
restaurant.Address: 4521 Sharon Rd., Charlotte, NC, 28211, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Don't have an Italian grandmother? Then head to Little Mama's, where you can sit at the counter, slide into a booth or find a seat in the main room and watch as they make their own mozzarella. This is a kitchen that takes a few prime ingredients and turns them into something special, with homemade pasta and pizza, as well as entrees. Begin with a salad or some of their house-made mozzarella or stracciatella and add a few of the suggested accompaniments to fill your own crostini before twirling your fork into a plate of pasta or tucking into meat or fish. Lasagna filled with ground beef, veal and pork and layered with ricotta is pure comfort. Brunch is available on the weekend.

restaurant.Name: Little Mountain
restaurant.Address: 516 San Ysidro Rd., Montecito, CA, 93108, USA
restaurant.Description: Chilean-born Chef Diego Moya cut his teeth working in kitchens around the globe before opening Little Mountain in Montecito. The rustic yet elegant dining room draws inspiration from the region's Spanish Colonial history, with tall, white walls, brick floors and wood beams. The intimate ambience makes it a natural fit for date night; be sure to make reservations (though the bar accepts walk-ins). Meanwhile, the menu uses local ingredients to tell a globally inspired story. To begin, a tile fish ceviche with yuzu kosho and sweet peppers is a perfect choice. It's hard to go wrong with any of their main dishes, but their Mt. Lassen trout with wild mushrooms and beurre blanc is a strong choice. Cherimoya panna cotta is the perfect conclusion.

restaurant.Name: Little Sparrow
restaurant.Address: 1198 Howell Mill Rd., Atlanta, GA, 30318, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking
restaurant.Description: We'll forgive you if you're looking through rose-colored glasses after a meal here. After all, Little Sparrow was singer Édith Piaf's nickname, and this très French bistro hits all the right notes from its design to its dishes. The menu, though compact, features all the favorites. Meals begin with a warm baguette and delicious butter before moving on to a fragrant and hearty onion soup and beef tartare. Entrées run the gamut from pork belly to chicken schnitzel with a mound of seasonal greens. Of course, there must be fries, and these house-made delights are thick cut and triple fried, accompanied by aïoli, Bearnaise sauce, or Raclette cheese service. End with a traditional chocolate soufflé or opt for a unique soft serve sundae.

restaurant.Name: Little Water
restaurant.Address: 261 S. 20th St., Philadelphia, PA, 19103, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This airy, seafood-inspired restaurant from husband-and-wife team Chef Randy and Amanda Rucker immediately charms with its pressed tin ceiling, globe lights and well-worn wood flooring. The menu is tight, starting with a raw bar of oysters, shrimp cocktail and scallops. Seafood gumbo arrives with lobster, crab and Carolina gold rice, and Caesar salads are showered in nori and toasted benne. Heartier fare like fried oyster BLTs and applewood-smoked steelhead trout show care, quality and sophistication. A seat at the raw bar in the back offers an up-close view of chefs in action.

restaurant.Name: Locanda Brasato
restaurant.Address: 270 Rele St., Mountain Brook, AL, 35223, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: With soaring ceilings, exposed red brick, and bright orange banquettes, this airy Italian restaurant in Mountain Brook takes a fresh look at the classic pasta and pizza genre. The menu is constantly evolving, moving with the seasons and reflecting the latest crops from local purveyors. Past highlights include whipped ricotta with smoked tomato pesto and a crisp pizza laden with zucchini, lemon, and parmesan. Pastas like short rib ravioli with caramelized onions or the classic spaghetti carbonara are made-in house. Tiramisu or a scoop of gelato will end the meal on a lovely, sweet note.

restaurant.Name: Lord's
restaurant.Address: 506 LaGuardia Pl., New York, NY, 10012, USA
restaurant.Description: It feels straight out of London at this meat-centric restaurant with a nose to tail ethos from Chef Ed Szymanski and Patricia Howard, the partners behind smash hit, Dame. It's ever so charming, with cozy nooks and banquettes, and even when it's packed, the bar maintains space for walk-ins. Come on a cold day for hearty English classics with a touch of creativity (think curried lamb scotch egg). Like most of the dishes, duck-stuffed cabbage with mashed potatoes could feed an army, so order shared plates-style to sample without becoming stuffed. The apple and calvados trifle closes things out with just the right note of sweetness.

restaurant.Name: Los Agaves
restaurant.Address: 600 N. Milpas St., Santa Barbara, CA, 93101, USA
restaurant.Description: Note: Temporarily closedServing generous portions of hearty south-of-the-border favorites by way of California, along with a relaxed, family-friendly vibe, this place deserves every bit of praise lavished upon it. The staff may bring chips immediately to your table, but salsa and drinks are both self-service. Remember to order at the counter and collect a number before taking a seat. Start with the likes of lime-marinated halibut ceviche tostada with cilantro and avocado. Then pick from a variety of sizeable burritos or go for the satisfyingly cheesy and crispy costra taco al pastor, with pineapple, marinated pork, and chipotle—enlivened with pickled onions.There may be four locations, but this one is the original. The room can get crowded, so takeaway is a popular option.

restaurant.Name: Los Burritos Juárez
restaurant.Address: 354 Myrtle Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Los Burritos Juarez is a compact Fort Greene shop serving burritos in the border style of El Paso and Ciudad Juárez. The foundation is its house-made flour tortillas, cooked to order with lard, yielding wraps that are soft, warm and pleasantly chewy. They encase generous guisados, or slow-cooked stews, such as pork simmered in red chiles or brisket braised in a mellow salsa verde, finished with a swipe of pinto beans that brings the components together. The menu is concise and the flavors are deeply comforting, offering a regional burrito tradition rarely found in New York. Breakfast burritos are available from opening until they sell out.

restaurant.Name: Los Fuegos by Francis Mallmann
restaurant.Address: Faena Hotel Miami Beach, 3201 Collins Ave., Miami Beach, FL, 33140, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: “Theatrical” barely begins to describe the scale and style of Francis Mallman’s restaurant set inside the FAENA Hotel. Much like the hotel itself, the director of Moulin Rouge is responsible for such décor elements as leopard-print booths, striking red-cushioned seats and flashes of gold that appear on everything from the bar to the carpet.Known for open-fire cooking, Chef Mallman is not outmatched by the room’s design, delivering an asado experience that rivals the city’s best steakhouses. Beets buried under coals for eight hours and festooned with pistachio yogurt and garlic chips are a must, followed by big proteins like Australian filet that's grilled, coated in breadcrumbs and fried.The bustling bar at the end of the room draws a stylish crowd.

restaurant.Name: Lotus Noodle Bar
restaurant.Address: 56 Grove Ave., St. Augustine, FL, 32084, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Lotus Noodle Bar began as a series of pop-ups from chef/owner Barry Honan and finally landed its brick-and-mortar spot in St. Augustine in 2023. It's a welcoming space with several different seating options, including a noodle bar. As expected, noodles are indeed the main event but kick off the meal with the sweet and spicy sunomono, made with cucumber and miso cashews, before slurping those namesake noodles. One worthy of consideration is the spicy Maple Leaf Farms duck tan tan ramen, with sesame Sichuan coconut broth made with three-month Kyoto white miso. To finish, try the NYC Dreams, with white chocolate mousse with a red rice aged sake and cherry reduction sauce sprinkled with brown butter sable crumble and a quenelle of caviar.

restaurant.Name: Lou Mitchell's
restaurant.Address: 565 W. Jackson Blvd., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Strategically set near Union Station, this beloved diner has stood the test of time. Open since 1923, locals and visitors alike have scooched into booths and sat at the bar for homey comfort food that never promises to be more than what it is. Eggs, waffles, and pancakes come prepared in a dizzying number of ways. There are all sorts of salads and sandwiches; try the La Conga Delight (cheese, bacon, tomato) or the hearty open-faced Reuben on homemade rye and served with a hot stack of thick-cut steak fries. Servers roam the floor with hot coffee and complimentary donut holes. Especially after a long night, such simple pleasures go a long way.

restaurant.Name: Lovers Pizzeria
restaurant.Address: 105 E. Ashby Pl., San Antonio, TX, 78212, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Expect a line at this popular neighborhood pizzeria, where pre-ordering a pie is often the best way to guarantee your dinner. Opened by husband-and-wife team Victoria Moreno and Dusty Dworak, Lovers specializes in 16-inch pizzas built on naturally leavened sourdough that is made fresh daily. The crust is the highlight: blistered, airy and pleasantly tangy from fermentation. Classic options like cheese, vodka and white pies share the menu with Texas-inspired creations such as the poblano pizza, while toppings range from pepperoni and house-made sausage to roasted jalapenos, confit garlic and spicy syrup. The commitment to local ingredients is evident throughout, resulting in pizzas that balance East Coast influences with a distinctly Central Texas point of view.

restaurant.Name: Lowland
restaurant.Address: The Pinch Hotel, 36 George St., Charleston, SC, 29401, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Find Lowland just off busy King Street in a two-story brick former residence across from the boutique Pinch hotel. The first floor is home to a buzzy bar room and casual dining space, while upstairs is a bit more formal. Come for comfort food like the tavern burger with fries and a cognac sauce. The range of entrees feature grilled local fish and squid-ink tinted pasta shells neatly tossed with a luscious rouille-inspired sauce stocked with rock shrimp and little neck clams. Elevated comfort continues through dessert with house-made hand pies with a seasonal fruit filling and vanilla-infused whipped cream.---

restaurant.Name: Lucia
restaurant.Address: 287 N. Bishop Ave., Dallas, TX, 75208, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Husband-and-wife owners David and Jennifer Uygur have built a beloved Bishop Arts destination, where David leads the kitchen and Jennifer welcomes guests with genuine warmth. Reservations are often in high demand, though a handful of seats are typically held for walk-ins. Chef Uygur’s cooking is rooted in Italian traditions and shaped by the availability of seasonal Texas produce. The menu shifts regularly, with house-made pastas and cured meats forming the backbone of the offering. Dishes favor clarity and comfort over excess, allowing quality ingredients and careful technique to take center stage. A thoughtfully assembled wine list, with a strong focus on Italian bottles, rounds out the experience.

restaurant.Name: Lucia Restaurant & Bar
restaurant.Address: Bernardus Lodge & Spa, 415 W. Carmel Valley Rd., Carmel Valley, CA, 93924, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: This dining room in the luxe Bernardus Lodge & Spa boasts its own garden, which provides many of the superb ingredients, and is proof of the kitchen’s dedication to local and seasonal food. It might show a talent and focus on vegetables, but highlights from the nightly menu as well as à la carte may include brilliantly tender lamb, served as medallions of deboned ribeye with rosemary jus on a bed of sautéed greens.There is a casual feel to the upscale lodge-like interior, with its large fireplace and muted colors. It's located just off the lobby but draws diners from well beyond mere hotel guests. The view alone, overlooking the Carmel Valley and Bernardus vineyards, may be worth a visit. Better yet, come on a sunny day and dine alfresco on the patio.

restaurant.Name: Lucky Star
restaurant.Address: 1050 Howell Mill Rd., Ste. 110, Atlanta, GA, 30318, USA
restaurant.Description: Lucky Star, located inside the lobby of Atlanta’s Star Metals office complex, is a two-in-one concept kitted out with green velvet couches and a stylish appeal. By day, it's a café pouring coffee and serving pastries and Taiwanese fare. Then, when the sun goes down, it flips into a cocktail bar with a focused à la carte menu. Breakfast sandwiches, noodles, French toast and house-made pastries make appearances on the brunch menu, while oyster omelets and rice bowls, along with a small but fun dessert section that includes mochi “dumplings” and a strawberry cheesecake cookie, show up throughout the day. A house-made scallion pancake stuffed with braised beef shank is a tasty treat any time of day.

restaurant.Name: Lulu
restaurant.Address: 10899 Wilshire Blvd., Los Angeles, CA, 90024, USA
restaurant.Description: Think dining at a museum requires toting a silver tray? Meet Lulu. This charming restaurant may be nestled within a courtyard at the Hammer Museum, but there's nothing ho-hum about it. Helmed by David Tanis with a little help from none other than Alice Waters, Lulu rewards guests who take a midday break from grokking the art. Fresh produce on display is more than just a design element; it's a hint at the philosophy of this spot, where the three-course and à la carte menus shift daily.Solid cooking leans heavily into the seasons while letting the ingredients shine. Dishes are a moving target, but a recent meal of blood orange citrus salad, chicken saltimbocca and Meyer lemon gelato proves that hyper-seasonal and local always steal the show.

restaurant.Name: Lumière
restaurant.Address: Fairmont Century Plaza Los Angeles at Beverly Hills, 2025 Avenue Of The Stars, Los Angeles, CA, 90067, USA
restaurant.Description: Nestled inside the Fairmont Century Plaza, Lumière is a relaxed brasserie-styled spot for French-inspired cooking. Friendly staff are on hand to offer guidance and share their favorite selections, but you'll certainly want to indulge in a variety of classics like fruits de mer and steak frites, if only for the delicious fries. Start things off right by ordering the velvety chicken liver mousse served with an olive jam, or sample the Bayonne, Fermin Iberico or five year-aged Iberico hams from the charcuterie menu. Seared sea bass is plated with a delicious onion soubise for a pleasing main dish. Then for dessert, you'll never go wrong with crème brûlée with its pure vanilla flavor and nutty caramelized crust.

restaurant.Name: Lunch
restaurant.Address: 24 University Ave., Sewanee, TN, 37375, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Lunch is an inviting operation run by Chef Mallory Tubbs and boasts a country store charm that's thoroughly authentic. The structure dates back to the 1930s, and features cream walls and wainscotting, a variety of wood tables, and displays of local vegetables, jams and honey, and dry goods. This Sewanee operation lives up to its name, open from morning to afternoon and serving a concise menu featuring products from local farms that may offer up the likes of seasonal salads, huevos rancheros or a steak sandwich on house-made baguette with Gruyère, tender peppers and onions, and chimichurri sauce. Be sure to save room for one (or more) of the freshly baked pastries, say a wedge of zucchini cake with buttermilk glaze.

restaurant.Name: Lung Yai Thai Tapas
restaurant.Address: 1731 S.W. 8th St., Miami, FL, 33135, USA
restaurant.Description: You could drive down the street a dozen times and still overlook this intimate little nook that hides in plain sight. Little Havana is certainly an unexpected place to find one of the city’s hottest Thai kitchens, but the long waits are an indication (no reservations) that Chef/owner Veenuthri Trisransri knows what he’s doing. On a menu that mixes typical standbys with Northern specialties, begin with an order of homemade dumplings with a pork or shrimp filling, served steamed or fried. Khao Soi, a coconut-based curry with your choice of protein, bobs with egg noodles and has a rich, creamy profile without too much heat. Tables, plates and even the place itself is small, so order ambitiously and be prepared for a kitchen that sends out dishes faster than you can finish them.

restaurant.Name: Lutie's
restaurant.Address: Commodore Perry Estate, Auberge Collection, 4100 Red River St., Austin, TX, 78751, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Located within the landmark Commodore Perry Estate, Lutie’s is a grand space done in a green and gold palette with windows overlooking a stunning patio with gardens and a fountain. Now helmed by Executive Chef Jakub Czyszczon, with Susana Querejazu overseeing the pastry program, the restaurant offers seasonally inspired cooking with a strong Texas sensibility. Estate bread comes with brown and cultured butter, while vegetables feature prominently in dishes such as brassicas with guajillo and pecan or grilled beets with black garlic and dill. Larger plates might include Yonderway pork with creamer peas, market fish with Delta Blues rice and smoked trout roe, or Texas beef with radish, marrow, and sweet potato.

restaurant.Name: Lutèce
restaurant.Address: 1522 Wisconsin Ave. NW, Washington, DC, 20007, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: With bottles of wine lining the shelves above, the dining room at this delightful Georgetown bistro is a charming, date-night oasis, thanks to exposed brick, hardwood floors and a pressed-tin ceiling. Not far behind the décor, the seasonal menu is tight knit, offering only a handful of appetizers and mains that could change on a moment’s notice. The kitchen team turns out an impressive array of cleverly rendered hits, like hand-cut fluke tartare with green strawberry, granny smith apple and marigold, or duck breast with duck sausage, cherries and bigarade. For dessert, consider the honey semifreddo with honeycomb and 18-month-aged Comté cheese. Organic and biodynamic wines comprise the list, and thoughtfully crafted cocktails are equally tempting.

restaurant.Name: Luyu Dumplings
restaurant.Address: 17980 Castleton St., City of Industry, CA, 91748, USA
restaurant.Description: This bare-bones operation hides in the back of a shopping center in City of Industry. The space is Spartan and deadly quiet, except for the sound of the refrigerators that hum constantly and the steady chop-chop of a chef’s knife in the nearby kitchen. If you want anything to drink, including water, you have to ask, and if you have questions about the menu, you’re better off looking at the poster of dishes on the wall. All to say, this humble restaurant is short on creature comforts but delivers admirably in the realm of excellent, handmade dumplings and bowls of chewy noodles glossed in scallion oil. From lamb with fennel to chicken with celery, dumplings come with a multitude of fillings, but the tender ground pork with lotus root win.

restaurant.Name: Ly Ly Vietnam Cookhouse
restaurant.Address: 306 E. 81st St., New York, NY, 10028, USA
restaurant.Description: Orange-and-white checkered floors, mustard-colored booths, and paper mâché flowers suspended from the ceiling—this Upper East Side spot is just plain charming. It's the kind of place you want to drop in on a cold winter's night to boost your mood but don't let the whimsical vibe fool you, as the Vietnamese dishes are seriously good. The concise offerings range from rolls and appetizers to larger plates like shaking beef. Kick off a meal with a plate of crispy spring rolls filled with pork, mushrooms, and glass noodles before moving on to a Vietnamese crepe with pork belly and nuoc mam sauce. Of course, pho is a must and the "UES" bowl doesn't disappoint with its complex 20-hour broth and meltingly tender five-spice smoked short rib.

restaurant.Name: Lyla Lila
restaurant.Address: 693 Peachtree St. NE, Ste. 118, Atlanta, GA, 30308, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: It bears repeating that Chef/owner Craig Richards' Lyla Lila is a good find in the heart of midtown. Sharing a contemporary design with a darker, moody color palette, the restaurant is divided into several rooms, starting with a handsome curved bar up front and a sunlit dining room further in. The kitchen follows the seasons and puts pasta as a key focal point. House staples include crispy duck lasagna with a cocoa béchamel, as well as roast chicken or snapper with pistachio pesto. Everything is scaled for sharing, down to dessert. Rotating flavors of gelato and sorbet or perhaps a wedge of tiramisu will close out the meal nicely.

restaurant.Name: L’abeille à Côté
restaurant.Address: 412 Greenwich St., New York, NY, 10013, USA
restaurant.Description: This jewel box of a restaurant is something of a rarity, as small dining rooms with even smaller menus are hard to come by these days. A chic operation with handsome wood floors and tables, marble finishes, and a French-Japanese cooking style, the restaurant exudes intimacy and quality. The menu is a friendly one, boasting an izakaya-like casualness, high-quality ingredients, and noteworthy prices. Think yakitori skewers with black garlic or a strikingly good strip loin served with barbecue sauce. A recent fried fish sandwich featuring mahi mahi arrived outlandishly sized – and beautifully executed. Those interested in a more elaborate and involved experience should consider the sister restaurant, l’abeille, next door.

restaurant.Name: MARKET Restaurant + Bar
restaurant.Address: 3702 Via De La Valle, Del Mar, CA, 92014, USA
restaurant.Description: This restaurant's creative cooking continues to draw patrons for both special occasions as well as date night. The dark and seductive décor manages to be elegant without a hint of pretense, but one glance at the parking lot and you know that this spot is favored by a moneyed lot. Sushi is well-loved here, but it would be a shame to miss the chef’s creative and internationally influenced dishes. For instance, blue cheese soufflé with anise-orange marmalade shows off a European bent, while miso-glazed cod with shrimp dumplings is resoundingly Asian.

restaurant.Name: MP Taverna
restaurant.Address: 1 Bridge St., Irvington, NY, 10533, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Michael Psilakis puts the "MP" in this taverna, serving his modern interpretation of Greek cuisine. Just steps from Hudson River, enter through the sleek bar area to arrive inside this 18th-century structure, with rustic brass chandeliers, mahogany panels, and neutral hues mixed with pops of blue. Whether seated at a booth, banquette or table, diners can count on family-style plates.Start with meze, like tzatziki imbued with fresh dill, before savoring mains like gently roasted chicken sporting perfectly crisp skin or aged grilled sausage with a hint of orange peel. Desserts, too, flaunt a contemporary twist, as in a whopping slice of galaktoboureko. Groups should go for the the chef's whole roast animal, but call ahead as it takes time to prep.

restaurant.Name: Macchialina
restaurant.Address: 810 Alton Rd., Miami Beach, FL, 33139, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Locals and residents are devout fans of this cozy spot, filling the space nightly. The setting features tufted leather banquettes tailed by a charming covered patio area. The bar is graciously attended to and pours an almost all-Italian wine list that's bolstered by house-infused grappa in flavors like chai tea and chamomile.The menu is concise, so it's easy for diners to focus on the best attributes of this kitchen team—that largely being the house-made pasta. Think of supple strands of spaghetti slicked with pomodoro sauce or cacio e pepe. Other highlights include the hearty veal parmigiana. But make sure you save room for the tiramisu—given a distinct Miami accent with dulce de leche-sweetened cream and a sea salt-sprinkled cap of espresso granita.

restaurant.Name: Mad Dogs & Englishmen
restaurant.Address: 4914 S. MacDill Ave., Tampa, FL, 33611, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Credit cards not accepted,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Mad Dogs & Englishmen isn't exactly new—the previous iteration down the street opened in 1991—but this new standalone space is bigger and better with a proper English pub style. Inside is a warren of small rooms, along with a bar and a large conservatory that opens up on nice days. In classic style, the walls are appropriately loaded with all manner of British paraphernalia, and the food follows suit, with a litany of traditional offerings including a weekly Sunday roast. Tuck into a puff pastry-wrapped sausage with a tangy curry-Dijon mayo. Shepherd's pie is a must in any pub, but here it's made with tender lamb. Topped with mashed potatoes and finished with breadcrumbs, it's a solid if slightly unique take on a classic.

restaurant.Name: Madeira Park
restaurant.Address: Otto's Apartment Hotel, 640 N. Highland Ave. NE, Atlanta, GA, 30306, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This stylish place in Atlanta's Poncey-Highland neighborhood is first and foremost a wine bar, so expect an impressive and interesting list with a wide variety of reserve wines and even a section for aged Madeira, but with Chef Ollie Honderd in charge of the kitchen, the food is far from an afterthought. Take a seat indoors or out to enjoy a buzzy vibe along with a variety of shareable dishes sporting a seasonal, contemporary flair. Start with a smattering of snacks from olives and ham and cheese beignets to crispy panisse or a selection of cheese, while in the evenings, full plates like bistro steak and seared tilefish over black lentils are on offer. No matter the choice, it all works. Vanilla semifreddo with melon granita and rosemary shortbread is a bright and refreshing finish.

restaurant.Name: Madeline
restaurant.Address: 1313 E. 6th Ave., Denver, CO, 80218, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef-owner Quincy Cherrett has designed a focused, seasonally minded menu at Madeline. Step inside to this warm and inviting space, where wood floors, dark walls and low lighting set a relaxed tone. Cherrett's contemporary American cooking winks at a French bistro influence while also weaving in Japanese, Thai and other global influences. This is a place to order with abandon, as the plates are small and designed for sharing. Begin with items like their tom yum toast on milk bread with shrimp, charred tomato and fish sauce vinaigrette before a plate of house-made summer corn agnolotti or pasta pomodoro. Halibut served over forbidden rice with shaved zucchini and squash is finished tableside with a spicy green curry sauce.

restaurant.Name: Madera
restaurant.Address: Rosewood Sand Hill, 2825 Sand Hill Rd., Menlo Park, CA, 94025, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Garden or park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Enveloped in the luxury of the Rosewood Sand Hill hotel, this elegant retreat boasts vaulted ceilings, a crackling fireplace, and a stunning backdrop of the Santa Cruz Mountains—think Silicon Valley meets Swiss chalet. Affluent techies clad in Patagonia vests flock here for the tranquil, sophisticated ambience and uncomplicated, ingredient-driven dishes that emerge from a grand open kitchen. An efficient power lunch might consist of a salad or a sandwich (think Dungeness crab and avocado roll) while dinner highlights the likes of house-made pastas and hearty steaks. In both cases, simplicity reigns, with local products placed front and center. An almond wood-fired grill is used liberally to lend a subtle, smoky savor.

restaurant.Name: Madre
restaurant.Address: Franklin Guesthouse, 214 Franklin St., Brooklyn, NY, 11222, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Madre sits at the base of the boutique Franklin Guest House, where industrial elements meet modern elegance. Make your way past stunning carved doors to arrive at the hotel—the restaurant has a separate entrance. Here, diners will find it hard to resist the kitchen team's sensational and contemporary cooking. Dishes that take center stage in this multi-level space include jalepeño cornbread madelines with a housemade whipped honey butter, or tender octopus plated with romesco, green chorizo, nopales and escabeche for a plate that straddles the Mediterranean and Latin America. From there, indulge in couscous with chickpeas, harissa, red peppers and a smoked onion broth. Pot de crème with Mast Brothers chocolate and Maldon sea salt is worth your undivided attention.

restaurant.Name: Main Street Meats
restaurant.Address: 217 E. Main St., Chattanooga, TN, 37408, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: The name truly says it all. Located on Main Street in Chattanooga, this spot is indeed all about meat. It's equal parts butcher shop and restaurant, and their whole animal butchery mindset is reflected on the menu. House-made sausages and boudin made with pork and rice and served with house-made crackers are a perfect introduction before meat-forward mains like a burger and a selection of steaks. There's a cut for everyone here, and each one arrives with perfect grill marks and house-made tallow fries. Need something green? Order a side of bok choy or broccoli before indulging in chocolate gelato or the crostada. At lunch, fried bologna and a Reuben sandwich entice.

restaurant.Name: Maison Bar à Vins
restaurant.Address: 1834 Columbia Rd. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.Description: Located in a multi-level brownstone in Adams Morgan, this stunning restaurant from the Popal Group is chic and contemporary yet manages to feel cozy and welcoming. Chef Matt Conroy heads the kitchen, delivering an à la carte that is seasonally minded, French-inspired and tightly edited. Most dishes are meant for sharing and nothing is overwrought. While the menu reads a bit like a bistro, the dishes are leveled up, featuring precise technique, vibrant flavor and unexpected twists. Case in point? A small bowl is set with whipped crème fraîche layered with diced steelhead trout, green strawberry, edible flower petals and a veil of grilled strawberry gelee. It's a gorgeous opener that sets the tone for a memorable meal. Creste di Gallo, or rooster crest-shaped pasta, is tossed with ramps, clams and toasted breadcrumbs with Aleppo pepper for a dialed-in dish. To finish, homemade almond ice cream with a rhubarb compote may sound simple but it's bold and distinctive.

restaurant.Name: Maison Passerelle
restaurant.Address: 1 Wall St., New York, NY, 10005, USA
restaurant.Description: Nestled within the luxe and glamour of Printemps is this stylish restaurant by Chef Gregory Gourdet, who pulls French, African and Asian influences into a tight menu teeming with personality. Striking tilework, an open kitchen and a green, patterned booth make for a distinct, photo-ready setting. Mature and composed, dishes like smoked beets with nuoc cham and pickled strawberries or asparagus soup with crab and grilled cucumber deliver flavor and finesse in spades. Duck glazed in cane syrup and finished with a tamarind jus is pure fireworks, while jasmine rice with red kidney beans is at once subtle, confident and deeply satisfying. Beautiful cocktails round out the experience.

restaurant.Name: Majka
restaurant.Address: 1704 15th St., Sacramento, CA, 95814, USA
restaurant.Description: Husband-and-wife team Alex Sherry and Chutharat Sae Tong are the driving force behind this charming neighborhood spot, which has risen to the forefront of the Sacramento pizza scene thanks to excellent ingredient-driven pies with naturally leavened crusts. The standout offering is an ever-changing daily creation highlighting seasonal toppings—as in the inspired combination of white asparagus, English peas, and ramps with peppery pecorino Calcagno. Better yet, Friday and Saturday evenings come with specials like lemony Ora king salmon crudo, crisp-skinned roast chicken, and skillfully made agnolotti with a silky filling of fava beans and mint. An exceptional assortment of natural wines (notably, grower Champagnes) further gilds the lily.

restaurant.Name: Mandu
restaurant.Address: 453 K St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Credit to Chef Yesoon Lee and her son Danny for showing this city that Korean cuisine is more than just bibimbap and barbecue. You can trace their steps back to 2006 when they opened the original Mandu in Dupont Circle, now reborn as Anju after an unfortunate fire in 2017. Fans who miss the original can still find pointed, fiery stews and broths at this Mount Vernon location, which sports soaring ceilings and a long bar. From plump, steamed beef and pork mandu to vibrant banchan, this is homey cooking that warms the spirit. And regardless of the weather, no visit would be complete without gamjatang, a bubbling-hot soup featuring tender, bone-in pork ribs and potatoes swimming in a devilishly red broth fired up with gochugaru and perilla seeds.

restaurant.Name: Mango Bay
restaurant.Address: 271 Adelphi St., Brooklyn, NY, 11205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Tucked inside a Fort Greene brownstone, the look hints at the islands (hello, floral wallpaper) blended with city chic (leather booths and exposed brick walls). Casual and welcoming with a new take on Afro-Caribbean cuisine, it's the sort of place you want to go again and again with friends. Snack on starters like a char-grilled octopus tentacle with jerk gremolata over braised collards tossed with burrata, then move on to main dishes like braised oxtail with roasted rainbow carrots. Sides like spicy-sweet mango chow or tender, fried plantains round out the meal in the very best way.

restaurant.Name: Manhatta
restaurant.Address: 28 Liberty St., New York, NY, 10005, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Great view,Interesting wine list,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Set in an iconic skyscraper in the heart of the Financial District, this stylish dining room possesses all the allure and magic of a penthouse. Indeed, some 60 floors up, a talented team bucks the trend with cooking that is as impressive as the views. Reflecting the bounty of the seasons, a flexible, contemporary tasting menu tempts with diverse choices each step of the way. Soigne in look and bold in taste, past highlights include Jonah crab with coins of asparagus, paper-thin slices of apple and sorrel as well as glazed Sweetbreads with parsnips. The beverage program is complete through and through with a deep wine list bursting with gems as well as a smart cocktail program that meets every need.

restaurant.Name: Manhattan Beach Post
restaurant.Address: 1142 Manhattan Ave., Manhattan Beach, CA, 90266, USA
restaurant.Description: Just a stone's throw from Manhattan Beach Pier, this restaurant is big and buzzing. It's almost always packed, especially with plenty of young families, and they're all here for a taste of Chef/co-owner David LeFevre’s globally minded creations with a clear California point of view. Head-on Caledonian blue prawns ajillo atop diced potatoes with saffron mayonnaise. Beeler's Farm pork porterhouse is grilled and accompanied by Asian pear kimchi and a black mustard sauce. Everything revolves around gathering, conversing and sharing, and portions lean small, so plan your ordering as a group to explore a majority of the menu.

restaurant.Name: Mano Libera
restaurant.Address: 7201 S.W. 59th Ave., Miami, FL, 33143, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed everywhere,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Located on a tree-lined, twinkly lit residential street with a neighborhood feel, this restaurant with strong Neapolitan roots offers an array of both modern and classical Italian dishes. Begin with a basket of their fresh breads, including rustic grissini and focaccia, served with creamy house-made ricotta. Move on to the gamberi and calamari fritti, properly enrobed in a double crispy batter, with a spritz of Amalfi lemon and a Dijon mustard dipping sauce. Pastas are the highlight here, particularly the Linguine alla Nerano — a fine base of Gragnano pasta, perfectly al dente, enveloped in light creamy sauce with a mix of fresh and dried zucchini and rounded out with Parmesan foam and plenty of freshly ground pepper. Don't ignore dessert, as their pistachio ice cream is truly special.

restaurant.Name: Manohar’s Delhi Palace
restaurant.Address: 581 Azusa Way, La Puente, CA, 91744, USA
restaurant.Description: Manohar's Delhi Palace is a mainstay thanks to their delicious Punjabi cuisine, and there's a welcoming vibe about this place, where the waitstaff is especially friendly and attentive. Indicative of its north Indian focus, the food here leans on the milder side, so don't expect an onslaught of spices. Order à la carte or go all in on the tandoori dinner but be sure to get an order of the samosas, fried to a perfect crisp with that comforting filling of potatoes and peas. Chicken tikka masala features a generous amount of tender and juicy chicken that's skewered and seared before being added to the vibrant sauce. For dessert, the gulab jamun is a clear winner.

restaurant.Name: Manuela
restaurant.Address: 907 E. 3rd St., Los Angeles, CA, 90013, USA
restaurant.Description: Tucked inside the multi-use Hauser & Wirth Arts Complex with an open-plan kitchen and conceptual art, Manuela has a creative, contemporary look and feel. The cooking is strong, with a Southern leaning, and features a menu with a heavy leaning toward local ingredients (including from their own garden). Choose a cocktail from their classic list, all elevated with house-made bitters and tonics. Warm, flaky biscuits with aged country ham and whipped butter are a must before a main course like their roasted duck breast with nicely rendered, crispy skin served over a bed of smoked soubise and paired with sliced yellow peaches. End the meal with one of their desserts, like their take on s'mores or their Harry's Berries and genmaicha shortbread ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Maple & Ash
restaurant.Address: 8 W. Maple St., Chicago, IL, 60610, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Credit cards not accepted,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Did someone say scene? Oh darling, that’s half the fun at Chicago’s buzziest steakhouse, Maple & Ash. Deep-set leather couches, clubby music and even a photo booth lend the multilevel marvel an irresistible party vibe.This restaurant is set to the soft glow emanating from the semi-open kitchen, where a wood-fired hearth lights up dry-aged steakhouse classics, cut to generous proportions. Seafood lovers will find plenty to mull over too, like a tangle of octopus and squid, prepared in the wood-fueled oven and served with dill yogurt, arugula and roasted potatoes. Then, a fire-roasted seafood tower is brought tableside, featuring lobster tail, scallops, Manila clams and king crab, all bathed in garlic butter, chili oil and served with house-made pasta.

restaurant.Name: Mar'sel
restaurant.Address: Terranea Resort, 100 Terranea Way, Rancho Palos Verdes, CA, 90275, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: At the end of the Palos Verdes Peninsula, find a windy road that meanders through the plush grounds of the Terranea Resort. Beautiful herb gardens are planted along the sidewalk leading you to Mar’sel, a blend of the Spanish and French words for sea and salt. Inside, breathtaking ocean views and a roaring fireplace take the chill off the evening breeze. A sense of opulence pervades everything here, including the superb service. Meals commence with a warm homemade English muffin that may have its own cult following. Every dish looks beautiful and well made, especially those cubes of supremely tender wagyu beef short ribs, with celery prepared four different ways. For dessert, caramel pot de crème is the house specialty, with ganache, cocoa nibs and flecks of sea salt.
