restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: The husband-and-wife duo of AJ and Rachael Donner are behind Pump Social, located just outside Charlotte in downtown Concord. Set inside a vintage gas station, this casual sandwich shop turns out playful options like the Boys of Summer with thick-cut bacon, garden tomatoes, green-leaf lettuce and house aioli on sourdough, or the Service Station Steak with seared sirloin, blue cheese, house onion jam, creamy horseradish, and arugula on a soft baguette. La Famiglia takes toasted ciabatta and layers in capicola, Genoa salami, mortadella, cheese and a spicy pickled pepper spread for a subtle heat. Don't even think about skipping their potato salad. While it's mainly a takeaway spot, there are a few seats indoors and out.

restaurant.Name: Purdy's Farmer & the Fish
restaurant.Address: 100 Titicus Rd., North Salem, NY, 10560, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Great view,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Plenty of restaurants claim a farm-to-table philosophy, but Purdy’s Farmer & the Fish truly lives it. Set beside its own four-acre farm in North Salem, this charming white farmhouse overlooks the fields that supply much of the kitchen’s produce, herbs, berries and honey. The atmosphere is relaxed and welcoming, while the cooking remains simple, seasonal and very rooted in ingredient quality. A hearty clam chowder packed with fresh shellfish, potatoes and bacon highlights the kitchen’s restraint, and a lobster roll filled with generous chunks of sweet claw and tail meat wisely keeps the focus on the seafood itself. Desserts, like a warm berry crunch topped with brown butter ice cream, are equally comforting and homemade. Before leaving, stop by the adjacent farm shop for local produce and provisions.

restaurant.Name: Purveyor
restaurant.Address: 201 Jefferson St. N., Huntsville, AL, 35801, USA
restaurant.Description: A part of the Church Street Family Hospitality Group, this restaurant in downtown Huntsville has been a hit from the beginning. The eclectic menu emphasizes big, bold flavors and, in the process, roams the culinary map, starting with hot cornbread that arrives in a cast-iron skillet and comes paired with honey butter and smoked salt. From there, think wagyu beef tacos with aji amarillo aioli, rack of lamb with pomegranate molasses, and swordfish with braised cabbage. For the regulars who know this restaurant well, special supper club events throughout the year feature different themes and menus.

restaurant.Name: Pylos
restaurant.Address: 128 E. 7th St., New York, NY, 10009, USA
restaurant.Description: Restaurateur Christos Valtzoglou has found a winning formula with this longstanding hideaway, which continues to sparkle as brightly as the Aegean Sea on a summer day. Taking its name from the Greek translation of “made from clay,” this contemporary taverna also features a ceiling canopy of suspended terra-cotta pots, rustic whitewashed walls and lapis-blue insets.Pale-green stemware and stark-white crockery are used to serve wines from the homeland as well as a menu of rustic, home-style food. Keftedakia are light and texturally exquisite meatballs, pan fried in olive oil and proffered as an appetizer. Gigantes are baked in honey-scented tomato-dill sauce; while aginares moussaka is a creamy vegetarian take on the classic, made here with artichokes.

restaurant.Name: Pèppoli
restaurant.Address: 2700 17 Mile Dr., Pebble Beach, CA, 93953, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Great view,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: The ocean and golf course views may be pure California, but a meal here is all about Tuscany. Named for the Pèppoli Vineyard in Italy and owned by the legendary Antinori family of winemakers, this restaurant delivers rustic cooking to a discerning Pebble Beach clientele. Many of their own labels are featured here, as a perfect complement to the cuisine. The dining room, styled to resemble an exclusive Italian estate, spotlights a menu of wood-fired Tuscan food. Expect hearty but skillfully prepared dishes like hand-crafted orecchiette tossed in vibrant green pesto, mixing puréed kale and broccoli with house-made sausages. Save room for excellent desserts like tiramisu and torta di burro, an Italian pound cake with orange compote and blood orange gelato.

restaurant.Name: Pêche
restaurant.Address: 800 Magazine St., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
restaurant.Description: With a decade of history under its belt, Donald Link’s Pêche continues to deliver in this rustic-industrial space on Magazine Street. Seafood sourced directly from the Gulf and prepared with care, often on a grill, continues to be the restaurant’s calling card. Smoked tuna dip, fried shrimp toast or a classic seafood gumbo all make for sensible starters. Larger parties should consider sharing a whole fish complemented by a host of fun sides like brown rice congee or citrus glazed turnips. Comprising a wood-burning grill, a marble-topped raw bar and an always buzzing bar up front, there's no bad seat in this house.

restaurant.Name: Q Sushi
restaurant.Address: 521 W. 7th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Notable sake list,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Authenticity and tradition are paramount in this little sushiya. From the moment you walk in, to the rapid succession of courses that follow, everything in this dining room seems steeped in a sense of calm. Chef Hiroyuki Naruke prepares every item and thoughtfully serves each diner. Edomae-style sushi arrives as an omakase of fish, while other courses may commence with sashimi and nigiri. Case in point—amberjack sashimi with onions and soy, where each morsel is sliced, seasoned and set before your eye. This may be tailed by nigiri such as Hokkaido scallops, kohada, and fatty tuna. The pleasure of dining here extends right to end with the simple, spongy, and fluffy block of tamago.

restaurant.Name: Quarter Acre
restaurant.Address: 2023 Greenville Ave., Ste. 110, Dallas, TX, 75206, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Here the name embodies a pastoral suburban ideal, while the strikingly chic space flaunts an airy forest-meets-island aesthetic, both nodding to Chef/owner Toby Archibald’s New Zealand roots. His cuisine walks a line between flashiness and substance, blending broadly international flavors with classical European technique and polished presentation. Diners may explore the à la carte offerings or opt for a multicourse tasting that traces the kitchen’s evolving perspective, moving from carefully composed seafood and raw preparations to more expressive, fire-kissed dishes. The overall experience reflects a chef eager to weave personal references and seasonal ingredients into a cohesive, thoughtfully paced meal.

restaurant.Name: Quarters BBQ
restaurant.Address: 3465 W. 6th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90020, USA
restaurant.Description: LA's barbecue scene is forever brimming with options, so it can be hard to ferret out the more desirable spots. However, the lines wrapping around this upscale, longstanding gem are a sure sign you’ve chosen well. Make sure to make a reservation, or try to sneak in for lunch or an early dinner to avoid a wait.Its name reflects how the menu is organized—offering meats in quarter-pound portions, thereby allowing diners to sample an ample array of marinated cuts. Come hungry or bring a friend, as solo diners are required to order at least a couple orders of meats. Kick things off with the sizzling pork skin, loaded with rich collagen and excellent seasoning. Four strips of beautifully marbled boneless short rib are then presented on a platter, judiciously seasoned and cooked to pink perfection.

restaurant.Name: R40
restaurant.Address: 47-16 Vernon Blvd., Queens, NY, 11101, USA
restaurant.Description: As the saying goes, the nose knows. These are words to live by at this vibrant Argentinian parilla. With big meats sizzling over a roaring grill, a subtle smoke wafts through the long dining room, built out of sleek wood, exposed brick and dangling greenery. When the nights are cool, the party is further back out on the well-tended patio. Everything here is meant to be shared, starting with the hearty empanadas that come stuffed with everything from filet mignon and raisins to pork shoulder and potatoes. Housemade pastas and chicken milanesa are always tempting, but first timers should dig into favorites like skirt steak with chimichurri. Only serious appetites should order the combination platter featuring steak, ribs, chorizo and sweetbreads.

restaurant.Name: ROOP Chicago
restaurant.Address: 736 W. Randolph St., Chicago, IL, 60661, USA
restaurant.Description: This bright and beautiful setting, located at the edge of the crowded dining strip of West Randolph, is spread over two floors and outfitted with deep blue velvet seats. Libations poured here have their own flavor matrix—study them if you must but rest assured that all are great.Similarly, the menu is dotted with Indian classics enhanced by such cutting-edge flavors as seen in the deep-fried cauliflower koliwada, accompanied by tempered yogurt and a rice mousse with peanut thecha. Follow this up with hearty beef short rib curry stocked with carrots and marrow kofta. Classic palates will relish the wonderfully creamy dal coupled with a plain naan for scooping, while a baked semolina cake with milk ice cream and pistachios will have sweet teeth swooning.

restaurant.Name: RPM Steak
restaurant.Address: 66 W. Kinzie St., Chicago, IL, 60654, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: This bi-level space, centered around a large wraparound marble bar, flaunts a warm, sleek, and moneyed vibe. The polished black- white- and wood-décor speaks to the finer things in life, with a menu of succulent steaks, shellfish, and sides to boot. There's always a full house; for the best people-watching, score one of the semicircular booths. While the aging process and cuts on offer keep spinning, expect to find Japanese prefectures and solid American producers. Highlights include classic steak frites, petite filets, and that mighty cowboy steak—cooked to pink and seasoned with a winning blend of ground and fried thyme, rosemary, garlic, and kosher salt.The wine list meanders around the globe with nods to Napa, Burgundy, and everything in between.

restaurant.Name: RYLA
restaurant.Address: 1220 Hermosa Ave., Hermosa Beach, CA, 90254, USA
restaurant.Description: Ryla, from husband-and-wife chefs Ray Hayashi and Cynthia Hetlinger, remains one of Hermosa Beach’s splashier dining destinations, pairing a lively coastal atmosphere with contemporary cooking rooted in Japanese technique and broader Asian influences. The menu encourages sharing across a wide range of small plates, sushi, noodles and larger mains. Dishes like Japanese yellowtail hiramasa sashimi with mizuna, nori crema and ponzu, or blistered green beans with crispy tofu and black bean sauce showcase the kitchen’s bold flavors and layered textures. Larger plates range from “3 Cup” wild black cod glazed with ginger, soy and sesame to honey-glazed duck breast with cherries and hibiscus gastrique, while the sushi offerings span from pristine nigiri to playful rolls and hand rolls. Desserts remain crowd-pleasing, including yuzu “strawberry shortcake” posset with sour cream whip and aji sugar biscuits.

restaurant.Name: RaaSa
restaurant.Address: 145 E. Main St., Elmsford, NY, 10523, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed everywhere,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: RaaSa's menu is bright, refined and expansive as it meanders through the myriad Indian regions.Kick things off with an order of bhel puri, a palate-pleasing combination of sweet, spicy and tart that is a popular street snack. Coconut rice, garlic naan and raita make delicious accompaniments to the likes of lamb curry in a tomato-based curry that balances sweet and savory with notes of sweet onion, garlic and a subtle gingery kick. If that doesn't leave you wanting more, desserts like kulfi falooda garnished with vermicelli, tapioca seeds and rose syrup, will do the trick. Drinks are equally strong, but there's no going wrong with the creamy mango lassi.

restaurant.Name: Rada
restaurant.Address: 2820 Selwyn Ave., Ste 180, Charlotte, NC, 28209, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: With its sleek, understated design and metropolitan vibe, Rada might just be the hippest spot in town, but fortunately its cool trappings are accompanied by genuinely warm hospitality and crowd-pleasing cuisine. Before turning to food, whet your appetite with one of their impeccable martinis, like the San Sebastian, enlivened with Basque pepper brine. The compact, broadly Mediterranean menu is well-suited to sharing, with frequently changing options that might include small bites like eggplant escabeche or a meatball with zingy harissa, as well as more substantial fare like buttery Dover sole meuniere accented with sherry. The theme of stylish simplicity continues to the desserts, as in a sweet-savory Brillat-Savarin cheese tart with whipped honey.

restaurant.Name: Radicato
restaurant.Address: 137 S. Main St., Breckenridge, CO, 80424, USA
restaurant.Description: Describing itself as “mountain Italian," this bustling, stylish alcove, just off Main Street, offers plenty of charm. The menu blends regional Italian flavors with a wealth of local ingredients in hearty, colorful dishes. A meal might begin with a creamy house-made stracciatella with Calabrian chili-infused honey and fresh herbs, well-matched by crusty focaccia from Threefold bakery just a few doors down. Handmade pasta is a highlight, like indulgent agnolotti with a rich parmigiano artichoke filling, or garganelli with fennel sausage and sweet corn. Mains like an apricot-glazed pork collar with fennel follow the same appealing combination of rusticity and refinement, as do desserts like sweet pea mousse with mint.

restaurant.Name: Radici Italian Chophouse
restaurant.Address: 4376 Bluffton Parkway, Bluffton, SC, 29910, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Meaning “root” in Italian, Radici in Bluffton is on firm ground here in Lowcountry. Several friends run this ambitious restaurant that celebrates Italian flavors with contemporary verve. Appetizers like savoy cabbage stuffed with sausage and smoked cheese set the mood, followed by rich pastas like potato gnocchi with duck ragu. Proteins are serious and meaty, showing a fine degree of care and creativity. Think pork chop with ’nduja or venison loin with goat cheese. Feeling adventurous? The kitchen offers a full tasting menu, as well as counter seats for those who want a front-row view of the action.

restaurant.Name: Raf's
restaurant.Address: 290 Elizabeth St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
restaurant.Description: Raf's has all the charm of an old world bistro, albeit with a modern polish. Chef Mary Attea and Pastry Chef Camari Mick have partnered with Jennifer and Nicole Vitagliano to create a broad European menu with strong Italian and French influences. From escargot and house-made breads (a must-order) to pastas like mafaldine tossed with shredded rabbit and favas in a bright lemon pesto, everything is made with care. There are plenty of shareable dishes (think Sicilian cast iron skillet pizza), and while they aren't reinventing the wheel, they are turning out well-prepared meals with subtlety and style. Dessert is non-negotiable, especially the simple-but-superb white chocolate budino.Didn't plan ahead and get a reservation? Pick your perch at the bar instead.

restaurant.Name: Range Life
restaurant.Address: 2160 Railroad Ave., Livermore, CA, 94550, USA
restaurant.Description: This charmer from husband-and-wife team, Bill and Sarah Niles, may look straight out of a trendy, urban neighborhood, but instead calls Livermore home. The rustic interior with big arched windows and plenty of succulents screams "hipster hotspot." However, few big-city restaurants can offer such an enthusiastic, passionate staff and friendly local crowd.Sip on a Sun Sleeper spritz and tuck in to appealing bites bursting with a bounty of seasonal ingredients, like blistered snap peas with feta and walnut pistachio dukkah; pasta like campanelle with spring lamb belly sugo; or ling cod bathed in dashi butter with bok choi and daikon radish. Finish with malted milk ice cream topped with flaky sea salt, honeycomb candy and grassy olive oil.

restaurant.Name: Raoul's
restaurant.Address: 180 Prince St., New York, NY, 10012, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace
restaurant.Description: In a city that changes faster than you can go from uptown to down, Raoul’s (open since the 1970s) is a stalwart—here long before SoHo was a brand name. Once inside, order a cocktail and admire the art-filled walls; it’s a veritable walk down memory lane for the bohemian set. This is a place where diners return for consistently well-prepared French American cooking. The kitchen has a delicate touch as seen in the golden-brown jumbo lump crab beignets with a drizzle of Fresno chili remoulade. Duck cooked to medium-rare accompanied by seared foie gras and duck confit on a bed of lentils is a delight. Few things beat profiteroles filled with vanilla ice cream and served with a tableside pour of hot fudge.

restaurant.Name: Rasika
restaurant.Address: 633 D St. NW, Washington, DC, 20004, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Valet parking
restaurant.Description: With easy access to the Metro, Rasika is a good-looking, loud, and lively spot that lures all types of diners. Everyone is here for their kitsch-free Indian cuisine and laid-back ambience—both of which are as perfectly suited for a casual night out with friends as they are for a formal dinner with colleagues or festive celebration.Rasika is beloved for their popular dishes ranging from well-spiced kebabs and fresh curries to a vibrant lamb rogan josh with layers of flavor. Word to the wise: the breads, especially the naan, are outstanding, so order two because one is just not enough.

restaurant.Name: Ravello
restaurant.Address: Four Seasons Resort Orlando at Walt Disney World® Resort, 10100 Dream Tree Blvd., Orlando, FL, 32836, USA
restaurant.Description: This more casual concept at the Four Seasons Hotel has Executive Chef Fabrizio Schenardi at the helm. The room is bright and sleek with a laid-back feel. High ceilings, muted hues with an occasional pop of orange and a verdant terrace enhance the inviting vibe. Modern Italian is the menu's focus, which includes everything from small plates and pizzas to house pastas and hearty mains. The chef employs his own family's recipes, so expect such personalized plates as grilled melanzane with zucchini, cucumber and ricotta; or calamari sautéed in tomato sauce, with oregano, olives and capers. Spinach, veal and ricotta ravioli is an homage to his grandmother; and desserts are made with consummate skill.A shot of house-made limoncello hits all the bright spots.

restaurant.Name: Raven Steakhouse
restaurant.Address: 211 W. Broadway Ave., Maryville, TN, 37801, USA
restaurant.Description: Raven Steakhouse isn't your typical steakhouse. While this Maryville restaurant does indeed offer steaks, there's also plenty more to enjoy on this menu. Begin with oysters, fried green tomatoes or a classic wedge with candied bacon before tucking into signature dishes like beef Wellington. It's a perfect medium rare, tucked with a layer of duxelles and wrapped in prosciutto over a celery root puree. While some dishes lean traditional, others display an original twist. Case in point? Crème brûlée corn, a reimagined version of that steakhouse staple, creamed corn. You likely won't be hungry but the layered chocolate cake is a showstopper.

restaurant.Name: Recoveco
restaurant.Address: 6000 S.W. 74th St., Ste. 1, Miami, FL, 33143, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: This South Miami restaurant from Chefs Maria Teresa Gallina and Nicolas Martinez may be diminutive but there's plenty of personality packed into this small space. The menu echoes that tiny-but-mighty sentiment with a concise format that shifts often, particularly with the seasons. Small and large plates are approachable but far from standard, and for a ringside seat, snag a spot at the kitchen counter. The chicken liver mousse displays their signature flair, with house-made speculaas cookies made with peppercorn and cardamom piped with ribbons of velvety mousse and a starfruit jam. Roasted dry-aged chicken is a signature, though, if on offer, the wagyu ribeye in a banana au poivre is a nice choice. For dessert, sapodilla sticky toffee pudding is a sweet closer.

restaurant.Name: Red Hook Tavern
restaurant.Address: 329 Van Brunt St., Brooklyn, NY, 11231, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: From the team behind Hometown BBQ arrives this cozy, quaint, and vintage American tavern. Guests enter to arrive at an expansive bar complete with a brass footrest. Exposed brick, frosted-glass light fixtures, and floral wallpaper are also on display, not to mention closely packed tables with a ledge for votive candles and wine bottles.Start things off with a house spritz or a sip from the eclectic wine or cocktail list. The menu is small and focused; the cooking classic and comforting. But first, start things off with such familiar items as a dry-aged burger enrobed by melted American cheese and served with cottage fries to French onion soup with that trademark bubbly and dark golden cheese top.

restaurant.Name: Red Paper Clip
restaurant.Address: 120 Christopher St., New York, NY, 10014, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Chef Kevin Chen's restaurant is nestled inside a narrow storefront but look for the large red paper clip—it's the only sign you've arrived. Inside, the space is left simple to focus all attention on the inventive food. The team's commitment to local farms is the cornerstone of this kitchen, and seasonal dishes showcase the chef's Taiwanese heritage and Queens upbringing through a fine-dining lens. Parsnip puree with thin ribbons of celtuce is given a tableside pour of chilled cucumber broth infused with chive oil for a refreshing dish. Hainanese chicken sided by a pickled salad is another highlight.

restaurant.Name: Redbird
restaurant.Address: 114 E. 2nd St., Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
restaurant.Description: This airy stunner, which occupies a former church in the heart of Downtown, flaunts an impressive open ceiling allowing diners to stargaze—and that’s not even counting the occasional celebrity sighting. The boisterous atmosphere is beloved by the trendy patrons, who can be seen swapping small plates from perches at the two circular bars and eclectic sofa-stuffed lounge. On the global menu, creative dishes sit side-by-side with more traditional treats like John Dory in a leek fondue strewn with pan-seared gnocchi and mushrooms. Save room for clever desserts like their Meyer lemon tart with blueberry frozen yogurt or opt for another cocktail from the extensive list.

restaurant.Name: Reese Bros Barbecue
restaurant.Address: 906 Hoefgen Ave., San Antonio, TX, 78210, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This spot near the stadium is only open a few days a week, and the line is long, even when you come early. That said, it's worth queuing up for a taste of brothers Elliott and Nick Reese's barbecue. They're turning out Texas-style meat and while brisket is their focus, don't sleep on the queso fundido sausage or smoked turkey breast. It's not all traditional, though, as they substitute house-made flour tortillas and salsa for the typical white bread, and their sides are given an interesting spin. Poblano mac and cheese, or beans with peppers, onions and okra, anyone? Round it all out with a slice of piña colada cobbler for dessert.

restaurant.Name: Reserve
restaurant.Address: 6934 E. 1st Ave., Scottsdale, AZ, 85251, USA
restaurant.Description: Provided cost is no concern, Reserve offers a particular kind of luxury, one built on intimacy, soft piano music, a real dress code and flickering candles. In comparison to its rambunctious sibling Cafe Monarch across the street, this private cottage serves a robust tasting menu that features extensive caviar flights, dry-aged duck, plucky lobster and beautifully marbled wagyu. Restaurants sometimes rush guests, but not in these upholstered environs. Whether you’re indoors or on the spacious patio, a polished service team calibrates the pace with tender care. There’s no shortage of wine either: the extensive cellar is one of the largest in the region, and diners will have options for all budgets. Note: they are open seasonally.

restaurant.Name: Restaurant August
restaurant.Address: 301 Tchoupitoulas St., New Orleans, LA, 70130, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Housed inside a handsome 19th-century warehouse in the Warehouse District, Restaurant August has been a fixture of New Orleans dining for more than two decades. Beneath glittering chandeliers and soaring ceilings, diners settle into one of the city’s grandest dining rooms, where exposed brick, dark wood and white tablecloths create a sense of occasion without feeling stuffy. Executive Chef Corey Thomas continues the restaurant’s long-standing mission of pairing French technique with Louisiana ingredients, drawing on local seafood, regional produce and Creole influences throughout the menu. Dishes balance refinement with a strong sense of place, while warm, professional service keeps the experience firmly rooted in New Orleans hospitality.

restaurant.Name: Restaurant BT
restaurant.Address: 2507 S. MacDill Ave., Tampa, FL, 33629, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Both intimate and serene, this romantic retreat is restaurateur and Chef BT Nguyen's flagship. Its motto "eat local, think global" accurately captures both her genre-defying, eclectic cuisine as well as her dedication to high quality, local ingredients. Although the presentation may lean a bit fussy and old-fashioned (think tomato roses and other such twee garnishes), there's plenty of substance behind the fluff. This is cooking that's assiduously seasoned and bursting with flavor.Many of the dishes draw upon the chef's Vietnamese heritage, seen in the telltale use of bright, aromatic flavors, but items like a sophisticated vichyssoise and Basque-inspired pink prawns are a testament to her classic French training and time spent abroad.

restaurant.Name: Restaurant Constance
restaurant.Address: 2200 Thrift Rd., Charlotte, NC, 28208, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Sam Diminich named this Wesley Heights restaurant for his daughter, though his strong-but-subtle affection for local farmers and producers rings true. While you won't find them name-checking growers, you will find a natural look and feel from the dining room to the plates themselves. This is a kitchen with a global mindset, where you'll find dishes as diverse as pork belly dumplings with shiso, collard greens and chili jam alongside pan-roasted scallops from the Outer Banks topped with prosciutto and set over couscous tossed with vegetables. Like the dumplings, the jalapeño cornbread waffles have been on the menu since the very beginning with good reason. Savor variety for a better price by choosing their three-course offering.

restaurant.Name: Restaurant Martin
restaurant.Address: 526 Galisteo St., Santa Fe, NM, 87501, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Husband-and-wife team Martín and Jennifer Rios are behind Restaurant Martin, where American cuisine is given a global lift. The dining room sports a stylish-yet-comfortable decor with gray chairs and wood tables, as well as distinctive wood art on the walls. The focused menu relies on the seasons and changes often, but a few signature dishes, such as their Caesar salad, are always on offer. Duck breast with oyster mushrooms and curried squash puree or the pan-seared barramundi over sautéed spinach with eggplant puree and butter sauce are two recent highlights. End the meal a slice of molten bittersweet chocolate cake with baked bananas and house-made cinnamon ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Restaurant Olivia
restaurant.Address: 290 S. Downing St., Denver, CO, 80209, USA
restaurant.Description: Partners Ty Leon, Austin Carson and Heather Morrison bring their talents to bear at one of the city's hottest tables, respectively overseeing cooking, beverages and warm hospitality (Morrison's daughter is also the restaurant's namesake). House-made pasta occupies the bulk of the menu, from bronze-die extruded gemelli with Umbrian sausage and pecorino cream, or hand-shaped tortellini filled with braised duck. The offerings range from fairly traditional, like the tagliatelle Bolognese, to inventively globe-trotting, as in ricotta gnocchi paired coconut lobster bisque and black garlic, but assertive flavors are a constant throughout. Inventive cocktails serve well as aperitifs, or to sip while lingering in the relaxed, comfortable atmosphere.

restaurant.Name: Reveler's Hour
restaurant.Address: 1775 Columbia Rd. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: A simple black and glass facade belies the delicious small plates available at this place. Pass a set of double doors to be greeted by a U-shaped bar, arched ceilings and a romantic dining room. Natural wines are a serious focus and pair wonderfully with the shareable plates, and seasonal wines are even accompanied by a poem. Meanwhile, the food is as delightful as the wine selection, offering approachable dishes like pappardelle with spicy roasted pork ragu and fennel breadcrumbs. Be sure to indulge in a pillowy garlic knot, then finish with a Brazilian budino made with coconut caramel and toasted coconut flakes.

restaurant.Name: Rich Table
restaurant.Address: 199 Gough St., San Francisco, CA, 94102, USA
restaurant.Description: This petite Hayes Valley delight is packed nightly and yet nobody seems to care about its stream of crowds. Simply decked with a light-and-dark color scheme along with distressed wood, the room features a laid-back style and rustic-chic farmhouse vibe. It books out far in advance, so arrive early to score a seat at the bar, where trendy types can be found devouring the Californian fare, infused with global ingredients and fine-dining precision.The hip staff is quick on their feet and may present diners with a salmon tostada slathered with tangy avocado purée and dots of salsa verde; or lobster chow mein garnished with charred corn and scallions. Advertised as dessert, cucumber sherbet with diced melon and watermelon granita is a perfect bite by itself.

restaurant.Name: Ris
restaurant.Address: 2275 L St. NW, Washington, DC, 20037, USA
restaurant.Description: Ris Lacoste helms the stove at this terrific neighborhood spot, a draw for diners in the company of family, friends, and business associates alike. The sprawling, light-filled dining room is dressed in earth tones and filled with intimate corners for an air of seductive sophistication. And the menu, with its ramped-up takes on the tried-and-true, toes the line between familiar and surprising. Loaded with butter and olive oil and jazzed up with red pepper flakes, linguine with clams is briny and delicious and chicken Milanese has a perfectly zippy tomato topping. The crab cakes are always on point, and the crown of cauliflower is both interesting and complex, thanks to an ensemble of roasted vegetables slicked with mustard cream and an army of flavors.

restaurant.Name: Risbo
restaurant.Address: 701 Flatbush Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11225, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef/owner Boris Ginet's all-day cafe is a perfect spot to visit before or after a visit to Prospect Park, just a stone's throw away. And while its whitewashed walls lined with artistic photos, industrial-chic cement floors and a glorious garden patio hint at its Brooklyn locale, the anchor here is the open-air, Parisian-style rotisserie, churning out a host of delectably roasted items.This menu highlights everything from bowls and platters to seasonal soups, vegetables and grains. The roasted chicken is a must. Marinated for 72 hours with a host of spices, it's a signature. The Risbo platter is another house special, underscoring the likes of well-seasoned roasted pork served with hummus, a spicy cabbage salad and plantains.

restaurant.Name: River Twice
restaurant.Address: 1601 E. Passyunk Ave., Philadelphia, PA, 19148, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef-Owner Randy Rucker’s corner restaurant is an understated space that’s not without charm, with floor-to-ceiling windows making the most of its appealing location. The small tables come with drawers for your cutlery, but it’s really a seat at the counter you want if you’d like to watch the chefs in action. On offer is a multicourse set menu with a distinct seafood bias and varying degrees of French and Japanese influence. Diners can also order a la carte – and yes that includes the cheeseburger. Past highlights include halibut with shellfish emulsion, Peekytoe crab with fig leaf gazpacho, hiramasa with blistered tomatoes, and Parker House rolls with “tuna XO.”

restaurant.Name: Rolf and Daughters
restaurant.Address: 700 Taylor St., Nashville, TN, 37208, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: Chef/owner Philip Krajeck's Germantown restaurant lures a well-heeled crowd of locals who flock here for great food, done well. His cooking is earnest and approachable, with a seasonal and contemporary mindset. This is a menu where you'll want everything; luckily, it's all designed for sharing. The house-made pasta program turns out impressive work in plates that speak to the season, from fresh spaghetti tinted green from the inclusion of tomato leaves to a corn agnolotti tucked with sweet corn in a beurre blanc. Main dishes like chicken or pork t-bone lean into the refined comfort appeal. A very simple dessert of house-made vanilla bean ice cream with a mashed amaretti cookie topped with a poached peach is a perfect send-off.

restaurant.Name: Ronan
restaurant.Address: 7315 Melrose Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90046, USA
restaurant.Description: Aim for the two-story floral mural to find this Italian favorite with a dive bar-feel and plenty of LA style. Sit in the lovely patio, or head inside to the black marble bar. Other options include booths as well as an attractive communal table crafted from a varnished wood slab. Diners can expect to see pizza dough stretched, blenders whirring and the wood-fired oven crackling, all of which contribute to Ronan's swank allure.Come for their hand-stretched Neopolitan pizza, as well as their shared plates using seasonal produce and ingredients, with appetizers like their spring arancini with pastrami-spiced maitake with English peas and garlic, or their charred broccolini with their house blend of za'atar, fresh mint, and a Meyer lemon aïoli.

restaurant.Name: Rooh
restaurant.Address: 333 Brannan St., San Francisco, CA, 94107, USA
restaurant.Description: Amidst a slew of upscale Indian restaurants descending upon San Francisco, Rooh rises to the top, thanks to an innovative menu that fuses the subcontinent’s myriad flavors with modern restaurant staples (oysters, pork belly, burrata). The bold India-goes-industrial décor is a bit paint-by-numbers, with vivid jewel tones and an oversized mural, but the vibe is engaging and the cocktails quite unique. Rooh's cuisine is approachable, but an extra degree of care and punched-up ingredient quality are reflected in the pricing. Sharing is encouraged with an array of small and larger plates like tandoori black pepper chicken. Wrap up with unique desserts like a cashew praline cake paired with phirni mousse and thaindai ice cream.

restaurant.Name: Rootstalk
restaurant.Address: 207 N. Main St., Breckenridge, CO, 80424, USA
restaurant.Description: With this homey, easygoing landmark, set in a refurbished Victorian, Chef Matt Vawter established himself as the leading light of Breckenridge’s culinary scene. The approachable contemporary menu showcases his thoughtful style, featuring carefully sourced ingredients prepared with confident simplicity. Indulgent starters like chicken liver mousse with cherry mostarda and almond financier, or scallion pancake with peanut sauce and gochujang set the stage. More substantial dishes like ricotta cavatelli with chanterelle mushrooms and sweet corn, or rack of lamb with grilled spigarello and raclette fondue, likewise demonstrate the kitchen’s ingredient-forward sensibility. For a more involved experience, epicures can opt for the multicourse chef’s counter tasting menu.

restaurant.Name: Rory's Place
restaurant.Address: 139 E. Ojai Ave., Ojai, CA, 93023, USA
restaurant.Description: Sisters Rory and Meave McAuliffe run this charming Ojai spot with rustic, feel-good vibes. Wide plank wood floors lend warmth while exposed ducts keep things trendy. There is a little bit of everything here, from a local produce-driven menu and terrific raw bar offerings to a natural wine list and a provisions counter up front. Some dishes seem simple but deliver in spades. A stunning salad of avocado, baby beets and citrus served on a wide, oval plate is a riot of colors. Then, an herb-laced broth bobbing with Aleppo sausage, spring garlic, potatoes and steamed countneck clams offers a refined take on stew. Then, a classic Pavlova is topped with a citrus custard and fresh blood and cara cara oranges, grapefruit and kumquat for a bright finish.

restaurant.Name: Rose Mary
restaurant.Address: 932 W. Fulton Market, Chicago, IL, 60607, USA
restaurant.Description: Conceived by Chef Joe Flamm, this neighborhood delight in the West Fulton Market is worth every bit of hype—from its singular menu to the airy design. Imagine a setting that evokes Croatia's konobas (akin to a rustic trattoria) featuring whitewashed walls, rustic clay, and hanging plants with seating that can easily accommodate some-100 diners.Well-versed servers are on hand to guide patrons through the menu, which draws inspiration from the Adriatic. High points include tortellini djuvec (eggplant and preserved zucchini in a red pepper cream) as well as burek with ground beef and mozzarella. The charcoal hearth is solely responsible for such sumptuous mains as lamb with blitva and potatoes. Save room for sweet treats like rosewater fritule.

restaurant.Name: Rosella
restaurant.Address: 137 Avenue A, New York, NY, 10009, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: This high dining, hyper-sustainable operation is proudly unbound by tradition. The intimate dining room favors warmth and personality over minimalism, with cerulean tones and a handcrafted central counter. The à la carte menu clearly reflects the restaurant's sourcing philosophy, spotlighting local, responsibly harvested seafood treated with restraint and curiosity. Contemporary, gently playful touches appear throughout, from smoked or pickled fish preparations to subtle nods to hand-roll culture and dishes like XO grits that balance comfort with precision. A thoughtfully curated wine list leans domestic, drawing from the North Fork and West Coast.

restaurant.Name: Rossoblu
restaurant.Address: 1124 San Julian St., Los Angeles, CA, 90015, USA
restaurant.Description: This standout from Chef/owner Steve Samson is a favorite among local shoppers and visitors alike. While the area teems with restaurants aplenty, cutting-edge Rossoblu won't disappoint. There’s nothing avant-garde about its food however, and thankfully so. In fact, due to delicious summers spent in Emilia-Romagna, the chef's creations are a veritable ode to the region and promise to make Italian palates proud.Quality ingredients and simple execution come to life in redeye tuna tartare with shallots, capers, and preserved lemon over an avocado puree, served with lavash bread. Pastas, like Olimpia's tagliatelle, with house-made pasta with a pork and beef ragu, are just right. Close on the heels is an irresistible brick of tiramisu crowned with candied cocoa nib cream.

restaurant.Name: Routier
restaurant.Address: 2801 California St., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
restaurant.Description: Routier is a welcoming neighborhood spot serving its own take on French bistro fare, featuring a distinct Californian accent. Chef/owner JP Carmona's casual-meets-sophisticated approach can be seen in dishes like a hot-and-cold composition of crisp, buttery potato pavé topped with sweet Dungeness crab in an herby, lemony mayonnaise, or tender pork cheeks nestled on a bed of creamy lentils, topped with a salad of apples and mustard greens. Quality produce and satisfyingly rustic cooking are hallmarks year-round. Sweets are furnished by celebrated next-door neighbor, B. Patisserie, so it should go without saying, save room for dessert.

restaurant.Name: Roux 30A
restaurant.Address: 114 Logan Ln., Ste. 1A, Santa Rosa Beach, FL, 32459, USA
restaurant.Description: Set along Florida's Emerald Coast in Grayton Beach, Roux 30A is the kind of place that charms at first sight. Slightly quirky in style (think pot racks strung with flatware), it's an inviting space where diners are seated at communal tables or counter stools with a view of the open kitchen. The tasting menu is equally endearing. The kitchen prepares a handful of courses with contemporary American leanings, all based around the seasons. The ever-shifting menu promises creativity in dishes like pasta made with purple sweet potato powder with beech mushrooms in a Parmesan and sage sauce that's topped with a savory, seared U-10 scallop. Local cobia rolled with sweet potato threads over sautéed pumpkin and caramel apple sauce leans into the season in an especially flavorful way.

restaurant.Name: Roxanne
restaurant.Address: 607 S. 2nd St., Philadelphia, PA, 19147, USA
restaurant.Description: Restaurants could learn a thing or two from this eccentric spot. There are no long narratives or spiels once you’re seated, and the menu shows no interest in trends. The sparse room is painted in a quirky purple with Japanese tatami tables on one side. Named after her mother, Chef Alexandra Holt just wants to cook — and cook she can. Not one to shy away from seasoning, she offers a small selection of dishes that prioritize flavor over fuss. Garlic scapes arrive buried under a mountain of ripe melon with sheep’s milk cheese running down one side. Delicate ricotta gnudi are set in a fierce Sungold tomato sauce. Does roast duck really need a wedge of Stilton? How many cherries does it take to cover coffee crème brûlée? Just go with it.

restaurant.Name: Royal
restaurant.Address: 501 Florida Ave. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This airy, quaint, and relaxed all-day spot likes to keep things low-maintenance. The price point too is agreeably lower than its fussier competitors, and the Latin American food is decidedly scrumptious. No wonder, it's a legitimate local favorite.Breakfast is a must, especially if the messy, eggy arepa is on offer. Served wrapped in a white pouch, it resembles a present crafted from seared masa and filled with a fried egg, tomato, cotjia, and avocado. At dinner, hungry fans head to the intimate second-level space—complete with original details—to try their hand at tender pork empanadas laced with aji and the heavenly scent of garlic. The masa “gnocchi” is a rare treat, tossed with braised beef, maitake mushrooms, and loads of herbs.

restaurant.Name: Rue Saint-Marc
restaurant.Address: 2103 San Marco Blvd., Jacksonville, FL, 32207, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Located at the entrance to the historic San Marco Square in Jacksonville, this charming space featuring an open kitchen offers some of the best seasonal French-style cooking from husband and wife Scott and Gabrielle Alters. This dinner-only spot, having both à la carte and tasting menus, guarantees to satisfy with beautifully presented and skillfully cooked dishes. Start with the unagi tartlets, filled with a chilled koji "potato salad," topped with sweet glazed freshwater eel. Next, try the warm, savory gougères filled with black walnut béchamel. Outstanding main courses include Mediterranean sea bass, pan seared with fried mussels, matsutake mushrooms, grapes, gnocchi and a verjus vinaigrette. Complete your meal with the pleasing spiced apple crisp with vanilla ice cream and caramel drizzle.

restaurant.Name: Rumi's Kitchen
restaurant.Address: 640 L St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: This large, square dining room is ultra-grand and yet ultra-charming, with a melange of earthy, vivid hues, an inviting bar, and display kitchen fitted out with a tandoor oven. Find a seat at one of the high-backed banquettes or wood tables to start sampling from the classic Persian menu. Green tahini hummus sprinkled with urfa chili is a rich and creamy delight before a savory lamb shank resting in a tomato-based stew. Desserts enhance the experience, with the staple baklava or a more creative ice cream sandwich with rosewater and pistachios. Thirsty travelers will appreciate the Glimpse of Paradise cocktail, starring vodka, grapefruit and cardamom syrup.

restaurant.Name: Runner & Stone
restaurant.Address: 285 Third Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11215, USA
restaurant.Description: This ambitious operation's name refers to the two stones used to grind grain; the location is just blocks from where the city’s first tidewater grist mill once stood; and a Per Se alum heads the bakery. Inside, the theme continues with walls constructed of concrete blocks shaped like flour sacks.The menu is split between salads and sandwiches, with many between-the-bread offerings. Sandwiches showcase the house-baked breads, like whole wheat pain au lait grilled with cheddar and pickled peppers; or falafel-inspired broccoli fritters in a warm pita with harissa and walnut-yogurt sauce. The tuna melt, made with tuna confit, tomato olive relish, mayo, arugula, and fontina cheese on a semolina roll, is an elegant update. Don't miss dessert, and definitely bring extra home.

restaurant.Name: Rustic Canyon
restaurant.Address: 1119 Wilshire Blvd., Santa Monica, CA, 90401, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: A sense of community and warm hospitality pervades this beloved Santa Monica institution where the lighting is just right and where the bar and booths exude intimacy. Open since 2006, the restaurant has gone through many chapters and evolutions, but one guiding, foundational principle is a commitment to market-driven cooking. The menu today proudly acknowledges the farmers and producers behind every asparagus, chicory, persimmon and fish. The cooking is far from fussy. Think hearty pork terrines with pickled cauliflower, poached trout with sauerkraut, bay scallops with tomatoes and saffron, and roast chicken with walnut mole. Cocktails also follow the seasons and should be explored with no hesitation.

restaurant.Name: Rye Bunny
restaurant.Address: 1827 Adams Mill Rd. NW, Washington, DC, 20009, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: Jon Sybert and Jill Tyler are no strangers to the D.C. dining scene. The husband-and-wife team ran the highly regarded Tail Up Goat for a decade in this very same spot, but Rye Bunny is far from a reboot of the same concept. Everything, from the look and feel (think colorful farmhouse) to the service, is completely new. It's laidback, with no reservations and a hybrid style that has guests ordering at the counter before enjoying traditional service at their table. Meanwhile, the food is best described as contemporary, creative riffs on comfort food, as in fried chicken with Aleppo pepper and sumac honey served over black garlic toum with red pepper jam. Anchovy toast on milk bread with blood orange compote and fennel pollen is impossibly delicious.

restaurant.Name: Ryokou
restaurant.Address: 565 Northside Dr. SW, #A101, Atlanta, GA, 30310, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Car park,Counter dining,Pets not allowed
restaurant.Description: This Adair Park restaurant is a bit of a discovery. Tucked in an industrial building and behind a hidden door, it's the definition of minimalism in look and feel, with counter seating for just under a dozen diners. Ryokou, or journey, isn't just the name, it's the ethos, with Chef Paul Gutting taking guests on a culinary journey across Japan. He spotlights different regions and specialties, using high-quality products as the backbone for this highly original tasting. Somen, with a bold broth brimming with noodles, shrimp and scallop, is served with ice for a fresh take on cold noodles, while the salt-grilled black throat sea perch with tokyo negi. The soup course, or shiru, is a satisfying bowl of miso soup with langoustine.

restaurant.Name: République
restaurant.Address: 624 S. La Brea Ave., Hollywood, CA, 90036, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: In some ways, this all-day hit feels like a city of its own. With soaring ceilings, beautiful brickwork and sunny skylights, the cavernous space is a beehive of activity. In the morning, freshly baked pastries and breads draw long lines. Come evening, the open kitchen is in full swing, working quickly to serve wave after wave of diners. The tightly curated menu explores the cuisine of Southern Europe through exceptional ingredients, many of them local. Trays loaded with warm potato and leek beignets or toast points stacked with eggs and uni land on almost every table. Baguettes with superb French butter inevitably follow. Dungeness crab risotto, braised wagyu beef cheek and duck with baby beets round out an experience that never fails to satisfy.

restaurant.Name: Rêve
restaurant.Address: 1821 2nd Ave. N., Ste. 176, Birmingham, AL, 35293, USA
restaurant.Description: In a discreet corner of Birmingham’s Pizitz Food Hall, Chef Jacob Stull runs this modern dining room. Some walk-ins snag a seat at the bar. Others settle into the booths. Either way, dinner is an involved affair and revolves around a French-inspired tasting menu. A series of snacks and bites, each one carefully crafted, sets the tone for the evening. Warm Japanese milk bread is a frequent highlight, as luxuries like wagyu, foie gras, and turbot undergo elaborate, ambitious preparations. An upbeat playlist, along with relaxed, attentive service, makes for a welcome experience.

restaurant.Name: Rêve Bistro
restaurant.Address: 960 Moraga Rd., Ste. F, Lafayette, CA, 94549, USA
restaurant.Description: Enter through a metal gate to land upon this charming patio, virtually beaming with lights and greenery. The dining room is quaint, with a sleek bar, exposed brick and large tile floors. The décor is simple and clean, but a set of sparkling chandeliers add elegance. The staff are a smooth, efficient bunch; and the bistro menu from Chef/owner Paul Magu-Lecugy spans the classics. Think starters like buttery, garlicky escargots or roasted veal sweetbreads with asparagus and morel mushrooms. The ile flottante with crème anglaise, caramel and pistachios is a fitting end. A predominantly French wine list goes well beyond just Bordeaux and Burgundy— and even throws in a bit of California for good measure.

restaurant.Name: S.K.Y.
restaurant.Address: 2300 N. Lincoln Park W., Chicago, IL, 60614, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Counter dining,Pets not allowed,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: With a new location on the first floor of the Belden-Stratford apartment complex and a revamped menu, S.K.Y. doesn't let grass grow under their feet. Tall ceilings and dim lighting set the tone for an intimate experience in the dining room. Meanwhile, the kitchen promises a number of new dishes in addition to a roster of their classics. This is globally minded cuisine, where roasted lamb meatballs with tikka masala butter tempt alongside bibimbap with charred vegetables and mushroom bulgogi. And, while some things change, others remain the same. Banana budino, always a good choice, remains on the menu, though new creations, like strawberries and champagne with pistachio cake, strawberry ice cream and crisp crémant, make for a memorable finale.

restaurant.Name: SORA Craft Kitchen
restaurant.Address: 1109 E. 12th St., Los Angeles, CA, 90021, USA
restaurant.Description: SORA Craft Kitchen is a labor of love, a one-man show run by Chef Okay Inak. This Turkish-born chef has a fine dining pedigree but runs this DTLA spot entirely on his own, turning out hearty, honest Anatolian/Turkish dishes with modern techniques. With just over a dozen seats, the space is bright and inviting thanks to wood floors and ceilings, white wood tables set with stools and plenty of greenery. It's a casual spot, where guests order at a kiosk, choosing from appetizers like Spanish octopus with a Turkish white bean salad and entrees like sumac-cured tenderloin shish kebab over a smoked pepper sauce and house-made yogurt. Cheese halva with crushed pistachio and house-made ice cream makes for a great end to an enjoyable meal.

restaurant.Name: SPQR
restaurant.Address: 1911 Fillmore St., San Francisco, CA, 94115, USA
restaurant.Description: Kitschy and boisterous with modern cooking, this dining room is always packed. The space is slender while a soaring ceiling, skylights and open kitchen brighten the mood.Chef Matthew Accarrino's mingling of Italian and Californian elements makes for satisfying cooking, and the best of the season's produce is highlighted in the five-course prix-fixe menu. The meal might begin with a crespelle with pork belly, fennel and persimmon, or a chicken liver terrina with rhubarb and wood sorrel. Of course, choosing between house-made pastas like squid ink perciatelli with octopus cream and chili pequin or spinach pappardelle with mushroom and fried egg might seem challenging, but it's difficult to go wrong.

restaurant.Name: Sabio on Main
restaurant.Address: 501 Main St., Pleasanton, CA, 94566, USA
restaurant.Description: This far-from-sterile space might even be described as dramatic, given its arched wood panels, dark charcoal tiles, soft pendant lights and backlit wall of wine. A ladder running across completes the effect. Locally sourced produce, meat from regenerative ranches and responsibly caught seafood are the foundation of the impressive, hyperseasonal cuisine produced here. Menus dance to the seasons, unveiling such passionate and ingenious dishes as a spring garlic velouté with Livermore olive oil, and half a head of za'atar-roasted Romanesco with green tahini and pine nuts. The blueberry cheesecake sundae with cream cheese mousse and cinnamon-graham cracker crumble makes for a delightful ending.

restaurant.Name: Sachet
restaurant.Address: 4270 Oak Lawn Ave., Dallas, TX, 75219, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Counter dining,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: There’s something about this corner restaurant that makes it look so inviting—and sure enough, the moment you step inside you feel enveloped in the warm embrace of the bright, southern European sun. That’s not just down to the light, open feel of the large room, but also because of the charming service team. This may be the baby sister of Gemma restaurant, but the menu here looks to the wider Mediterranean for its influences, stretching from Morocco to Syria and round to Italy, France, and Spain. Dishes like octopus with freekeh and lamb with gigante beans are as colorful and appealing as they are satisfying and nourishing. If you can’t get a table—and the booths are much demanded—you can try your luck at the large counter bar.

restaurant.Name: Saffron
restaurant.Address: 1143 San Carlos Ave., San Carlos, CA, 94070, USA
restaurant.Description: From the very first moment you walk into this unique Indian gem, you will feel right at home. Ever so transporting, the space is a veritable comfort zone—stylish, breezy, and inviting. Over in the kitchen, the cooks are focused on vibrant and sumptuous renderings from the nation's myriad of regions. While the best dishes tend to be more traditional at heart, they boast a host of intriguing garnishings. Kale pakoras are deep-fried fritters served with onions in a light chickpea batter and a spectrum of chutneys; while lamb curry reveals a leg of lamb slow braised with over 21 Indian spices. Rasmalai, or cheese dumplings in a milk reduction, garnished with nuts and served cold, makes for a refreshing finale.

restaurant.Name: Saffron NOLA
restaurant.Address: 4128 Magazine St., New Orleans, LA, 70115, USA
restaurant.Description: Set among the galleries and boutiques of Magazine Street, Saffron NOLA has carved out a distinctive niche in the city by marrying Indian flavors with Louisiana ingredients. The warm, contemporary dining room reflects the restaurant’s family-run spirit, with Chef Arvinder Vilkhu, his wife Pardeep, and their children shaping a deeply personal vision of modern Indian cuisine. Signature dishes like the curried seafood gumbo seamlessly blend Gulf seafood, local traditions and Indian spices, while fragrant goat masala and freshly baked garlic naan showcase the kitchen’s command of classic flavors. The result is a restaurant that feels both unmistakably New Orleans and proudly Indian.

restaurant.Name: Saffy's
restaurant.Address: 4845 Fountain Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90029, USA
restaurant.Description: Crackling flames, heat radiating from the coals, the constant kneading and stretching of dough— the visceral nature of Ori Menashe and Genevieve Gergis’s latest restaurant is impossible to ignore. Clearly, as snagging a reservation at this hot spot isn't an easy feat.Lamb and pork kebabs cooked on long metal skewers are the main event, but grilled lobster marinated in green harissa is a luxurious feast that would dazzle in fine dining temples. Turmeric mussels are a delight, as is the golden-brown falafel with creamy tahini. Bread is a constant source of pleasure, from the delicate challah to the soft laffa, but dessert is far from an afterthought. Avocado honey butter soft serve ice cream with a tableside pour of sherry is a real treat.

restaurant.Name: Safta
restaurant.Address: The Source Hotel, 3330 Brighton Blvd., Ste. 201, Denver, CO, 80216, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Safta may mean "grandmother" in Hebrew, but there's nothing old school about this restaurant, Chef Alon Shaya's first outside Louisiana. Instead, this hot spot is located in the trendy Source Hotel. At first glance, it looks like you’re walking toward a coffee counter (and you are), but it wraps around to the restaurant and the kitchen. It's all airy and upbeat, just like the Israeli menu that lists many favorites but feels original and interesting. There must be hummus, of course, but here it's given a fresh take with roasted chanterelle mushrooms and chermoula butter served with freshly baked pita. Next up is a selection of salatim, or pickles and spreads, followed by a panoply of dishes ranging from harissa chicken, duck matzo ball soup, and short rib-stuffed cabbage to pomegranate lamb shank.

restaurant.Name: Sailor
restaurant.Address: 228 Dekalb Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11205, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: The determination required to score a table can almost feel excessive. Almost. With lines perpetually wrapped around this corner of Fort Greene, Chef April Bloomfield returns with familiar dishes that hew to the seasons and boast maximum flavor with minimum fuss. Who knew eggs with celery salt and mayonnaise could be this good? The Caesar salad, Swiss chard, and roast chicken all hit their marks. Some of these are only available during dinner when reservations are in limited supply. Lunch has its benefits too: The spring onion and goat gouda quiche is peerless, plus there’s a superb burger and a towering stack of French fries. All the while, sun beams through the skylight of a bistro that seems well on its way to becoming a neighborhood classic.

restaurant.Name: Saint Claire
restaurant.Address: 1300 Richland Rd., New Orleans, LA, 70114, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Although it’s only 20 minutes from the French Quarter, this charming experience in Algiers feels like a faraway escape. Set on pastoral grounds in a historic home, the restaurant oozes with comfort thanks to a living room aesthetic marked by well-worn furniture, vintage cutlery and flickering candles. A lesser restaurant might coast on its looks, but this talented team goes above and beyond with an endlessly tempting, French-inflected menu that recalls the very best kind of bistro cookery. Caramelized shallot tarte tatin is a knockout starter and nearly a meal all to itself. Gnocchi with jumbo lump crab? Smoked beets with trout roe? Everything sings down to the sweet finale of golden-fried hand pies for dessert.

restaurant.Name: Saint Julivert Fisherie
restaurant.Address: 264 Clinton St., Brooklyn, NY, 11201, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: This long-time neighborhood favorite comes courtesy of Chefs Alex Raij and Eder Montero, who also run next-door La Vara. The narrow space does not at all match the kitchen’s outsized talents and imaginative plates, which put seafood front and center. Consider starting with a plate of tempura-battered delicata squash with black garlic-infused labneh or golden-brown fried hamachi and shrimp boudin with Thai chili mayo before diving into the likes of Ibérico pork steak. Tamarind-glazed and grilled, it's served over a bed of coconut creamed spinach and okra and sided by a bowl of roasted potatoes with sauce choron.A generous selection of regional wines highlights small producers to match the cooking.

restaurant.Name: Salita Pizza
restaurant.Address: 615 S. 16th St., Ste. 130, Wilmington, NC, 28401, USA
restaurant.Description: Tucked into Wilmington’s Cargo District, Salita is a walk-up pizzeria with communal outdoor seating and an appropriately casual spirit. Chef Jim Diecchio takes a thoughtful approach to sourcing, using local produce and freshly milled North Carolina grains for his sourdough pizzas. The menu shifts with the seasons, and combinations can be unexpected but smart: roasted lemon joins lamb sausage, apricot and pistachio over spicy cream, and ripe peaches and cucumbers make for a bright summer salad with goat cheese, basil and pickled jalapeno. Don’t overlook the soft serve, where flavors such as olive oil-basil and fresh cantaloupe continue the kitchen’s playful, seasonal approach.

restaurant.Name: Salt
restaurant.Address: The Ritz-Carlton, Amelia Island, 4750 Amelia Island Pkwy., Amelia Island, FL, 32034, USA
restaurant.Description: Nestled inside the plush Ritz-Carlton on Amelia Island and blessed with a wall of windows fronting the Atlantic Ocean, Salt could coast on looks alone. It doesn't. A measured tasting menu is the best way to see how this contemporary kitchen threads European and Asian influences to deliver a broadly appealing menu that includes tuna tartare in a dashi emulsion, butter-baked halibut with a tableside pour of saffron tomato consommé, and wagyu ribeye cap finished with truffle hollandaise. An ace service team keeps close watch, ever sincere in their interactions and keen to remember the many diners who frequent this destination regularly. An early dinner time guarantees prime sunset views.

restaurant.Name: Salt Smokehouse
restaurant.Address: 1300 Meridian St., D-104, Huntsville, AL, 35801, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: In the sparkling Lincoln Mill district, this family-owned barbecue spot is out to satisfy. High ceilings, white walls and ample seating make for a Spartan vibe. The menu, by contrast, is full of personality, as it pulls global inspiration from all over, starting with a roster of hearty appetizers like brisket fritters with chihuahua cheese or fried soft-shell crab bao sliders. Sandwiches and burgers also tempt, but for the purists among us, stick with the fundamentals. A fatty slice of prime-grade smoked brisket cooked overnight cuts like custard and doesn’t need a lick of sauce. Soft, tender pulled pork is another winning order, along with creative sides like ginger serrano coleslaw or fried Brussel sprouts with hot honey and yuzu.

restaurant.Name: San Laurel
restaurant.Address: Conrad Los Angeles, 100 S. Grand Ave., Los Angeles, CA, 90012, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Great view,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: San Laurel is at the top of its game—quite literally, since this tenth-floor dazzler affords unobstructed views of Walt Disney Concert Hall from its polished perch. With soothing earth tones, lush greenery, a bustling bar and a breezy vibe courtesy of a fully opened facade, it looks and feels like an urban oasis. Expect modern Californian dishes with Spanish leanings from a talented team put together by visionary chef, José Andrés. A tartare turns tradition on its head when "beefsteak" is actually tomatoes in a perfect disc, topped with a "yolk" made of gelatinous tomato water. A rack of lamb, cut into four, is plated around a circle of red mole sauce and a half baby eggplant, roasted and topped with pea tendrils and puffed rice. Desserts really shine, as in an ethereal pistachio cake with fragrant lime zest and sweet strawberries matched by a tart mascarpone sorbet.

restaurant.Name: San Lorenzo
restaurant.Address: 1316 9th St. NW, Washington, DC, 20001, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Massimo Fabbri, who long ruled the kitchen at DC’s beloved Tosca, has traded in those white tablecloths for this neighborhood charmer, named after his son (Lorenzo is the “patron saint of cooks”). Photos of the chef's Tuscan hometown adorn the exposed brick walls and painted tiles line the floor, hinting at the delicious regional specialties that await.A dinner in this chef's hands might begin with grilled calamari (or fried, if that's your preference) with shaved broccoli, yellow bell pepper puree and white wine sauce. Pasta is a must: try the ravioli stuffed with ricotta, burrata and San Marzano tomatoes, sauteed with basil pesto and tomato.

restaurant.Name: Santi
restaurant.Address: 11 E. 53rd St., New York, NY, 10022, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Santi is Chef Michael White's paen to the Mediterranean in the heart of Midtown. There may be multiple spaces within, but this stunning spot feels intimate, making it a perfect date-night reservation. The menu draws on White's experience in the South of France and the Amalfi Coast with crudités di mare like prawns with pistachio, antipasti like butternut squash soup, primi including gnocchi and risotto, and secondi ranging from grilled steak to sea bass. Orecchiette tossed with blue crab and sea urchin is a highlight, as is the pan-roasted veal chop plated with pancetta-wrapped, charred radicchio. In a final bow, Delizie al Limone pays tribute to the Italian coast with white chocolate-covered sponge cake filled with limoncello cream and basil whipped cream.

restaurant.Name: Santo
restaurant.Address: 1265 Alpine Ave., Boulder, CO, 80304, USA
restaurant.Description: Chef Hosea Rosenberg draws inspiration from his hometown of Taos, in northern New Mexico, to deliver a menu of satisfying, rustic cooking. Guests can stop in at all times of day to satisfy a craving for southwestern fare. In the morning, grab-and-go breakfast burritos are the mainstay, while at lunch, casual counter service encompasses a broader array of options from pozole to tortas. Finally, at dinner, full table service accommodates a livelier crowd where margaritas flow with the full menu in play, featuring specialties like roasted chicken mole with red pepper polenta.

restaurant.Name: Saru Sushi Bar
restaurant.Address: 3856 24th St., San Francisco, CA, 94114, USA
restaurant.Description: Hilly Noe Valley is the perfect setting for this jewel of a sushi restaurant, so make your way inside to discover a bustling (read: energetic) vibe. The menu is thoroughly Japanese with a few Californian touches—think grilled shishito peppers tossed with crunchy daikon in a ponzu dressing.Begin with the signature tempura-fried seaweed cracker topped with spicy tuna and avocado. Then, perfectly sized tasting spoons of seared ankimo with scallions, as well as halibut tartare with yuzu make for delightful quick bites. Though rolls are available, regulars opt for the nigiri, which might include kampachi, baby snapper and snow crab. Several omakase (including an all-salmon variation) are also on offer. Since Saru doesn't take reservations, arrive early to avoid a line.

restaurant.Name: Sato Omakase
restaurant.Address: 1122 Post St., San Francisco, CA, 94109, USA
restaurant.Description: This stylish operation runs as smooth as silk, but more importantly, it serves up an indulgent tasting that highlights excellent ingredients with skill and flair. The menu draws upon both tradition and invention, as in a dish of butter-poached lobster with dashi. Though the cooking does flaunt luxury ingredients with a certain abandon, it's the more understated elements that most impress, like the soy-marinated tuna sashimi with a silky, meaty texture, dotted with freshly grated wasabi; or a nigiri of buttery hamachi belly, lifted with yuzu zest.Next door, livelier sibling Sushi Sato serves more affordable sushi and sashimi, assorted small plates, as well as a beverage program that highlights fine Japanese whisky.

restaurant.Name: Sawa
restaurant.Address: 75 5th Ave., Brooklyn, NY, 11217, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Pets not allowed,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: This lively spot lures a crowd: by the time they unlock the doors, the line is already long. Everyone is here for the convivial ambience and the standout Middle Eastern cuisine. This is a menu thick with options, with house-made pita arriving piping hot to scoop up labneh and hummus with wagyu beef cheeks plus baba ghannouj before a round of mezze like tabbouleh, fried meat pies and kibbeh nayeh. Don't miss the rakkakat, or akkawi and halloumi cheese wrapped in filo and fried to a golden crisp. Grilled Australian lamb chop with garlic labneh and a generous coating of urfa bibir is a smoky, savory main dish. Finish with the tamriyeh, phyllo pastries filled with sweet semolina pudding.

restaurant.Name: Se7en Bites
restaurant.Address: 617 N. Primrose Dr., Orlando, FL, 32803, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Brunch,Car park,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace
restaurant.Description: A large sign just off the street signals the entrance to this bakery-café. Its bright green structure is hard to miss; inside, diners will discover a large space with wood paneling and a corrugated metal ceiling. Another wall decked with Bundt cake pans makes for a cool design feature. This is an undoubtedly inviting spot, with a friendly staff that churns out hearty American-Southern dishes in big portions and small prices.The chicken biscuit is a tender-fried revelation spread with cream cheese and pepper jelly. Next up, chicken pot pie available in hearty portions. Marked by a golden crust covering chunks of meat, peas and carrots, this is a forever favorite—and fittingly so. The large, mouthwatering display of sweet treats reminds you to save room.

restaurant.Name: Secchu Yokota
restaurant.Address: 199 E. 3rd St., New York, NY, 10009, USA
restaurant.Description: This spot flies under the radar somewhat, and that’s just the way their loyal fan base likes it. Those who understand the fine art of tempura know how pristine the quality is here, where diners are treated to a mouthwatering omakase featuring succulent red shrimp, Japanese eggplant, and lightly battered anago. You probably won’t need it, but lemon, wasabi salt and seaweed salt are provided as enhancements. The man to thank for these treats is Chef Yokota, who takes his craft (and business) seriously, putting his clients first. Dining here is an intimate and deeply personal experience that highlights ingredients sourced mostly from Japan. As a bonus, his tempura is typically bookended by unique dishes that display his French culinary training.

restaurant.Name: See No Evil Pizza
restaurant.Address: 210 W. 50th St., New York, NY, 10019, USA
restaurant.Description: There are just some places that are so New York they couldn't be found anywhere else. See No Evil Pizza is just that. It could be the location in a subway station, or it could be because they're doling out an iconic New York staple—pizza—but don't be fooled by the environs, as a treasure awaits inside. It's casual with a hint of punk, with 80s classics overhead and black-and-white checkered floors. Sit back and let the commuters fly by as you snack on small plates like toast with sardines or a seasonal bowl of beautiful beans in a walnut sauce before moving on to the pizza. There are always specials, but the Hell pie, a thin crust variety topped with spicy meat, is always good. Finish with vanilla soft serve with olive oil and sea salt.

restaurant.Name: Seis Vecinos
restaurant.Address: 640 Prospect Ave., Bronx, NY, 10455, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace),Terrace,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Sitting on a prominent corner at the base of an ornate yet classic NYC building is this now-well ensconced restaurant. The interior is sunny and welcoming with a gracious staff to boot; the menu is melting pot Central America featuring papusas from El Salvador, baleadas from Honduras, and fajitas from Mexico. Guacamole made tableside in a molcajete is a great way to begin the meal before a main dish like enchiladas made with tender corn tortillas stuffed with shredded, seasoned chicken, topped with a smoky red sauce, crema, and queso.Breakfast delivers hearty offerings such as picaditas verdes with carne al gusto or huevos revueltos con verduras y casamiento.

restaurant.Name: Selam
restaurant.Address: 5494 Central Florida Pkwy., Orlando, FL, 32821, USA
restaurant.Description: This graciously run restaurant offers a rare taste of the Horn of Africa, specifically the cuisine of Ethiopia and Eritrea. Set at the corner of a shopping center, it boasts a commanding presence with bold signage and a nicely arranged alfresco section. Inside the incense-scented space, there are tiled floors, windows draped with woven fabrics and turquoise seating for a pop of color.Boldly flavored but subtly spiced stews arrive with spongy injera for sopping. The menu is meat-focused but there are plenty of plant-based items on offer. The combination platter is a great way to sample a bevy of bites, including the beef key wot seasoned with berbere, beef alecha wot rich with turmeric; gomen, or stewed collard greens; and house-made cottage cheese.

restaurant.Name: Selanne Steak Tavern
restaurant.Address: 1464 S. Coast Hwy., Laguna Beach, CA, 92651, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Air conditioning,Interesting wine list,Terrace,Valet parking,Wheelchair access
restaurant.Description: Once a home, this historic setting on Pacific Coast Highway now houses a winning steakhouse. Inside, a variety of settings welcome guests, ranging from the upstairs Loft, the bistro-style Wine Library, the handsome Tavern, or outside on the Veranda or Sunset Terrace. The buzzy bar is also a favorite perch for a crowd that's both relaxed and regulars. Steak is revered in this place and it lives up to its promise with tender, well marbled meat, but the kitchen ratchets it up with expert cooking (and dousing it in butter never hurts). Thick seared mushrooms in a Madeira reduction are a nice touch, and creamy, buttery mashed potatoes are a must, but don't monkey around when it comes to dessert—Selanne's monkey bread can't be missed.

restaurant.Name: Select Oyster Bar
restaurant.Address: 50 Gloucester St., Boston, MA, 02115, USA
restaurant.FacilitiesAndServices: Pets allowed only in outdoor dining areas (patio/terrace)
restaurant.Description: Long a local favorite, Chef Michael Sherpa's oyster bar is located on the ground floor of a Back Bay rowhouse, and the intimate setting, dominated by an L-shaped pewter bar, radiates good vibes. High quality seafood is the order of the day, be it the daily crudo, crab salad or honey-butter dressed Maine uni toast. The icy plateaux is a splurge-worthy indulgence, best shared with friends (or not). In true oyster bar fashion, the menu is supplemented by a daily offering of oysters and other shellfish.
